section and the welcome page read `UIState.Connections`: filled for live, a ring for `cold`, the
blink for a background reconnect), the dock per cluster (item 9: today every cluster's dock tab is
listed), Disconnect of a cluster that is not shown in its menus, and Diagnostics' per-cluster sums
in the tab. Stage 3, item 4's setting and item 8's restore, below. **Not verified:** a real credential
plugin's renewal on a background cluster, several clusters on a real computer's sleep, memory with
several clusters connected for hours.

**Stage 2, the window, built 2026-10-16** (the lead's run in a worktree of its own, beside stage 3's;
[architecture §4.3](architecture.md#several-clusters-connected-d-69)):

- **Switching without reconnecting** (item 1), checked at every entry point: a hotbar tile and its
  F-key (`hotbar.openCluster`), a row of the navigator's section, its › and ↵
  (`ui.setNavigatorScope`), a row of the welcome page (`cluster.connect`), a tab of another cluster
  (`ui.tab.select`) and the row and tile menus show a connected cluster at once: the engine only
  shows it, and the window asks for no login program's approval first, not even for one that
  changed since its connect (`switchable`, [`clustermarks.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clustermarks.go)).
  A cluster that is not connected connects and is shown; the others stay connected. A cluster shown
  while it reconnects loads its kinds for the navigator too (`connectionChanged`: every live state,
  not only Connected).
- **The marks of item 5 on every dot of a cluster**: its hotbar tile, its row in the navigator's
  section and the tree's root, its row on the welcome page (since stage 2 every connected cluster's
  row has a dot, not only the shown one's) and the status bar for the shown one (the top bar's went
  2026-10-21, [D-54](#d-54-the-layout-toggles-and-the-update-button)).
  `markOf` derives a cluster's mark from `UIState` alone: the shown cluster's `Connection`, another
  connected cluster's entry of `Connections`, else a failed last connect
  (`ContextInfo.ConnectProblem`, read again after every connect that ends). Filled green: the shown
  cluster connected, or a connected one whose views are warm ("Connected, in the background: its
  views kept warm, showing it is instant"); filled green blinking: (re)connecting; a green ring:
  `cold` ("…its views released, showing it lists them again"); a grey ring: `loginLapsed` ("Connected,
  its login lapsed: Cogpit did not renew it while the cluster was not shown; showing it or Log in
  again renews it"); filled red: a failed connect, a failed renewal (Login expired); filled grey: not
  connected. A ring is the dot's own 8-point circle drawn as a 1.5-point line
  ([`conndot.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/conndot.go), `ringStroke`), so no layout moves; a
  blinking dot is drawn filled. The tooltip names the state; no banner, no toast. A click on any
  dot still opens its cluster's connection log (D-66). The shown cluster's hotbar tile alone is
  raised; another connected cluster's tile has its dot.
- **Each cluster blinks for itself** (item 7): the blinker keeps a blink per cluster
  (`blinker.blinks`), follows every cluster's state (`observeAll`, the shown one's and each entry of
  `Connections`), and a cluster shown or left no longer ends another's blink; at least three
  intervals each, Reduce motion's steady half-alpha dot as before. One ticker serves every blink.
- **The dock per cluster** (item 9), engine state
  ([`dockscope.go`](../../internal/engine/dockscope.go)): the dock shows the shown cluster's tabs and
  those of no cluster (the Audit Log, the Diagnostics; `UIState.DockInScope`); `ActiveDock` and
  `DockOpen` are the shown cluster's, and the engine keeps every other cluster's active tab and open
  state while it is not shown (`dockMemo`, run by `SyncDock` after every change). Every tab stays in
  `Dock`, its stream running (`dock_read` finds a hidden tab by its id); the window keeps every
  tab's content and shows the strip's (`dock.sync`). A tab an agent opens on a cluster the window
  does not show goes to that cluster's dock, active and open for when it is shown; `dock.activate`
  of such a tab shows its cluster first (`Session.Show`, no connect); the active tab closing gives
  way to a tab the dock shows, never to a hidden one; a local terminal belongs to the cluster it was
  opened for (`DockTab.Context`). `ui.toggleDock` is greyed while the shown cluster's dock has no tab.
- **The tab bar** followed the navigator's scope as before (`TabsInScope`): at the section every
  cluster's tabs. **Changed by the owner on 2026-10-20 (GW11)**, after a screenshot with a
  Deployments tab of one cluster beside the shown cluster's Alerts tab at the section ("Ich glaube
  das ist ein Bug"; asked which tabs it should show: "Man sieht doch ganz klar, auf dem Screeny
  (Titelleiste awe-p und Status-Leiste awe-p) in genau diesem Cluster bin ich also gerade. Und nur
  genau diese Tabs werden angezeigt."): it shows the shown cluster's tabs wherever the navigator
  stands (`TabsShown`), every tab only while no cluster is shown (the lead's detail, as the dock
  before any cluster is shown); another cluster's tabs come with that cluster, from its hotbar tile
  or its navigator row. It greys a tab only while its cluster is not connected. **The restore and a
  switch** (the owner, the same day, after the lead stopped to ask): "Beim Start mit
  wiederhergestellten Tabs: werden alle Tabs nur auf dem jeweiligen Cluster wiederhergestellt. Zu
  einem Cluster (der als letztes benutzte) wird Cogpit die Verbindung hot wieder aufbauen, dass ist
  der Cluster mit den Tabs den wir sehen. Die anderen Cluster zu denen wir cold verbunden sind,
  bekommen auch ihre Tabs wieder aufgebaut, aber die sind halt nicht eingeblendet. Das wird aber
  eine konfigurierbare Eigenschaft von Cogpit. Unten in der Übersicht von "All Clusters" soll es ein
  Flag geben: "mixed environments", dann werden immer alle geöffneten Tabs aller Cluster
  angezeigt. Default für dieses Flag ist aus. Hinter "mixed environments" wieder ein ?-Icon mit
  einer Erklärung im Tooltip." Built: the restore as item 8 had it (the shown cluster first, the
  others in the background), the bar the shown cluster's whatever its connection; the preference
  `mixedEnvironments` (`preferences.set`, `ui_state`'s `preferences`), a check "Mixed environments"
  at the foot of All Clusters with a "?" whose tooltip says what it does (the generated dialogs'
  hint, D-104). The lead's details, open to revision: app-wide, not per cluster; agents may set it
  either way (it changes only which tabs the bar shows); it is not in the Preferences page (its
  place is where the clusters are listed); the dock stays per cluster (item 9) with it on. Tests:
  `TestTabsShown`, `TestTabsShownMixedEnvironments`, `TestMixedEnvironmentsCheck`; renders
  `navigator_section_*.png`, `start_restored_*.png`. **No tab of a cluster without a connection**
  (the owner on v0.31.0, the same day, GW13: after the update's restart awe-p's expired certificate
  failed its connect, and its Pods tab stood over the welcome page; a click showed an empty Pods
  list for a moment and fell back: "Es sollen keine Tabs angezeigt werden, von Clustern zu denen
  keine Verbindung besteht."): the bar shows a tab only while its cluster's connection is live
  (connected, interrupted, its login expired), with mixed environments on too; while it connects,
  after a failed connect and once disconnected its tabs are hidden, kept, and show again when it
  connects. The greyed tab of a cluster that is not connected (stage 2) is gone with it. The lead's
  details, open to revision: connecting counts as no connection (its tabs come when it stands);
  interrupted and an expired login count as one (D-58 keeps their views). Tests:
  `TestTabsShownMixedEnvironments`'s connecting, failed and not-connected cases. The "?" of Mixed
  environments ended v0.31.0 on a hover (a nil tooltip, G16 GW14); fixed, its hover tested
  (`TestMixedEnvironmentsHintHover`), and its text says "every connected cluster".
- **Disconnect** in a connected cluster's tile, section row and welcome row menus passes its context
  (`cluster.disconnect {context}`, `disconnectOther`); the shown cluster's Disconnect is the
  window's as before. A connected cluster's first menu item says **Show**, not Connect.
- **Diagnostics** (item 3): a line per connected cluster under the summary, the shown one first,
  while more than one is connected: its API requests, open and warm watches, objects and memory
  (`DiagnosticsReport.Clusters`).
- **A failed connect while another cluster was shown** (the lead's item 7 of stage 2, replaced
  2026-10-19 by the owner's WF40, [D-97](#d-97-a-connect-goes-on-when-another-cluster-is-shown-a-failed-one-stays)):
  the window stays on the failed cluster with its error, Connect Again and Show Connection Updates,
  and its dots turn red; the cluster shown before stays connected behind it and is never shown by
  itself. Until 2026-10-19 the window showed the cluster it showed before again, with a toast.
- **`ConnectedCluster.LoginLapsed`** (JSON `loginLapsed`) added in [`connections.go`](../../internal/engine/connections.go)
  for the grey ring; stage 3 sets it.
- **Tests:** in the engine `TestDockFollowsTheShownCluster`, `TestAHiddenClustersTabStaysInItsDock`,
  `TestDockMemoIsCloned`, and `TestDockActivateShowsTheTabsCluster` in the commands; in the window
  `TestDotsShowEachClustersMark`, `TestABackgroundReconnectBlinksItsDots`,
  `TestAConnectedClusterIsShownWithoutAReview`, `TestDisconnectInAClustersMenuNamesIt`,
  `TestTabsGreyOnlyWithoutAConnection`, `TestAFailedConnectStaysOnItsCluster` (until 2026-10-19 `TestAFailedConnectShowsTheClusterBefore`),
  `TestAFailedConnectWithoutAnotherClusterStays`, `TestWelcomeRowsShowTheConnectedClusters`,
  `TestDiagnosticsListsEachCluster`, `TestDockShowsTheShownClustersTabs`. PNGs: the hotbar's marks
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/hotbar_marks_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/hotbar_marks_light.png)), the navigator's section
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_section_marks_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_section_marks_light.png)), the dock before and
  after a switch ([before](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/dock_cluster_before_dark.png),
  [after](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/dock_cluster_after_dark.png), light
  [before](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/dock_cluster_before_light.png),
  [after](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/dock_cluster_after_light.png)), the Diagnostics with two
  clusters ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/diagnostics_clusters_dark.png)).

**The lead's decisions of stage 2, open to revision:**

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The tab bar with several clusters connected | every connected cluster's tabs; the navigator's scope's; the shown cluster's | the scope's until 2026-10-20 (at the section every tab); **the shown cluster's since, the owner's GW11** | One cluster shown is the owner's model: the status bar and the navigator name it (the title bar too until 2026-10-21, D-54), and the bar shows its tabs; the dock already did (item 9) |
| A tab of another connected cluster | greyed as before; drawn as the shown one's | drawn as the shown one's; greyed only while its cluster is not connected | Grey said "a click connects"; a connected cluster's tab shows at once |
| Where the dock per cluster lives | the window; the engine | the engine (`dockscope.go`) | UI state is engine state: `ui_state`'s `activeDock` and `dockOpen` are what the dock shows, and `dock_read` still finds every tab |
| Tabs of no cluster (Audit Log, Diagnostics) | one cluster's dock; every cluster's | every cluster's | They show Cogpit's own state, not a cluster's |
| A cluster shown the first time | its last tab, open; collapsed | its last tab, collapsed; a tab of no cluster that was active stays, open as it was | Showing a cluster does not open a panel the user did not ask for |
| A tab an agent opens on a cluster not shown | show that cluster; that cluster's dock | that cluster's dock, active and open for when it is shown; the shown dock keeps its tab | Item 6: agents work on any connected cluster without moving the user's window |
| `dock.activate` of a hidden cluster's tab | refuse; show its cluster | show its cluster first, never a connect | As `ui.navigate` shows the cluster of an object (stage 1) |
| The dock's height | per cluster; the window's | the window's | A layout preference like the panels' widths, not engine state |
| The dock before any cluster is shown | its own tabs only; every tab | every tab | Nothing to scope by; only the Audit Log can be there then |
| A failed connect while another cluster was shown | the error shown (stage 1's choice); the cluster before shown again | the error shown, on the failed cluster, its dots red (since 2026-10-19, the owner's WF40, [D-97](#d-97-a-connect-goes-on-when-another-cluster-is-shown-a-failed-one-stays); until then the cluster before shown again, one toast) | The owner: a window that shows another cluster than the one the user chose, after a long login, invites acting on the wrong cluster; `cluster_connect`'s result says `error` |
| Which hotbar tile is raised | every connected one; the shown one | the shown one; the others carry their mark | The raised tile says where the window is, the dots what is connected |
| A connected cluster's menu item | Connect; Show | Show | It connects nothing |
| A failed last connect on a hotbar tile | the shown cluster's only; every tile | every tile red while the connect log says the last attempt failed | Item 5's red "a connect failed" on every dot; it stays red once another cluster is shown |
| The grey ring's colour | the muted text colour; the not-connected grey | the not-connected grey (`status.unknown`) as a line | Grey says resting, the ring that the connection stands |
| The ring's line | 1, 1.5 or 2 points | 1.5 points inside the 8-point dot | Readable at 1×; the dot's size unchanged |
| Several states at once | — | red over the grey ring over blinking over the green ring over filled | What needs the user first; a cold cluster's reconnect blinks (item 7) |
| Diagnostics with one cluster | a line for it; none | none: the summary says it; a line per cluster from two | No repetition |

**Not verified:** a real credential plugin and real clusters in the window (the tests drive a fake
engine; the engine's dock rules run against the pool's fake connectors); the marks on a Retina
screen (the renders are at 1×); the window under a wake that reconnects many clusters at once (each
change of `Connections` reads the hotbar again, not measured); the grey ring with stage 3's
`loginLapsed` on a real lapsed login.

**Stage 3, the two settings, built 2026-10-16** (the lead's run in a worktree of its own, beside
stage 2's):

- **Item 4, a background cluster's login** ([`connwatch_lapse.go`](../../internal/engine/connwatch_lapse.go),
  [`cluster/loginhold.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginhold.go)): Cluster Settings › General ›
  "Renew the login while the cluster is not shown", **on by default** (kept as its negation
  `holdBackgroundLogin` in `cluster-settings.json`, so that the default is the zero value;
  `cluster.settings.set {renewLoginInBackground}`, `cluster.settings.get`'s
  `renewLoginInBackground`). Off, a connected cluster the window does not show holds its credential
  plugin (`cluster.Conn.HoldLogin`; `Session.applyLoginHolds` after every show, connect and change
  of the setting). **How:** client-go's exec authenticator starts the plugin by itself in
  `refreshCredsLocked` (a credential expired by its time, none cached, a 401, a client
  certificate's handshake), inside its own round-tripper and in the exec, attach, port-forward and
  Helm transports, in front of which Cogpit has no round-tripper; `refreshCredsLocked` asks the
  Authenticator's unexported `interactiveFunc` first and runs nothing when it fails. Cogpit wraps
  that field once per Authenticator under the Authenticator's own lock, as D-66 sets its `stderr`:
  while every connection using the Authenticator holds it, the wrapper fails and **no plugin process
  starts**, and the request ends as `cluster.ErrLoginLapsed`; the login guard ends a held
  connection's 401 the same way instead of handing it to the plugin. The watch makes the login
  **lapsed**: `UIState.Connections[].loginLapsed` (the connection `connected` with `since` and the
  reason "the login lapsed; it is renewed when the cluster is shown"; not red), the gate holds the
  informers' lists and watches and refuses every other request with the lapsed login's error, the
  heartbeat pauses (a wake or a network change asks nothing of it), writes are disabled with "login
  lapsed: show the cluster to renew it", a log that has to open again writes "[cogpit] the login
  lapsed; it is renewed when the cluster is shown" and waits, port forwards do not dial, a running
  drain or Helm action stops as at an interruption. **Shown again**, the login is renewed as D-58
  renews the shown cluster's: the approved plugin runs once (one whose program changed asks first,
  D-26), Login expired (red, Log in again) when that does not help within 30 s. **Log in again**
  (`cluster.login {context?}`, GUI only, with a context since stage 3) renews it where it is, the
  hold let go for that login only; turning the setting on renews it in the background.
- **Item 8, restoring the last session** ([`restore.go`](../../internal/engine/restore.go),
  [`connect_background.go`](../../internal/engine/connect_background.go)): Preferences › App ›
  "Restore the last session", **off by default** (`preferences.set {restoreSession}`); since
  2026-10-17 evening also a checkbox on the welcome page under "Add Kubeconfigs…" (the owner's walk,
  WF1: he missed it there; the same preference, the lead's wording and place, open to revision;
  [`welcome.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/welcome.go) `welcomeRestoreLabel`).
  `workspace.json` keeps `connected` (every context of `UIState.Connections`) and `shown` beside the
  tabs (D-41 changed above). At start with it on, the tabs come back as D-41 restored them, and
  `Session.RestoreLastSession` (called by `cmd/cogpit` before the window runs) connects the cluster
  shown at quit with `Connect`, which the window shows as any connect, then the others one after
  another with `ConnectBackground`, a connect that shows nothing (the cluster joins the pool cold,
  its entry `connecting` while it connects; a user's connect of it meanwhile waits for it and shows
  it). Each is a connect of the user's: an approved credential plugin runs as on any connect, one not
  allowed yet or changed since is refused with its reason (D-26). `--context` shows its own cluster
  and the restore connects the others behind it; a context no kubeconfig source offers any more is
  left out with a notice; a background connect that fails says why in a toast. Off: no tab, no
  connect. `cogpit-cli` reads no workspace and is not affected.
- **Agents** (D-2): both settings are UI commands, and each one's "on" makes Cogpit run credential
  plugins without a click, so agents and the CLI may turn each **off** only
  (`ErrRenewLoginGUIOnly`, `ErrRestoreSessionGUIOnly`); `cluster.login` stays GUI-only. An agent's
  read of a lapsed cluster comes from the cache with a note (`lapsedNote`), one that needs the
  cluster and every write get the lapsed login's error; no agent command renews it but a show
  (`cluster.connect`, `ui.navigate`), which the window shows.
- **Tests:** on client-go with a credential plugin script that notes each run,
  `TestHeldPluginDoesNotRun` (a held, expired login: `ErrLoginLapsed`, no process; let go, one run),
  `TestHeldLoginKeepsA401FromThePlugin`, `TestSharedLoginIsHeldOnlyWhenEveryConnectionHoldsIt`,
  `TestHoldWithoutAPluginChangesNothing`, and in the engine `TestHeldPluginOnARealStack` (two fake
  API servers: the background cluster's plugin login lapses without a run, showing it runs the
  plugin once); `TestABackgroundLoginLapsesWhileHeld`, `TestLogInAgainRenewsALapsedBackgroundLogin`,
  `TestTurningTheRenewalOnRenewsALapsedLogin`, `TestABackgroundLoginIsRenewedByDefault`,
  `TestALogOfALapsedClusterWaitsWithANotice`, `TestRenewLoginInBackgroundIsOnByDefaultAndKept`,
  `TestRestoreSessionIsOffByDefault`, `TestRestoreOffStartsWithoutTabsAndConnections`,
  `TestWorkspaceOfV0170Loads`, `TestWorkspaceKeepsTheConnections`,
  `TestRestoreOnConnectsTheLastSession` and `TestRestoreBehindAnExplicitContext` (two fake API
  servers), `TestRestoreOffOnARealStack`, `TestConnectWaitsForTheBackgroundConnect`;
  `TestSessionSettingsAgentsMayOnlyTurnThemOff`; in the window `TestPreferencesRestoreSession`,
  `TestClusterSettingsRenewLogin`, `TestStartWithoutTheRestoreShowsNoTabs`, renders
  `preferences_restore_session_{dark,light}.png` and `cluster_settings_login_{dark,light}.png`. The
  workspace tests that assumed the tabs come back by default turn the preference on.

**The lead's decisions of stage 3, open to revision:**

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the plugin is held | Cogpit runs the plugin itself (client-go's exec authenticator re-done); refuse every request of a background cluster; wrap the Authenticator's `interactiveFunc` | wrap `interactiveFunc`; the login guard for the 401 | client-go starts the plugin inside its own round-tripper and transports Cogpit cannot wrap; `refreshCredsLocked` asks `interactiveFunc` before it builds the command. The reflection is D-66's, and a test fails on a client-go that renames the field. Refusing every request would also stop a working login's streams; re-doing the authenticator was rejected in D-58 |
| Two contexts with the same plugin configuration | held per connection; per Authenticator | held only while every connection using it holds it | client-go keeps one login per plugin configuration: the shown cluster's renewal serves both, and holding it for the shown one would break the cluster the user looks at |
| What renews a lapsed login | showing the cluster; Log in again; an agent's command on it | showing it (an agent's `cluster.connect` or `ui.navigate` too, which the window shows), Log in again, turning the setting on | The lead's suggestion: an agent's read or write gets the lapsed login's error, never a silent plugin run |
| Streams of a lapsed cluster | stop them; let the open ones run and hold the ones that must open again | the open ones run (the API server checked the login when they opened); a log that must open again writes the notice line and waits; port forwards do not dial; a shell is not ended | Stopping a working stream loses output for nothing; a shell cannot be resumed |
| A drain or Helm action when the login lapses | go on; stop as at an interruption | stop (`errJobLoginLapsed`, `OperationContext`), finishable afterwards (D-11) | Its next request would fail anyway |
| The heartbeat while lapsed | on; paused | paused; a wake and a network change ask nothing either | Every request would fail; reachability is checked when the cluster is shown |
| The renewal setting's agents' rule | free both ways; the user only; agents may turn it off | agents and the CLI may turn it off only | Off runs less; on lets a browser login pop up while the user works elsewhere |
| The restore's connects | all at once; the shown first, the others concurrently; the shown first, then one after another | the shown first, then one after another in the background | The lead's suggestion: the window is usable at once, and never two plugins (two browser logins) ask at the same time; a plugin that waits holds the next ones back at most for its connect's limit |
| What the file keeps with the preference off | nothing of the session; the session as at quit | the session as at quit (`connected`, `shown`, the tabs) | Turning the preference on later restores the session of the last quit; the file held the tabs' context ids before |
| What comes back with the preference off | nothing; the window's arrangement | the column layout, the collapsed groups, the navigator hidden, the chat column | They are the window's arrangement; the owner's "without tabs and without connections" names the session |
| The dock's tabs | restored where they can be reopened (logs, the Audit Log); none, as D-41 | none, as D-41 | A log would open a stream and a shell run `exec` (a write) at start; an editor's text has its draft; the dock per cluster is stage 2's |
| The restore's agents' rule | free; the user only; agents may turn it off | agents and the CLI may turn it off only | The lead's suggestion: on, the next start connects clusters and runs their plugins without a click |
| `--context` with the restore on | skip the restore; restore behind it | its cluster shown, the others (the one shown at quit among them) connected in the background | The explicit wish wins the window; the rest of the session still comes back |
| A plugin not allowed at the restore | a dialog at start; refused with the reason | refused with its reason (a toast, or the shown cluster's error on the welcome page) | D-57's road for `--context`: allowed in the navigator, never a dialog that pops up at start |

**Not verified in stage 3:** a real credential plugin (kubelogin with a browser) held on a real
cluster and renewed when shown; the restore on the owner's computer with his clusters; a real lapsed
login in the window (stage 2's grey ring reads `loginLapsed`; rendered from a test state only).

## D-70: The disk image's window

**The need (the owner, 2026-10-16 morning, F15):** the disk image opened in Finder's default
window, small icons on white ("absolut hässlich"). Wanted: big icons, Cogpit on the left, an arrow,
the Applications folder on the right, and under the folder Kubernetes's helm wheel, to say "Cogpit
goes into your Kubernetes lifecycle". He decided that the look and the trademark question are
settled with him interactively, in a visual review, never by the lead.

**The review (2026-10-16):** a lab (a claude.ai artifact, its link in
[`packaging/dmg/lab.json`](../../packaging/dmg/lab.json)) drew the window in light and dark Finder
side by side, with presets and controls for the background, the arrow, the wheel, the icons and
the window, and the names' contrast measured on the background under them. **The owner's pick:**
a 600 × 340 window on the app's plate (the logo's navy gradient and halo), the icons at 124 points
at 27 % and 68 % of the width, a straight light-blue arrow, Cogpit's own wheel (the logo's wheel
without the C) at 240 points and 22 % opacity behind the Applications folder, the names at 14 points
on grey pills (about 4.4:1 against both black and white, so they read in both Finder themes).

**The trademark (read 2026-10-16, not legal advice):** the Kubernetes logo falls under the Linux
Foundation's trademark guidelines ([usage guidelines](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/logo/usage_guidelines.md),
[LF trademark usage](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/legal/trademark-usage)): modifying it is allowed
for non-commercial items such as t-shirts and stickers; a mark is not to be incorporated into one's
own logos or designs, used on marketing material, recoloured or overlaid, and must not imply
endorsement. An installer's background is the product's own design, so the official logo was not
offered without the Foundation's written permission; a seven-spoke heptagon in Kubernetes blue was
shown for comparison only and not recommended (confusingly similar). The wheel in the disk image is
Cogpit's own drawing.

**How it is built (the owner's choice of three, 2026-10-16):** dmgbuild (pure Python, MIT, pinned
by version and hash) writes Finder's view settings itself, without Finder or AppleScript, so it runs
on a CI runner; but it is code from PyPI, and until now the signing job ran only Apple's tools and
bash. Options weighed: (a) a template made in the app's job, which holds no secret, filled in by
the signing job with Apple's tools after checking its contents; (b) a job of its own building the
whole image around the signed app, the signing job comparing the app's code directory hash (a job
and an artifact more, about five minutes per release, estimated); (c) dmgbuild in the signing job
with its environment emptied and the keychain locked (third-party code on the same machine as the
identity, which a left-behind process could use once the keychain is unlocked for the disk image).
**Chosen: (a)**, the lead's recommendation ([releasing › the disk image's window](releasing.md#the-disk-images-window)).

The lead's decisions of the build, open to revision:

| Decision | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The tool | dmgbuild 1.6.7 with ds_store 1.3.3 and mac_alias 2.2.3, wheels only, `--require-hashes` | `create-dmg` drives Finder through AppleScript and needs a login session; a `.DS_Store` made once by hand breaks with the volume's name, which carries the version |
| Python on CI | `actions/setup-python@v6`, 3.13 | dmgbuild needs 3.10 or newer, the system's Python is 3.9 |
| The background | the lab's own drawing code rendered at 1× and 2× (headless Chrome), committed as PNGs, joined into one TIFF at build time | the window the owner saw is the one that ships, pixel for pixel |
| The check of the template | a UDRW image, the volume's name, exactly `.DS_Store`, `.background.tiff`, `.VolumeIcon.icns` and `Applications` → `/Applications` | anything else in the template would ship signed and notarized; the files' bytes are not checked ([updates › H-18](../security/updates.md#h-18-dependencies)) |
| Hiding `.app` | no Finder flag | `SetFile -a E` puts `com.apple.FinderInfo` on the bundle and `codesign --verify --strict` refuses it; Finder hides an app's extension anyway |
| Renovate | proposes updates of the three packages, never merges them on its own | their output ships in every disk image |

**Built 2026-10-16:** [`dmg-template.sh`](../../hack/macos/dmg-template.sh),
[`dmg_settings.py`](../../hack/macos/dmg_settings.py),
[`dmgbuild-requirements.txt`](../../hack/macos/dmgbuild-requirements.txt), `build_dmg` and
`check_dmg` in [`release.sh`](../../hack/macos/release.sh), the step in
[`build.yml`](../../.github/workflows/build.yml)'s app job, `make dist-dmg-template`. **Checked**
locally (`make dist-app`, `dist-dmg-template`, `dist-macos MACOS_SIGN=adhoc`, VERSION 0.0.99).
**Not checked yet:** a Retina screen (the owner's two are at 1×).

**The name pills, the owner's WF42 (walk of 2026-10-19 on v0.26.1, verbatim):** "Die Unterlegung der
Namen sitzt nicht richtig. Beide Namen sind zu niedrig auf der Hinterlegung und die Pill hinter
Cogpit ist zu schmal." **Measured** the same afternoon in a disk image whose background was a ruler,
opened in Finder on his Mac, his screenshot read out: Finder writes the names with the capitals'
top 76 points and the baseline 86 points under the icon's centre (descenders to 87), centred on it,
in black in the dark mode too; "Cogpit.app" 69 points wide (his Finder shows extensions, so the
name has ".app"), "Applications" 77. The lab had placed them 6 points under the icon: its pills
lay 66–89 points under the centre (the text's middle at 81, the pills' at 77.5) and were made for
"Cogpit", 59 points wide. **The lab** ([its link](https://claude.ai/artifact/GYAkHGF8QJpVwXBFnCSpKg),
version 2) draws the names where Finder does and offers the pills' place, height, margin, width and
rounding. **The owner's pick (2026-10-19, in a visual review, then a disk image in his real
Finder: "passt"):** the pills centred on the names (70–91 points under the icon's centre), 22 points
high, both as wide as the wider name plus 10 points a side (102 points), their corners rounded to
40 % of a half circle, grey at 90 % as before ([`lab.json`](../../packaging/dmg/lab.json)'s new
`pill*` settings and `ext`; the backgrounds the lab rendered, made smaller losslessly by the pinned
oxipng). Measured for icons of 124 points and names of 14 points; other sizes the lab estimates.

## D-67: The demo cluster stays out of releases

**Decided by the owner (2026-10-16, task F14):** "Der Demo-Cluster ist für die Entwicklung, er soll
nicht über den Release ausgeliefert werden." Asked how, he chose: compiled out of release builds by
a build tag that only the release pipeline sets. A release then contains neither package
`internal/demo` nor the flags `--demo`, `--demo-pods` and `--demo-events`, and lists no context
`demo`; development builds, `make run-demo`, the tests and the README's pictures (`make showcase`)
keep the demo. Releases up to v0.16.0 carry it.

**Built 2026-10-16.** The choices of the build, open to revision:

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The tag's name | `release` (what the build is); `nodemo` (what it leaves out); a positive `demo` that development builds would set | `nodemo` | A `release` tag would invite other release-only behaviour behind the same switch, code that no development build, test or CI job runs. A negative tag keeps every build without tags as it was (`go test`, `go run`, gopls, golangci-lint, `make showcase`); only the pipeline opts out. No dependency reacts to it: none of the 1,614 package directories both binaries build from has a file constrained by `nodemo` (checked 2026-10-16) |
| Where the tag cuts | a pair of tagged files in every package that names the demo (the UI, the commands, `cogpit-cli`); a pair only where the demo is wired in, and everything else from data or one constant | the second: [`engine/connector_demo.go`](../../internal/engine/connector_demo.go) (`//go:build !nodemo`: `DemoBuilt = true`, `DemoOptions` = `demo.Options`, the demo's backend) against [`connector_nodemo.go`](../../internal/engine/connector_nodemo.go) (`DemoBuilt = false`, an empty `DemoOptions`), and [`cmd/cogpit/demo.go`](../../cmd/cogpit/demo.go) (the three flags) against [`nodemo.go`](../../cmd/cogpit/nodemo.go) | The window shows the demo only where the connector says so (`ContextInfo.Demo`, `Connection.Demo`): with no such context, the welcome page, the navigator, the hotbar and the status bar have nothing to show. The constant lets the compiler drop the remaining branches |
| `ClusterConnector.IncludeDemo` in a release | remove the field; keep it without effect | kept, ignored (`DemoBuilt && IncludeDemo`) | `cogpit-cli` and the tests set it unconditionally; one rule in one place |
| A kubeconfig context called `demo` in a release | shadowed by a demo that is not there; one like any other | one like any other: listed, resolved and connected through its kubeconfig; Cluster Settings and Remove from Cogpit treat it as any context (`engine.IsDemoContext` is false) | Only a run without a configuration directory gives a context its bare name as its id, but there the old comparison with `"demo"` would have shown the demo's notes for a real cluster; with sources, a bare `demo` (`--context`, a link, an agent) now resolves to the one file that defines it |
| Texts that named the demo (the tools `cluster_contexts`, `cluster_connect` and `cluster_remove`; `cogpit-cli contexts --help`, `get`'s `--context` and its usage example; a Prometheus setting's refusal) | worded per build; worded for both | for both | The demo's id is "a context id as `cluster_contexts` lists it"; the generated [commands.md](commands.md), from a development build, stays true for a release. The Prometheus refusal names the demo only when the connection is the demo |
| What guards it | the release's own check; a Go test of the Makefile; a check in CI | all three: `make dist-app` passes `DIST_TAGS` and fails unless `go version -m` shows `-tags=nodemo` for both binaries; [`TestReleaseBuildsLeaveTheDemoOut`](../../internal/engine/connector_test.go) checks that `dist-app` passes `DIST_TAGS`, that `build` gives both binaries `GO_TAGS`, and that `DIST_TAGS` name the tag of `connector_nodemo.go`; CI's lint job runs `make check-nodemo` | A tag no file knows is ignored without a word, and the release would ship the demo. `check-nodemo` proves the result: `go list -deps` has `internal/demo` in both binaries without the tag and in neither with it, `./cmd/...` and `./internal/engine/...` lint with it, and `TestNoDemoInARelease` runs in `internal/engine` and `cmd/cogpit-cli` |
| Which job runs `check-nodemo` | a new job; the macOS job; the lint job | the lint job | Linux, 3.2 minutes, Fyne's headers installed; about a minute more locally (not measured on CI yet) |
| Tests that need the demo | compiled with the tag and failing; left out with the tag | left out where the tag is vetted: `engine/connector_demo_test.go` (the demo tests of `detail_test.go` and `applications_test.go` moved there) and `hidemetrics_test.go` carry `//go:build !nodemo`, and `cogpit-cli`'s tests size the demo in `demo_test.go` (`nodemo_test.go` for the variant) | The packages `check-nodemo` lints compile with the tag, tests included. The UI's, the agent's and the kind tests drive the demo and are not compiled with the tag |

**What it saves** (2026-10-16, darwin/arm64, `go build -ldflags '-s -w'` as `DIST_LDFLAGS`): the
app's `cogpit` 108,649,938 bytes without the tag, 108,341,170 with it (308,768 less); `cogpit-cli`
75,175,330 against 74,904,306 (271,024 less), about 0.3 % each. The release binaries carry no
string of the flags (`demo-pods`, their help text) and no symbol of `internal/demo` (checked with
`grep -a`). The point is the owner's: a release ships no development fixture, not the bytes.

**After an update from v0.16.0 or earlier** (read in the code, not tried): a restored tab of the
context `demo` is dropped as a context no longer offered (`goneContexts`: not offered, while the
list of contexts read without an error), and a hotbar tile of it shows as missing.

**Open:** the owner's confirmation of the build's choices; `check-nodemo`'s time on CI; Windows
releases (M11) must build through `DIST_TAGS` too. The Linux packages do since 2026-10-20: `make
dist-linux` builds both binaries with `DIST_TAGS` and checks they recorded them, as `dist-app` does
([D-108](#d-108-cogpit-for-linux-a-deb-and-an-apt-repository-on-pages)).

## D-68: One short name for a cluster, and the user Cogpit is logged in as

**Changed 2026-10-19 by the owner's decision on [H-125](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-125-until-the-accent-colour-shows-a-clusters-name-and-icon-colour-are-agents-to-change)**
("Nein, sollen sie nicht können."; built the same day, [D-2](#d-2-agent-interface-scope)): the
display name that wins over the short name below, and the icon beside it, are the user's alone:
agents and the CLI read them but no longer set or clear them (`cluster.settings.set`'s `name` and
`iconColor` refused, `cluster.settings.resetIcon` GUI-only; `TestClusterIdentityIsTheUsers`). So
the name the window shows of a cluster is the user's or the kubeconfig's, never an agent's. The rest
stands.

**Decided by the owner (2026-10-16 morning, task F17)**, his answers of the same morning. He looked
at the navigator's root row: its badge, the cluster's name (the Cluster Settings' name, else the
context's) and as its subtitle the kubeconfig file, "Synthetic demo cluster" or a connection word.

1. **One short name for a cluster, everywhere** ("überall gleich"): a context name with an "@"
   shows only the part after the last "@" ("kubernetes-admin@prod-eu" → "prod-eu"), else the whole
   name; a name the user set in Cluster Settings › General still wins. The window names a context so
   wherever it names one: the navigator's root and section rows, the hotbar's tiles, the status bar
   (and the top bar until 2026-10-21, [D-54](#d-54-the-layout-toggles-and-the-update-button)), the
   tab bar, the command palette and the welcome page. The full context name
   stays in each tooltip and in Cluster Settings. The navigator's search still finds a context by
   its full name. Agents keep the full context ids in every command and in `ui_state`.
2. **The user Cogpit is logged in as, in the root row's subtitle**, fetched live at every connect
   as `kubectl auth whoami` asks: a `SelfSubjectReview` in package `cluster`, no kubectl process; a
   failure never fails the connect; renewed when the login is renewed and on every reconnect that
   re-authenticates. Shown: the username, and beside it a small box with an icon whose tooltip lists
   the groups, the groups only (no UID, no extra fields); no groups, no box.
3. **Fallback:** where the API server does not know the review (404, older than 1.27) or refuses
   it (403), the kubeconfig's user entry's name with the mark "(kubeconfig)" and the tooltip "not
   confirmed by the API server"; the reason in the connect log's line.
4. **Not connected:** the last known user of the context, dimmed, its tooltip saying when it was
   last seen ("last seen 2026-10-16 09:12", in the user's date and time format, D-31). Only the
   username is kept, per context, where Cogpit keeps its per-cluster state, owner-only. Never
   connected: the kubeconfig file as before. The demo cluster keeps "Synthetic demo cluster".
5. **Agents:** `ui_state` names the shown cluster's username and groups, and whether the API server
   confirmed them or the kubeconfig stands in. A read without secrets; that an agent (and a built-in
   agent's LLM endpoint) can learn the organisation's structure from the groups is the owner's
   choice ([agents and MCP › H-113](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-113-the-users-name-and-groups-reach-every-agent-that-reads-ui_state)).

**Built 2026-10-16.** Where:

| What | Code |
|---|---|
| The short name | [`engine.ShortContextName`](../../internal/engine/displayname.go) (the part after the last "@", trimmed; nothing after it keeps the whole name), used by [`engine.ClusterName`](../../internal/engine/clustersettings.go) (the display name, else the short name of the context's name without its file), which the window's `sh.identity` and every place below read: the tabs' titles (`tabTitle`), the palette's tile entries, the hotbar's tiles (`HotbarTile.DisplayName`, new beside `label`), `cluster.settings.get`'s `name` |
| The review | [`cluster.Conn.ReviewUser`](../../internal/cluster/whoami.go): `authentication.k8s.io/v1` `SelfSubjectReviews().Create`, on a 404 `v1beta1` once more (client-go 0.37.1 has both typed clients); the username and the deduplicated groups kept on the connection (`Conn.User`), UID and extra dropped there; 404, 403 and every other failure give the kubeconfig's user entry's name, read again from the connection's files, with the reason |
| At the connect | [`engine/whoami.go`](../../internal/engine/whoami.go): `Session.learnUser`, one line in `Session.Connect` after the connector returned and before the connection is published, bounded by 5 s (`DefaultProbeTimeout`); its line in the connect log ("Logged in as … (confirmed by the API server); groups: …", or "The API server did not confirm the user: <reason>; Cogpit shows the kubeconfig's user entry …") |
| The renewal | `Session.renewUser`, one line in the connection watch's `reconnect` (connwatch.go): after an interruption and after Log in again (`cluster.login`), in the background; "Logged in again as …" in the connect log |
| The UI state | `UIState.User` (`ClusterUser`: `context`, `username`, `groups`, `source` `apiServer`, `kubeconfig` or `lastSeen`, `reason`, `lastSeen`), derived after every change (`syncUser`) from the session's book of answers and last known users |
| The last known users | [`engine/whoami_store.go`](../../internal/engine/whoami_store.go): `<user config dir>/Cogpit/cluster-users.json` beside `cluster-settings.json`, owner-only, the username and when it was last seen per context id |
| The window | [`fyneui/clusteruser.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clusteruser.go) (the root row's subtitle, the groups' box, its tooltips), [`fyneui/clustername.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clustername.go) (the bars' name with the full name as the tooltip) |
| Tests | `TestShortContextName`, `TestClusterNameIsTheShortName`, `TestConnectLearnsTheUser`, `TestUserFallsBackToTheKubeconfig`, `TestLoginRenewsTheUser`, `TestSyncUserFollowsTheContext`, `TestLastUsersFileUnreadable`, `TestPaletteNamesTilesByTheShortName`, `TestHotbarTilesCarryTheDisplayName` (engine); `TestReviewUser*` (cluster, against the fake API server's `FakeIdentity`: v1, v1beta1 only, 404, 403, 500); `TestRootRow*`, `TestShortClusterNameEverywhere` and the renders `navigator_user*` (window); `TestKindWhoAmI` (kind: a ServiceAccount without permissions of its own, its username and its three groups confirmed, one review) |

**The lead's decisions, open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| When the connect's review runs | before the connection shows Connected; in the background after it | before, bounded by 5 s | The root row never shows a connected cluster without its user, and `ui_state` names the user the moment `connection.state` says connected. The cost is one round trip on the connect (P1 counts it; measured on the fake API server: within the connect's 25–34 ms); a server that does not answer the review delays the connect by 5 s at most, then the fallback stands |
| Kubernetes 1.26's `v1alpha1` | ask it after `v1beta1`; not | not | Behind a feature gate that is off by default; a third request on every old cluster for almost none |
| What renews it | only after Log in again; every reconnect | every reconnect (after an interruption and after Log in again) | Cogpit cannot tell whether the credential plugin ran while the connection was away (its token may be another identity's); one request per reconnect |
| What "last seen" is | the connect's time; the time the connection ended | both: the last confirmation (connect, renewal), and the moment a connection that showed it ended (a disconnect, another cluster, a failed reconnect) | Tells the user when that identity last worked, not only when it began |
| What is kept | every answer; only the API server's | only usernames the API server confirmed, never the fallback's label, never the groups | The fallback's name says nothing of who the server sees; the groups were the owner's "not stored" |
| Where it is kept | in `cluster-settings.json`; a file of its own | `cluster-users.json` beside it | It is no setting: `cluster.settings.get` and the settings' `IsZero` would change with every connect |
| The fallback's and the last known user's tooltips | the owner's words alone; with a second line | the owner's words, then a line: "The name of the context's user entry in its kubeconfig; its connection updates say why", "The user the API server last confirmed for this cluster" | The reason itself stays in the connect log and in `ui_state`'s `reason` |
| The groups' box | an icon; an icon and a count | an icon (two people, drawn for Cogpit) in a small outlined box | The owner's words; the tooltip lists them |
| Its tooltip | the box a hoverable widget of its own; the row choosing its tooltip by where the pointer is | the row (`tipAt`) | The row keeps its hover while the pointer crosses the box and the name |
| The short name's edge cases | | "@prod" → "prod"; "admin@", "@" and blanks after the last "@" keep the whole name | Nothing after the "@" would leave no name |
| The full name where nothing has a tooltip | — | the palette's tile entry: "Open prod-eu", the full context name as its category (shown at the row's end and searched); the welcome page's row: the short name as its title, "context <full name>" in its second line, as for a display name | The palette's and the welcome page's rows have no tooltips |
| The tooltips that carry the full name | | the section row's first line (the full context name before its source; until now the display name), a tab's (its title, then the context id), the status bar's (the context id with its file; the top bar's name, the context's full name with the file beside it, went 2026-10-21, D-54), the hotbar tile's and the root row's (the context id, as before) | |
| What keeps the full id | | the engine's connect log and toasts ("Connecting to <id>", "Reconnected to <id>"), Remove from Cogpit's list of the contexts that leave with a file, the navigator items' "<item> - <context>" tooltips | Logs and a confirmation name exactly what they mean; the hotbar's own toasts use the short name |
| Where the root row shows a cluster that is not connected | | while it connects (the navigator shows the section after a failed connect or a disconnect, D-57); its dot says the state, the subtitle the last known user | |

**Open:** Lens's root row is not captured for a
user, so the row is Cogpit's own ([UI parity](../parity/ui-parity.md)).

## D-71: Thanos and VictoriaMetrics, read as Prometheus

**The lead's decisions (night run 2026-10-16/17), built the same night, open to revision.** Lens's Metrics provider list names VictoriaMetrics and VictoriaMetrics single besides
the Prometheus installations (captured); Cogpit found Prometheus by its Services' names only, so a
cluster whose metrics live in Thanos or VictoriaMetrics had them only through the address the user
typed, and the window called them "Prometheus". Both speak the Prometheus HTTP API, so the provider
and its queries stay as they are ([architecture §9](architecture.md#9-metrics-internalmetrics),
"Thanos and VictoriaMetrics under their own names"; G12). Cogpit still installs nothing (D-61).

| Question | Options | Choice | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) How they are found | (a) by their Services' names among the cached Services, as Prometheus is; (b) a buildinfo probe of every Service on a port such as 9090, 8428 or 8481; (c) the operators' custom resources (VMSingle, VMCluster, a Thanos operator's) | ★ (a) | (b) sends requests to services that are none of these, each learning nothing but receiving a request with the user's identity; (c) needs the right to list those kinds and a watch for each, and misses the charts' installs. (a) costs nothing new: the same cached Services, the same three probes at most |
| (2) Which names | the charts' and operators' documented defaults: Thanos's Querier (`<release>-thanos-query`, `thanos-query`, `thanos-querier`) and query frontend (`…-thanos-query-frontend`); VictoriaMetrics single-node (`vmsingle-<name>`, `<release>-victoria-metrics-single-server`) and the cluster's vmselect (`vmselect-<name>`, `<release>-victoria-metrics-cluster-vmselect`) | as listed | The components that answer the query API. The store gateway, the compactor, the ruler, the receiver, the gRPC Services, vminsert, vmstorage, vmagent, vmalert and vmauth never: they would cost a probe and answer nothing Cogpit can draw (vmauth fronts a vmselect but needs its own credentials) |
| (3) Their rank beside a Prometheus | ★ (a) after every Prometheus name (Thanos 76 and 75, VictoriaMetrics 74 and 73; `prometheus-server` 80, a bare `prometheus` 70); (b) before them, for the longer history a Querier or VictoriaMetrics keeps; (c) never automatically, the user names them | ★ (a) | A Prometheus by its own names holds the cluster's own series; a Querier or a VictoriaMetrics may hold several clusters', and Cogpit's queries do not narrow by a cluster label, so the Overview's sums would count other clusters' nodes. (b) would change what a cluster that runs both shows today, the owner's test cluster among them; (c) leaves a cluster that runs only VictoriaMetrics without history. The user names a Querier in Cluster Settings › Metrics for its longer history |
| (4) vmselect's tenant | ★ (a) the default tenant, `/select/0/prometheus`; (b) try several tenants; (c) ask | ★ (a) | VictoriaMetrics' cluster stores a write without a tenant under 0; another tenant is the path prefix the user sets (the settings' help names `/select/<tenant>/prometheus`). (b) costs a probe per guess; (c) asks something most never need |
| (5) The name shown | ★ (a) the product's, "Thanos", "VictoriaMetrics"; (b) the component's, "Thanos Querier", "vmselect"; (c) "Prometheus" as before | ★ (a) | The source line already names the Service, which tells the Querier from its frontend and vmsingle from vmselect; (c) told the user something that is not what runs |
| (6) A service the user names | ★ (a) named by the same rules (the name, else a vmselect tenant's path), the prefix taken as typed; (b) "Prometheus" for every address the user types; (c) the default tenant's path added to a vmselect named without one | ★ (a) | The user's address is the same service detection would find; (c) would change what the user typed: a vmselect named without its path answers "not found or not a Prometheus", and the help line says which path it needs |

**Built 2026-10-16 night** ([`metrics/promflavor.go`](../../internal/metrics/promflavor.go),
[`metrics/promdetect.go`](../../internal/metrics/promdetect.go); `TestCandidatesThanosAndVictoriaMetrics`,
`TestDetectThanosAndVictoriaMetrics`, `TestFlavorNames`). **Checked:** a real Thanos 0.40 Querier and
query frontend on a cluster the owner provides for tests, read only (`TestRealThanos`: candidates by
these rules, named in the setting the drawers' history and network through each); VictoriaMetrics
v1.106.1 single-node and a cluster on kind (`make kind-vm`, `TestKindVictoriaMetrics`). What the
owner sees: on a cluster that runs a Prometheus too, as the test cluster does, nothing changes; a
cluster whose metrics are a Thanos or a VictoriaMetrics alone gets history where it said "no
Prometheus found"; a named Thanos or VictoriaMetrics is called so.

### What it does not cover

- **Auto-detection on a cluster without a Prometheus,** live: neither cluster at hand has one, so
  detection choosing a Querier or a VictoriaMetrics by itself is checked against fakes only.
- **A store of several clusters,** dormant until a Querier or VictoriaMetrics that holds them is
  found or named: the Overview's sums and the pod counts count every cluster's (no cluster label
  narrows the queries); a drawer's object is narrowed by its names, which may match another
  cluster's object of the same name.
- **Names an operator makes,** inferred: the kind manifests are written by hand, named as
  VictoriaMetrics' operator documents a VMSingle's and a VMCluster's Services.
- **MetricsQL,** inferred: VictoriaMetrics' `rate` does not extrapolate as Prometheus's does; the
  charts checked on kind matched in shape, not compared point by point.

## D-72: Native file panels and macOS folder access

**Ordered by the owner (2026-10-16 night)**, his words: "Ach und wenn man in der App irgendwo ein
Bild oder ein kube_config, per file picker suchen soll, dann nimmst du bitte den Systempicker.
Jeweils vom jeweiligen OS, hier MacOS. Mir ist auch schon aufgefallen, dass ich nach Permissions
auf User Folder durch MacOS aufgefordert wurde. Das wollen wir vermeiden." Two requirements: every
file chooser of the window is the operating system's own (macOS first), and Cogpit no longer
raises macOS's privacy prompts for the user's folders ("Cogpit would like to access files in your
Documents folder").

**What raised the prompts (verified in the code, 2026-10-16 night).** Every chooser was drawn by
Fyne. Fyne's file dialog (v2.8.2) builds its sidebar each time it is shown: `loadFavorites` asks
`storage.ListerForURI` for `~/Desktop`, `~/Documents`, `~/Downloads`, `~/Music`, `~/Pictures` and
`~/Movies`, and Fyne's `CanList` opens each folder and reads one entry (`Readdir(1)`;
`fyne.io/fyne/v2/dialog/file.go`, `internal/repository/file.go`). Desktop, Documents and Downloads
are protected by macOS's Files and Folders privacy (TCC), so opening any Fyne file dialog of
Cogpit's (a cluster's icon, a folder, a chat connection's CA file, each of the three saves) asked
for up to three folders before the user chose anything. Cogpit's own Sync Files and Folders browser
listed only the folder the user opened. Further sources of a prompt, by their mechanism: a
kubeconfig source, a CA file or a terminal folder in a protected folder, read again in every run;
the files a kubeconfig names there; a shell or credential plugin Cogpit starts there. Which prompt
the owner saw is not known.

**Built 2026-10-16 (night run).**

| What | Code |
|---|---|
| The panels | [`internal/ui/nativedialog`](../../internal/ui/nativedialog/): `Open` and `Save` show NSOpenPanel and NSSavePanel through cgo as a sheet on the NSWindow Fyne hands out (`driver.MacWindowContext`), configured from `OpenOptions` and `SaveOptions` (title, message, button, files and/or folders, several, hidden files, the allowed extensions as `UTType`s, the folder to open in, the suggested name); the answer is handed to Go on the main thread and on through `fyne.Do`; no goroutine waits for it. Elsewhere and without cgo `ErrUnsupported` ([`panel_darwin.m`](../../internal/ui/nativedialog/panel_darwin.m), [`panel_other.go`](../../internal/ui/nativedialog/panel_other.go)) |
| The choosers | One seam on the shell, `filePicker` ([`filepicker.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/filepicker.go)): the system's panels in the app (`Run`), none in the shell's default, a recorder in tests; each chooser falls back to its Fyne dialog where no panel is shown ([`filepicker_choosers.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/filepicker_choosers.go)). Sync Files and Folders: one open panel for files and folders, several at once, hidden files listed, the button "Sync", opening in the home folder, each pick synced in the order chosen (`kubeconfig.addFile` or `kubeconfig.addFolder` through `dispatchInOrder`); Cogpit's own browser stays as the fallback, since Fyne's dialogs choose a file or a folder, never both. Upload Icon: PNG, JPEG and SVG files. The folder buttons of Cluster Settings › Terminal and Preferences › Kubernetes › Directory for binaries: folders only, "Choose". Preferences › Agent › CA file › Choose…: `.pem`, `.crt`, `.cer`. The three saves: a table's CSV (`.csv`), the Create tab's YAML (`.yaml`, `.yml`), a log tab's lines (any name), each suggesting the name it did before; the panel asks before replacing a file, the window writes it off the main goroutine, a new file owner-only |
| The bookmarks | Of every pick Cogpit reads again in a later run the panel's side makes a security-scoped bookmark while the grant is fresh: a kubeconfig source read-only, a CA file read-only, a folder read-write (kubectl's downloads are written there). They are kept in `<user config dir>/Cogpit/bookmarks.json`, owner-only (0600 in 0700, `engine.WritePrivateFile`; no keychain), by use and path ([`store.go`](../../internal/ui/nativedialog/store.go)) |
| At start | [`cmd/cogpit/fileaccess.go`](../../cmd/cogpit/fileaccess.go): before anything reads a kubeconfig source, the store is opened, a kubeconfig bookmark whose path is no longer a source dropped, the rest resolved (without UI, without mounting a volume), their items accessed for the process's life and a stale bookmark replaced by a fresh one; the log names counts, never paths |
| The prompts' words | `make app` writes `NSDesktopFolderUsageDescription`, `NSDocumentsFolderUsageDescription`, `NSDownloadsFolderUsageDescription`, `NSRemovableVolumesUsageDescription` and `NSNetworkVolumesUsageDescription` into the bundle's Info.plist ([`Makefile`](../../Makefile), `TCC_WHAT`, `TCC_TOO`): "Cogpit reads the kubeconfigs, folders and certificate files you chose in your Documents folder. Programs Cogpit starts for you, such as a terminal or a login plugin, ask through Cogpit too." |
| Tests | `TestPanelConfiguration`, `TestPanelCATypes`, `TestBookmarkHarness` (a harness in a process of its own, [`testdata/panel_harness.m`](../../internal/ui/nativedialog/testdata/panel_harness.m): the panels as built, read back without showing them; a bookmark made, resolved, started and stopped), `TestBookmarkRoundTrip` (a moved file's stale bookmark refreshed), `TestStoreRestoresRealBookmarks`, `TestStoreKeep`, `TestStoreRestore`, `TestStoreRestoreUnsupported`, `TestStoreBounds`, `TestStoreUnreadable`, `TestStoreWithoutFile` (nativedialog); `TestSyncPanelSyncsEveryPick`, `TestSyncFallsBackToCogpitsPicker`, `TestPanelShown`, `TestIconAndFolderPanels`, `TestCAFilePanel`, `TestCSVSavePanel`, `TestManifestSavePanel`, `TestLogSavePanel` (fyneui); `TestKeptSource` (cmd/cogpit) |

**What macOS documents, and what is not known** (researched 2026-10-16 night; none of it tried on
a real Mac in this run):

- **A prompt comes once per app and folder, and its answer is kept for a stable signature.** Apple
  DTS (Quinn, ["On File System Permissions"](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/678819)):
  "This system only displays this alert once … This relies on your code having a stable code
  signing identity. If your code is unsigned, or signed ad hoc …, you'll encounter excessive
  prompts." The release (Developer ID, D-48) is asked once; a build of `make app` or `make build`
  (ad hoc) is a new app after every build. The same post: the prompt and the decision belong to the
  *responsible* app, so a helper or a program it starts asks under its name.
- **A pick in the system's panel needs no prompt.** Apple's [NSOpenPanel](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsopenpanel):
  since macOS 10.15 the system draws open panels in a separate process whether or not the app is
  sandboxed, and "when the user chooses a file to open, macOS adds that file to the app's sandbox";
  WWDC 2019 (701, quoted by [Michael Tsai](https://mjtsai.com/blog/2019/12/18/persistent-file-access-via-com-apple-macl-xattr)):
  "your app gets access to the file or files that the user selected without the need for a consent
  prompt". Because the panel lists folders outside Cogpit's process, browsing it costs no prompt.
- **How that grant lasts.** Apple DTS ([forum thread 750962](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/750962)):
  the user-intent allowance rests on "security-scoped URLs, security-scoped bookmarks, an extended
  attribute in the file system … MAC works with all apps, so it uses an extended attribute to
  provide similar functionality" (`com.apple.macl`). Howard Oakley ([The MACL extended
  attribute](https://eclecticlight.co/2026/04/21/the-macl-extended-attribute/), April 2026) finds
  intent overriding the protection of Desktop, Documents and Downloads through MACL, not of iCloud
  Drive or File Provider storage, and reports that such grants are invalidated by restarting the
  Mac; others report them kept until `tccutil reset` and a restart.
- **Security-scoped bookmarks in an app without a sandbox: not documented.** Apple documents the
  option for "an app that adopts App Sandbox" ([`withSecurityScope`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsurl/bookmarkcreationoptions/withsecurityscope));
  DTS names them among the criteria above; developers disagree whether they matter outside the
  sandbox. Verified here only that Cogpit's unsandboxed process can make, resolve and start
  accessing them (`TestBookmarkHarness`, `TestBookmarkRoundTrip`). **Observed in the owner's walk
  of 2026-10-19** (v0.26.1, walk steps W41 and W42): with Cogpit's Downloads grant reset
  (`tccutil reset`), a source picked in Downloads earlier was read at the next start of Cogpit
  without a prompt and without a grant recorded afterwards. Whether the kept bookmark or the
  item's own grant from the pick (`com.apple.macl`, written at the pick) carried it is not told
  apart; a restart of the Mac was not tried. Since that walk the owner's Cogpit has no folder grant
  in TCC (his wish).

**The lead's decisions (night run 2026-10-16/17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The saves | only the open choosers (the order names "ein Bild oder ein kube_config"); every chooser | every chooser, the three saves included | A save panel is a file chooser too, and Fyne's save dialog read the same three folders when it opened: leaving the saves on Fyne kept the prompts |
| Where the native layer lives | in `fyneui` beside `titlebar_darwin.m`; a package of its own | `internal/ui/nativedialog`, without Fyne | `cmd/cogpit` resolves the bookmarks before the window exists; a package without Fyne is tested by a harness and linted alone (the macOS job's `LINT_PKGS`) |
| How a panel shows | app-modal (`runModal`); a sheet on Cogpit's window | a sheet (`beginSheetModalForWindow:`), the answer through `fyne.Do` | `runModal` holds the main thread Fyne's loop and GLFW share; a sheet keeps the window drawing and is where macOS apps ask |
| A request while a panel is up | queue it; show Fyne's dialog; drop it | drop it (`ErrBusy`) | The panel in front is the one the user answers |
| Where the system has no panel | Fyne's dialogs for all; Cogpit's browser for Sync | Fyne's dialogs, Cogpit's own browser for Sync | Fyne's dialogs choose a file or a folder, never both (why the browser exists, 2026-10-12); Windows and Linux have no TCC, their native dialogs come with M11 |
| Which picks keep a bookmark | every pick; what Cogpit reads again | kubeconfig sources and CA files read-only, folders read-write; not an icon (copied into `cluster-icons/` at once), not a saved file | A bookmark lets Cogpit open the item again: only what it needs again, with the least access |
| Bookmarks while it is unknown whether they help | build them; copy picked files into Cogpit's folder; neither | build them, say what is not known | The mechanism Apple names for a grant that outlives the process, cheap, and harmless if macOS ignores it; copies would freeze a kubeconfig or a CA bundle the user edits or rotates, and a sync folder cannot be copied |
| When a bookmark goes | look up every setting that refers to it at start; by use | a kubeconfig source's with the source (the sources' list at start); a folder's and a CA file's when 16 newer of their use came | The folders and CA files are referred to from three stores (cluster settings per context, the preferences, the agent's connections); reading all three at start for a file of a few kilobytes couples the start to each of them |
| Where they are kept | the keychain; a file in Cogpit's configuration directory | `bookmarks.json`, 0600 in 0700 | The owner's rule: no keychain; the file holds paths and bookmark data, no credential |
| An unreadable `bookmarks.json` | kept aside as `.unreadable`, as the preferences are; replaced | replaced by the next pick | A bookmark is made again by the next pick; nothing the user wrote is lost |
| A saved file's mode | as Fyne's dialog made it (0644 by the umask); owner-only | owner-only when new, an existing file keeps its mode | A table, a manifest or a log of a cluster is the user's, not every account's on the Mac |
| Where the Sync panel opens | the folder macOS remembers; the home folder | the home folder, hidden files listed | As Cogpit's own picker did: `~/.kube` one double-click away |
| Where the other panels open | the home folder; the folder macOS remembers | the folder macOS remembers | The system's default; the panel lists it outside Cogpit's process, so it costs no prompt |
| The Info.plist's usage descriptions | none; the five Files and Folders keys | the five keys, one sentence each and one about programs Cogpit starts | A prompt that still comes says why in plain words; a terminal's or a credential plugin's access is asked under Cogpit's name ([H-116](../security/file-access.md#h-116-programs-cogpit-starts-act-with-cogpits-folder-access)) |
| Several picks in Sync | one; several | several, synced in the order chosen | Lens's system dialog is titled "Sync file(s)" (captured 2026-10-12; whether it takes several is not captured); the order decides the ids ("dev.yaml (2)") |

**What only a real window shows (walk steps for the owner, in the release, not a `make app`
build):**

1. Cluster › Sync Files and Folders…: a sheet slides out of the window's top, its line "Select
   kubeconfig files or folders of kubeconfigs and press Sync. …", the button "Sync", in the home
   folder with `.kube` listed dimmed. ⌘-click two files, Sync: both are synced, a toast each. With
   nothing selected, Sync should take the folder shown (AppKit's behaviour, not tried); ⌘⇧G types a
   path.
2. In that panel, open Downloads and Documents in its sidebar: no "Cogpit would like to access files
   in your … folder".
3. Sync a kubeconfig from `~/Downloads` and connect to one of its clusters: no prompt.
4. Quit Cogpit and start it again: the source in Downloads is read at start. No prompt is the hoped
   result; a prompt that comes names the reason ("Cogpit reads the kubeconfigs, folders and
   certificate files you chose in your Downloads folder. …"): that answers the open question above.
5. Restart the Mac and start Cogpit: the same check.
6. Cluster Settings › General › Icon › Upload Icon…: only PNG, JPEG and SVG files can be chosen,
   the button "Upload".
7. Cluster Settings › Terminal and Preferences › Kubernetes › Directory for binaries, the folder
   buttons: only folders, the button "Choose".
8. Preferences › Agent, a connection's CA file, Choose…: only `.pem`, `.crt` and `.cer` files.
9. A table's download, the Create tab's save, a log tab's download: a save sheet with the name
   proposed; an existing file asks before it is replaced; `ls -l` shows a new file as `-rw-------`.
10. After each panel closes, typing goes to Cogpit's window again (the search field, an editor).

**Open:** whether the bookmarks keep macOS quiet
after a restart (walk steps 4 and 5); the native dialogs of Windows and Linux (M11).

## D-73: A login that waits: Cancel Connecting and a bound

**The owner's finding (2026-10-16 night, verbatim):** "ich wollte mich zu [einem Cluster]
verbinden, aber habe den OIDC Login verkackt, jetzt blinkt [er] die ganze Zeit und ich habe keine
Möglichkeit den Prozess von vorne zu beginnen. Es gibt keinen Timeout seit 10min." The context
logs in with an interactive OIDC credential plugin. The lead read his running v0.19.0 over MCP:
`ui_state` said `connecting` without anything else; `cluster_connectLog` showed one attempt
running for ~19 minutes whose last step was "Login: credential plugin … interactive mode
IfAvailable"; the plugin's process, a child of Cogpit's, had run as long, waiting for its browser
callback; an agent's `cluster_disconnect` got no answer within 15 s and the state stayed
`connecting`; only after the lead ended the plugin's process did the connect fail and the queued
Disconnect run.

**Why, read in the code (client-go v0.37.1, `plugin/pkg/client/auth/exec/exec.go`):** the exec
authenticator runs the plugin with `exec.Command` and `cmd.Run()` (458–472), without a context,
under the Authenticator's lock, and every request that needs the credential waits for that lock
whatever its own context says (`getCreds`, 402–415). So the connect's 15 s timeout and its cancel
had no effect while the plugin ran, and `Session.DisconnectContext` waited for the connect's
`connMu`. Found on the way: the connect's timeout applied to the whole first request, the plugin's
run included, so a browser login that took longer than 15 s failed the connect after it had worked
("no answer from the API server … within 15s"; `TestConnectTimeoutDoesNotCountTheLogin`).

**Built 2026-10-16 night** (the lead's design in the run's brief, built by its agent E):

- **The cluster layer** ([`cluster/loginrun.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginrun.go),
  [`pluginproc.go`](../../internal/cluster/pluginproc.go), [`pluginproc_*.go`](../../internal/cluster/pluginproc_darwin.go)):
  the wrapper of the Authenticator's `interactiveFunc` that D-69's hold set ([`loginhold.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginhold.go))
  also notes each run's begin; a goroutine that takes the Authenticator's lock after it notes the
  run's end. A run that has not ended after its bound (`Options.LoginTimeout`, 5 minutes), or that
  the user cancels (`Connect`'s context, `Conn.CancelLogin`, `Conn.Close`), is ended: Cogpit
  signals the plugin's process, SIGTERM and SIGKILL after 3 s if the run has not ended and the same
  process still runs. Since 2026-10-19 (WF38, below) the process is the child of Cogpit's that
  appeared at the run's begin, followed by its number and start time (before: the child whose
  command line was the plugin's at the cancel, which missed a wrapper that `exec`s; a plugin the
  kubeconfig names by its path is matched under that path only, since 2026-10-16 night); one not
  found is not ended, and the error and the log say so (`LoginEndedError.RunsOn`). Once Cogpit
  ended a run, no run of that plugin configuration starts until the user connects again or logs in
  again (`ArmLogin`); a request that needed one ends as a `*LoginEndedError`. Since 2026-10-19 a run
  starts only while an open connection the user did not cancel asks for one (`admit`). A
  `LoginWatch` tells the engine when a run begins and ends. The connect's first request is bounded
  below the plugin (`withRequestBound`), so its timeout no longer counts the login.
- **The engine** ([`engine/loginwait.go`](../../internal/engine/loginwait.go)):
  `Connection.waitingForLogin` (`program`, `since`, `until`) while a run is under way, wherever the

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |

| The command | a new `cluster.cancelConnect {context?}`; `cluster.disconnect` extended | `cluster.disconnect` extended: it already ended "a connect under way", now at once and with its plugin, a background connect too; the window labels it **Cancel Connecting** while the cluster connects | The same effect for every origin without a second tool that agents must tell apart; the command count stays. UI danger: it stops only what the user's own connect started (D-2) |
| How the plugin's process is ended | Cogpit runs the plugin itself (client-go's exec authenticator re-done; rejected in D-58: certificate plugins need client-go's TLS callback, D-26's binding); a wrapper program in the plugin's place (changes the command D-26 approved; rejected in D-66); abandon the waiting request only (the plugin runs on and keeps client-go's lock: the next connect of the context waits behind it); find the process among Cogpit's children by its command line, noted where client-go starts it, and signal it | find and signal it (how it is found changed with WF38, 2026-10-19: below) | client-go offers no context, no `*exec.Cmd` and no `SysProcAttr`; the run's begin is seen where D-69's hold already sits. macOS through `proc_info` and `kern.procargs2`, Linux through `/proc`, both without cgo (`cogpit-cli` is pure Go) and without a direct `golang.org/x/sys` dependency; Windows by the program's file name (its command line is not readable without another process's memory), not tried on Windows |

| The connect's 15 s timeout | the whole first request, the login included (as built); the request below the plugin | below the plugin | Its purpose is a server that does not answer; the login has its own bound now. Before, a browser login longer than 15 s failed the connect after it had worked |

| Log in again while an earlier automatic run still waits | join it (D-58 as built); end it and start a new one | join it, as built; Cogpit ends it at its bound, and Disconnect then Connect starts over at once | D-58's confirmed behaviour; ending a run the user may be finishing in the browser is the owner's call. **For the owner:** should Log in again start over? |
| The plugin's standard error of an ended run | kept as after a failed login; dropped | kept after the bound (a failed login: scrubbed, 4 KiB, D-66; it may say what it waited for); dropped after a cancel (the user's action) | |

**WF38 (the lead's walk W44, 2026-10-19), built the same day.** The walk's plugin was a wrapper
script doing `exec /bin/sleep 900`. After Cancel Connecting its process ran on, while the
connection log said "Login cancelled: Cogpit ended walk-login.sh": the cancel looked the process up
by the kubeconfig's command line, which the `exec` had replaced, and the error had been told before
the lookup. Two more connects, each cancelled after 2–3 s, had queued their first request behind
that run (client-go's `getCreds` waits for the Authenticator's lock without the request's
context); each later started a new `/bin/sleep 900` when the run before it ended, with no connect
waiting. A connect's registration had cleared the stop that the first cancel set, and its own
cancel set none, since the run was already being ended. Built in the cluster layer
([`pluginproc.go`](../../internal/cluster/pluginproc.go), [`loginrun.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginrun.go),
[`loginhold.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginhold.go)); H-118 narrowed; tests above. The engine
reads the same `*LoginEndedError`: its texts follow from it.

**H-118's residual (2026-10-20), built the same day.** After WF38 a connection that waited
behind a run Cogpit had stopped waiting for and could not end (the plugin gone, a child of it
holding its output, so client-go's run and its lock go on) still promised what no longer happens,
or said nothing. A connect that registered behind such a run was not told of it at all: a
`LoginWatch` heard of runs that began or ended while its connection was registered, so the
workspace said "Connecting to …" and nothing else, and the log had no line
(`TestAConnectBehindARunCogpitCouldNotEndHasNoEnd` failed so against the code before). A
connection that already showed a run kept "Cogpit ends it at 14:33" after 14:33 when the bound had
not found the run's process (`TestARunPastItsBoundThatCogpitCouldNotEndHasNoEnd`). The plan's note
said the later connect "still says Cogpit ends it at …"; read in a test, it said nothing, and the
passed end time showed where the run was already shown. Built in the cluster layer
([`loginrun.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginrun.go): `LoginRun.RunsOn`, `pluginHold.current`,
`configureRuns`, `end`), the engine ([`loginwait.go`](../../internal/engine/loginwait.go):
`LoginWait.RunsOn`, `waitingReason`, `loginNotes.log`) and the window
([`loginwait.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/loginwait.go), [`tableview.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/tableview.go)
`updateConnecting`, [`conndot.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/conndot.go)); H-118's bullet says
what is true now. Read in the code and tested: the connect's own wait behind such a run has no
bound (the 5 minutes act on a run Cogpit can still end, and the engine's connect has no deadline);
it lasts until that process ends, or until Cancel Connecting, which leaves the run alone and
returns within half a second (`cancelSettle`).

**The lead's decisions for WF38 (2026-10-19, by the agent who built it) and for H-118's residual
(2026-10-20), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
