"Cogpit ended <program>" only then; otherwise "Cogpit stopped waiting for <program>; its process was not found and may run on" (or "could not be signalled"), `LoginEndedError.RunsOn` for the engine; the timeout's "Connect starts it again" is left out then | The log said Cogpit had ended a process that ran on (W44). Telling before signalling keeps a request that the plugin's end fails counted as an ended login (the count `loginEndedSince` reads), as before |
| A request that queued behind a run for a connect the user cancelled | client-go's behaviour (it starts the plugin when it gets the lock: one run per cancelled connect, nobody waiting); follow each request's context into the run (client-go's `getCreds` does not pass it, and `interactiveFunc` has none); the hold refuses a run while no open connection asks for one | the hold: `admit` starts a run only while an open connection that neither holds its login nor was cancelled uses the plugin. `CancelLogin` (a cancelled connect, `Close`, Disconnect) withdraws its connection until `ArmLogin` (Log in again) or a new connect; `Close` drops it. A refused request fails with `errLoginNotAsked` and an INFO line in the app log naming the program | The gate already sits where client-go asks before every run (D-69's hold). A request that queued behind a run while another connection asks may start one, and the run then serves that connection: its watch shows it, its cancel ends it (`TestCancelledConnectsStartNoRunAfterAStrayOne`) |
| How the run's process is found | by its command line at the cancel (as built; misses a wrapper that `exec`s); a marker of the run in the plugin's environment, found in the process's (changes the environment D-26 approved; macOS 26 leaves the environment out of `kern.procargs2` for a caller that is not root, tried 2026-10-19); the plugin's standard error as a pipe of Cogpit's own per run, found by the pipe the process holds (redoes D-66's capture; it would find the plugin's children too); Cogpit's children noted at the run's begin, the new one taken | the new one: noted at the begin (inside the `interactiveFunc` wrapper, before client-go forks), the one new child seen running the plugin's command line, else the one new child in Cogpit's process group when no other plugin run was under way alongside; followed by its number and start time (`proc_info` `PROC_PIDTBSDINFO` on macOS, `/proc/<pid>/stat` on Linux, `GetProcessTimes` on Windows); a run not found then falls back to a new child running the command line | Small and local to the cluster layer; the number and the start time survive the `exec` (checked on macOS 26); a terminal's shell runs in a session of its own and a run that begins alongside another disables the group rule instead of guessing. The pipe stays the option for H-118's children |
| How long the search looks | 100 ms; 500 ms; until the cancel | 500 ms after the run's begin, every 1 ms for the first 50 ms (to see a wrapper's own command line before its `exec`), then every 10 ms | client-go starts the process microseconds after it asked; a race-enabled test binary on a loaded runner needs margin; a cancel within the window waits for the rest of it |
| What a connection says that waits behind a run Cogpit stopped waiting for and could not end (2026-10-20) | as built: a run already shown kept "Cogpit ends it at <the passed bound>", a connect that registered behind it said nothing; drop the end time only; say what it waits behind, that Cogpit stopped waiting for it and could not end it, that it has no end time, and what Cancel Connecting does then | the last. The workspace: "Waiting behind the login through <program>, running since 14:28, which Cogpit stopped waiting for and could not end." and below it "It has no end time: it lasts until its process ends. Cancel Connecting stops this wait; that login goes on."; the dot's tooltip the same in one paragraph, "Cancel Connecting in its menu stops this wait; …" only while connecting; the reason "waiting behind the login through <program>, which Cogpit stopped waiting for and could not end; it has no end time"; the connection log "Login: waiting behind the login through <program>, running since 14:28, which Cogpit stopped waiting for and could not end; it has no end time and lasts until its process ends", while connecting with "; Cancel Connecting stops this wait, that login goes on" | Without the end time alone a connect waits for no reason it can see, and the usual "Cancel Connecting … ends it now" would be false: the cancel stops the connect's wait, the run and its process stay. "Behind" is true for both cases, a later connect and a connect's own run past its bound: the connection's requests queue behind the run; the clock of its begin shows a later connect that the run is older than it. ## D-74: How the lead's decisions are reviewed

**Decided (owner, 2026-10-17): option (a).** The question, asked once after the night run of
2026-10-16/17: how the details the lead decides are reviewed from now on. The owner had said the
evening before: "Ich kann nicht so viel kleine Details beantworten. Manches muss auch die Zeit und
Feedback anderer abwarten." About 125 table rows and as many sentences then said "for the owner to
confirm" (D-55, D-58 to D-70, the night decisions of 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-16), and two audit
rounds of about 100 details each had run on 2026-10-16.

| Option | What it means | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) The lead decides details, open to revision (chosen)** | Each detail is recorded where it lives with the question, the options, the choice and why, as the lead's decision; no confirmation queue. The owner gets decisions of product direction, scope, security posture and anything irreversible or outward-facing, one question at a time; what the window shows he judges in walks ("stört mich" changes it, the rest stands); the rest waits for use and others' feedback (G16). | A detail he would have chosen otherwise stays until a walk or a user finds it; details are cheap to change. |
| (b) As before: every detail "for the owner to confirm", audits on request | The queue grows by 50 to 100 a day of night runs. | His time, which he said he does not have for this. |
| (c) A short list: "to confirm" only for details with a high cost of reversal or a visible effect, at most about five a week | The lead picks the list. | A little of his time every week. |
| (d) Walks only, nothing listed | Invisible details are never reviewed unless something goes wrong. | Security-relevant defaults lose their review path. |

**Built 2026-10-17:** every "for the owner to confirm" outside the change logs reads "open to
revision" (the change logs and the pages' "Change:" lines keep what was written then); the rule in
this page's introduction, in [conventions › Decisions](conventions.md#decisions) and in AGENTS.md's
rules. "Undocumented" is not a state a decision may have (the owner, the same message: "Bitte
dokumentiere undokumentiertes"): a choice that only a report, a chat or a commit message names is
written into the page where it lives.

## D-75: A client certificate's validity in the cluster lists

**The owner's finding F22 (2026-10-17, verbatim):** "Wenn es sich um ein Standard Kubernetes
Zertifikat in der kube_config handelt, können wir doch die Laufzeit ermitteln oder? Ich möchte dass
im Cluster picker bei solchen kube_configs die verbleibende Laufzeit steht oder expired, ein
Verbindungsaufbau soll dadurch nicht blockiert werden, auch wenn er fehlschlagen wird."

**Built 2026-10-17** (the lead's brief, built by its agent G): for a context whose user logs in with
a client certificate (`client-certificate-data`, or a `client-certificate` file), Cogpit reads the
certificate's NotBefore and NotAfter and shows the time left, or "expired" (since 2026-10-17 without since when, the owner), where
the user chooses a cluster. Lens's cluster list shows no certificate: this is Cogpit's own
([beyond Lens › Everyday use](../parity/beyond-lens.md#everyday-use)).

- **The data** ([`kubeconfig/clientcert.go`](../../internal/kubeconfig/clientcert.go),
  [`cluster/clientcert.go`](../../internal/cluster/clientcert.go)): `kubeconfig.Context.ClientCert`
  and `engine.ContextInfo.ClientCert`, `{notBefore, notAfter, state}`, the state set when
  `cluster.contexts` lists (`valid`, `expiring`, `expired`, `notYetValid`); `cogpit-cli contexts`'
  last column CLIENT CERT ("expires in 23 days").
- **The window** ([`fyneui/clientcert.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clientcert.go)): the navigator's
  section, the one list that chooses a cluster (D-57, ⌘P), a second line under the name, "cert
  expires in 23 days" or "expired" alone (the owner, 2026-10-17); the welcome page's row a pill, "client
  certificate expires in 23 days"; the section row's and the hotbar tile's tooltips a line with the
  date in the user's format, "Client certificate expires in 23 days (valid until 09.11.2026
  14:03)". Muted while valid, the warning colour while expiring or not valid yet, the error colour
  once expired.
- **Never in the way:** no dialog, no question, no warning before a connect, and no refusal; a
  click on an expired context's row connects as any other
  (`TestAnExpiredClientCertificateDoesNotHoldTheConnect`, `TestProtectedClientCertificateIsReadAtConnect`,
  `TestContextsCarryTheClientCertificate`: the connect reaches the server).
- **Tests:** `TestClientCertificateDates` (a certificate valid for 23 more days and one expired 3
  days ago, a real, a garbage and no key: the same dates; the context's JSON holds neither the
  certificate nor the key), `TestUnreadableClientCertificate`, `TestClientCertificateIsTheLeaf`,
  `TestClientCertificateState` (kubeconfig); `TestClientCertificateFileIsRead`,
  `TestProtectedClientCertificateIsReadAtConnect`, `TestProtectedPlaces`,
  `TestUnreadableClientCertificateFile`, `TestListingNeverOpensTheKey` (the key a FIFO: listing
  would block if it opened it) (cluster); `TestContextsCarryTheClientCertificate` (engine, the JSON
  agents read, a real connect of the expired context against the fake API server);
  `TestContextsShowTheClientCertificate` (cogpit-cli); `TestClusterListsShowTheClientCertificate`,
  `TestClientCertificateLinesFollowTheClock`, `TestAnExpiredClientCertificateDoesNotHoldTheConnect`
  and the PNGs of the section
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_client_certs_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_client_certs_light.png)) and the welcome page
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/welcome_client_certs_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/welcome_client_certs_light.png)) (window).
- **Checked on kind** (2026-10-17): the kind cluster's kubeconfig, its context `kind-cogpit`; Cogpit
  read notBefore 2026-10-11T10:47:10Z and notAfter 2027-10-11T10:52:10Z, `openssl x509 -startdate
  -enddate` of the same certificate the same dates.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where it shows | the navigator's section only; also the welcome page, the hotbar and the palette | the section, the welcome page's rows, the hotbar tile's tooltip, and agents and `cogpit-cli contexts` | Since D-57 the section is "the cluster picker" (⌘P shows it); the welcome page's rows and the hotbar's tiles are the other ways to choose a cluster. The palette lists no clusters of its own since D-57. A tile has only room for its dot, which shows the connection: the date goes into its tooltip |
| How the section's row shows it | a short suffix at the row's right ("23d"); a second line under the name; the tooltip only | a second line in the caption size, as the section's root row has one | The owner wants it to stand there ("steht"), so not the tooltip alone; the sidebar is 216 px wide and the name would lose the width a suffix takes. A row with a certificate is as tall as the section's root row, 45 px against 36 |
| The wording | Lens's age style ("23d", "5h"); words | words: "cert expires in 23 days", "5 h", "12 min", "less than a minute", from two years on "3 years"; "expired" alone in the window (the owner, 2026-10-17; the CLI and agents keep "expired 3 days ago"); "cert not valid yet" | Reads as a sentence; days up to two years as kubectl's age steps. "cert", not "client certificate", in the section: the full words (177 px in the caption size) do not fit beside the badge; the tooltip and the welcome page's pill, where "certificate not checked" (the server's certificate) may stand beside it, say "client certificate" |
| When it is "expiring" (the warning colour) | a fixed 14 or 30 days; a share of the lifetime; both | within 14 days, or within the last fifth of the certificate's lifetime when that is shorter | A certificate issued for hours (logins that hand out short-lived certificates) would be in the warning colour all its life with a fixed window; kind's and kubeadm's year-long certificates turn in their last 14 days, a 12-hour certificate in its last 2 h 24 min |
| Colours | one colour; per state | the status tokens: muted while valid, warning while expiring or not yet valid, error once expired | The theme's tokens (rule 6); the text says which state, so the near orange and red of Solarized need not carry it alone |
| What is read and kept | the certificate (subject, issuer, dates); the dates only | NotBefore and NotAfter of the leaf, the first CERTIFICATE block, as crypto/tls presents it; never the PEM, the subject or the key (`client-key-data` and `client-key` are never looked at) | The least the feature needs. The user's name comes from the API server since D-68. An intermediate in a chain that expires before the leaf is not looked at: Kubernetes signs client certificates directly, a chain in a kubeconfig is rare |
| Which contexts | every user entry with a certificate; not those whose credential comes from a program | a certificate in the user entry, with or without a token, but not for a user with a credential plugin (`exec`) or an auth provider: nothing shown | What such a program hands out, a certificate included, is not known before it runs; the owner asked for "Standard Kubernetes Zertifikat" in the kubeconfig |
| A `client-certificate` file and macOS's privacy prompts (D-72, [file access](../security/file-access.md)) | read it whenever the contexts are listed; only at connect and remember the dates; only beside the kubeconfig; at listing unless macOS protects its place, else after a connect | at listing unless it lies in a place macOS protects, or a link on the way leads into one; there right after client-go read it to connect, remembered for the run | Listing must not raise a prompt the user did not ask for. minikube's `~/.minikube` and a hand-made `~/certs` show before any connect; a file in Documents shows from its first connect on, where client-go reads it anyway (its prompt, if any, is client-go's). Remembered in memory only: a file of Cogpit's for the dates of a rare case would need its own place in the docs and the security pages. A certificate in such a place renewed on disk shows its new date at the next connect. What the list of places misses: [H-119](../security/file-access.md#h-119-a-client-certificate-file-is-read-while-the-contexts-are-listed) |
| A certificate that cannot be read | an error in the list; nothing | nothing shown, logged once at debug level (per context, file and problem; fixed texts that quote nothing) | It must not stand in the user's way, as the owner said of the connect |
| The time moving on | a timer per row; only at each listing; the shell's existing tick | the shell's ten-second tick (`shell.tick`, which re-renders the tables' ages) computes the texts again from the dates and refreshes only rows whose line changed | A day boundary passes without a listing; no file is read and no cluster is asked for it (`TestClientCertificateLinesFollowTheClock`) |
| Agents | the state in `ui_state`; the dates in `cluster.contexts` | `cluster.contexts`' `clientCert` with the state at the listing, the threshold the window's | The contexts are not part of `ui_state`; agents list them with `cluster_contexts` (rule 1: what the window shows, agents read) |
| A connect of an expired certificate in the connection log | a line of its own naming the expiry; the Login line, which names the dates already (D-66: "client certificate CN=…, valid until … (expired 3 days ago)"), as a warning; what the server answers only | the Login line as a warning (WARN) while the certificate is expired or not valid yet, beside the server's answer (the lead's decision of 2026-10-17, open to revision; `TestAnExpiredClientCertificateWarnsInTheLog`) | A second line would repeat the dates the Login line holds; the warning colour points at the likely cause of the 401 without holding the connect |

**Not verified:** whether `lstat` of a path inside a protected folder raises a prompt at all (the
walk avoids it either way); the lines in a real window and a real cluster whose certificate is
short-lived. The walk steps are in the run's report.

## D-76: Integrations per cluster, and the question at a new cluster's first connect

**Changed 2026-10-17 evening by [D-82](#d-82-a-pre-choice-before-any-integration-is-looked-for-and-ask-again)** (the owner's WF5 and WF4): the question opens on a pre-choice, and in the window's session nothing of a cluster without a choice is looked for or read until it is answered, also after Later; so "until it is answered the default applies", the detection at once when the question shows, and Later's "meanwhile the default applies" below no longer hold. The default for new clusters is what the pre-choice's Check all looks for (and what the CLI's session and the demo cluster read); the rows' switches are engine state (`integrationsLookFor`) and a tick looks for that integration at once, where below they were the dialog's own until Apply; a change of an undecided cluster's switches starts from what applies now (none), not the default; Cluster Settings › Integrations has Ask again. The rest stands.

**Changed 2026-10-19 by the owner's decision on [H-126](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-126-an-agent-can-answer-the-integrations-question-for-the-user)**
(2026-10-19 afternoon: "Nein"; built the same day, [D-2](#d-2-agent-interface-scope)): agents
neither answer the question nor switch an integration on, so "agents switch both ways" and "Whether
agents answer the question: agents too" in the table below no longer hold. `cluster.integrations.step`,
`.lookFor` and `.answer` are GUI-only; `cluster.settings.set`'s `integrations` naming one `true`,
its `metricsSource` other than `none`, and `preferences.set`'s `integrationDefaults` naming one
`true` are refused to external agents, the built-in agent and the CLI (`ErrIntegrationsGUIOnly`,
[`engine/integrationsguionly.go`](../../internal/engine/integrationsguionly.go); the fields' and the
commands' descriptions say so, the three question commands "GUI only" in the MCP tool list, and the
built-in agent is not offered them). Tests: `TestIntegrationsOnAreTheUsers` (the three refused as
GUI-only and every switch of a cluster the window still asks about, with and without agent writes,
the question untouched; on a decided cluster on by name, by a source and as a default refused, a
mixed change refused as a whole, off by name, the source `none` and a default off accepted; nobody
asked; the tools' descriptions), `TestGUIOnlyCommandsRefuseOtherOrigins`; the existing tests turned:
`TestIntegrationsQuestionLifecycle`, `TestIntegrationsConsentCommands` and
`TestIntegrationSwitchCommands` step, tick, answer and switch on as the window. **The lead's
decisions (2026-10-19), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whether agents may still switch an integration off | refused as on is; allowed | allowed: `integrations` `false`, `metricsSource` `none`, `integrationDefaults` `false` | Off only stops reads, so it narrows what Cogpit does on the cluster with the user's identity; it is the direction of "agents may only turn it off" of D-69's two session settings. What it leaves with agents (an alert source switched off while the user works) is named in H-126 |
| An agent's off-switch on a cluster the window still asks about (no choice of its own, the window's session, not the demo cluster) | allowed, starting from what applies now; allowed, starting from everything off; refused | refused (`Session.RefuseIntegrationSwitches`) | Either allowed form ends the question: from what applies now the user's ticks so far become the cluster's choice (reads the user only looked for are kept), from everything off the cluster is decided "without integrations" and never asked again. Both answer the question, which the owner refused; nothing is read there anyway but what the user ticked |
| What counts as switching on | a switch that turns on what is off now; any `true` | any `true`, and any `metricsSource` that names a provider (`auto`, `prometheus`, `metrics-server`), whatever is on now | Stateless: the same call is refused or not whatever the cluster's state, and the rule is one line in the tool's description ("may only switch integrations off"); an agent that wants Prometheus alone off names `prometheus: false` |
| A change that switches one on and another off | split, applying the off; refused as a whole | refused as a whole, before anything is written | One call, one outcome; a half-applied change would read as accepted |
| The default for new clusters (`integrationDefaults`) | open both ways (it switches no cluster on in the window's session); off only | off only | It is what the user's Check all looks for at once; an agent turning a default back on would make the user's next click look for what the user had turned off. Off narrows it |
| Later and Ask again | GUI-only with the rest of the question; open to agents | open to agents | Later puts the question off and reads nothing meanwhile; Ask again forgets a choice and reads nothing until the user answers: both make Cogpit read less, never more, and neither answers for the user |
| The refusal's form | `AgentsAsk` (the user accepts in a dialog, the lead's proposal before the decision); refused | refused, GUI-only for the three commands, a field refusal in `cluster.settings.set` and `preferences.set` | The owner's "Nein" is a refusal, not a question; the field refusals follow the proxy's and the login renewal's in the same command |
| One error or several | one per command or field; one | one, `ErrIntegrationsGUIOnly`: "only the user, in Cogpit's own window, can switch a cluster's integrations on or answer the question about a new cluster's integrations …; agents and the CLI may switch integrations off on a cluster the user has chosen them for" | One rule, one reason an agent can act on: it says what the agent may still do |

**Changed 2026-10-18 by [D-87](#d-87-cluster-settings-the-integrations-under-a-divider-a-section-each-metrics-their-consumer)** (the owner's WF22): the integrations stand under a divider below Agents, the heading Integrations a section of its own (the rows, the note, Ask again) and each integration a section with its switch, its state and its details; Prometheus's fields moved there from Metrics, Alertmanager's address from under its row; Metrics names the two metrics integrations with their states, and Lens's "Metrics source" dropdown left the page (`metricsSource` stays for agents). So "Integrations stands right before Metrics", the Metrics section's dropdown and "a manual Prometheus links to Cluster Settings › Metrics" below no longer hold. The rest stands.

**The owner's words (2026-10-17, verbatim, the part this decision answers):** "Pass auf, ich will
in der Cluster Settings eine Section bei der ich einstellen und anklicken kann, welche
Integrationen ich für den jeweiligen Cluster wünsche. Wenn man einen Cluster neu hinzufügt für den
noch keine Einstellung getroffen wurde, soll der Nutzer gefragt werden, welche Integrationen er
aktivieren möchte, in der Anzeige muss direkt ersichtlich sein, ob wir das jeweilige Tool schon
automatisch gefunden haben, oder ob es eine Manuelle Konfiguration für die Integration erfordert.
Der Nutzer muss auch einen haken haben, der diese aktuellen Settings als default für zukünftige
Abfragen anderer Server speichern soll. Unser Default ist alles an. Aktuell haben wir also schon:
metrics-Server, prometheus." The ticket's requirements I1 (a section per cluster, each integration
switched, found automatically or needing a manual configuration at once), I2 (asked on a new
cluster, the same status, the checkbox for the default) and I3 (default: everything on). The rest of
his message, Alertmanager, Trivy and Kyverno, is D-77 to D-79; each fills its integration's probe and
reads against this decision's switch. Lens has no integrations section: everything here is
Cogpit's own ([beyond Lens › Cluster integrations](../parity/beyond-lens.md#cluster-integrations)).

**Built 2026-10-17** (the lead's foundation, then the settings, the question and the docs by its
agent):

- **The switch** ([`engine/integrations.go`](../../internal/engine/integrations.go)): five
  integrations, `metrics-server`, `prometheus`, `alertmanager`, `trivy`, `kyverno`, in that order.
  A cluster's choice is `ClusterSettings.IntegrationsOff`, the integrations switched off
  (`integrationsOff` in `cluster-settings.json`, a list of names), absent while the user made no
  choice for it; the default for new clusters is `Preferences.IntegrationsOff` (`integrationsOff`
  in `preferences.json`, absent: every one on). `UIState.IntegrationOn(context, name)` is the one
  switch every integration reads, and `UIState.IntegrationsDecided(context)` whether the cluster has
  a choice of its own. An integration switched off sends nothing to the cluster and shows nothing:
  no column, no drawer section, no pill, nothing in `ui_state` (as hidden metrics).
- **The Metrics source moved into the two metrics switches:** `metricsSource` of an older
  `cluster-settings.json` is read once and becomes the cluster's choice: `prometheus` switches the
  Metrics Server off, `metrics-server` Prometheus, `none` both; Automatic (no value) stays no
  choice. Cluster Settings › Metrics keeps Lens's "Metrics source" dropdown, which shows and sets
  the same two switches (both on is Automatic, one on that provider alone, both off No metrics), and
  so does `cluster.settings.set`'s `metricsSource` (`TestIntegrationSettings`,
  `TestMetricsSourceFromTheSettings`).
- **Probes and followers, the contract for each integration's file:** a probe
  (`integrationProbes[name]`) says what Cogpit knows of the integration on a connected cluster from
  what its own reads, the cache and API discovery hold, sending no request: found (and where),
  configured (an address the user set answers), manual (none found by name: its address is to be
  set), missing (not in the cluster), forbidden, unavailable, checking, off. A follower
  (`integrationFollowers`) starts and stops the integration's reads on every UI state change while
  the engine reconciles, without blocking. `Session.IntegrationStatuses` and
  `cluster.settings.get`'s `integrations` show them; `EventIntegrations` tells the window and agents
  that what Cogpit knows changed.
- **Cluster Settings › Integrations** ([`fyneui/clustersettings_integrations.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clustersettings_integrations.go)):
  a row per integration: its switch with its label, a status line in the status colours ("Found
  automatically: monitoring/kube-prometheus-alertmanager:9093", "Needs manual configuration: none
  found by name", "Not in this cluster: …", "No permission: …", "Not answering: …", "Checking…",
  "Off: nothing is asked of the cluster", "Not connected: found when the cluster is connected"), and
  the line of what it adds; a manual Prometheus links to Cluster Settings › Metrics, where its
  address is set ("Set its address…"); a note while the cluster has no choice of its own. A switch
  dispatches `cluster.settings.set`'s `integrations` at once; the status follows `EventIntegrations`
  and `EventMetrics`. An integration's own file puts its controls under its row through
  `integrationRowExtras` (Alertmanager's address fields, D-77).
- **The question** ([`engine/integrationsask.go`](../../internal/engine/integrationsask.go),
  [`fyneui/integrationsask.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/integrationsask.go)): while the shown
  cluster is connected and has no choice of its own, `ui_state`'s `integrationsQuestion` names it and
  the window shows a dialog "Integrations for <name>" over the workspace, the views loading behind
  it: the same rows, prefilled with what applies now (the default for new clusters), their statuses
  live, the checkbox "Save as the default for new clusters" (off until ticked), Later and Apply.
  Apply is `cluster.integrations.answer` ({context, integrations, saveAsDefault}), Later
  `cluster.integrations.later`; the dialog closes when the engine drops the question, whoever
  answered it. Until it is answered the default applies; nothing waits for it, an agent's connect
  included.
- **Detection when shown:** while the question or the cluster's Settings › Integrations shows a
  connected cluster, the metrics providers nothing looked for yet are detected once
  (`metrics.Hub.DetectUnknown`, started by the follower `detectShownIntegrations`), so that both
  say "found" right after the connect where before Prometheus was looked for only when a drawer
  opened or the Metrics Server failed. Bounded as detection is ([D-71](#d-71-thanos-and-victoriametrics-read-as-prometheus)):
  the Metrics Server one discovery request, Prometheus the cached Services and at most 3 probes,
  each within the request timeout; a detection the timeout cut short is not tried again before the
  retry TTL (2 minutes); never polled.
- **Preferences › Kubernetes › Integrations of new clusters**
  ([`fyneui/preferences_integrations.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/preferences_integrations.go)):
  the default as five switches, besides the question's checkbox that sets it.
- **Commands:** `cluster.settings.set`'s `integrations` (`{"alertmanager": false}`; an unknown name
  refused with the known ones; not together with a `metricsSource` naming the same providers),
  `preferences.set`'s `integrationDefaults` (the same form), `cluster.integrations.answer`,
  `cluster.integrations.later` (both UI commands; the answer GUI-only and switching one on refused
  to agents since 2026-10-19, the note above); `cluster.settings.get` returns `integrations`
  (name, label, on, state, where, detail, adds) and `integrationsDecided`.
- **Tests:** `TestIntegrationSettings`, `TestIntegrationStatusesNotConnected`,
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionSync`, `TestIntegrationsShownDetectOnce` (engine);
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionLifecycle` (asked at a new cluster's first connect; Later for the run, a
  reconnect included, asked again at the next start; an answer with and without `saveAsDefault`; the
  next new cluster starting from the saved default; a decided cluster not asked),
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionNotAsked` (the demo cluster, a session without cluster settings),
  `TestIntegrationSwitchCommands` (commands); `TestDetectUnknownOnce`,
  `TestDetectUnknownTimeoutWaitsForTheRetry` (metrics); `TestIntegrationsSection`,
  `TestIntegrationRowExtras`, `TestIntegrationsSectionOnTheDemo`, `TestIntegrationsQuestionApply`,
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionLaterAndAgent`, `TestNewClusterIntegrationsPreference` and the PNGs of the
  section ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/cluster_settings_integrations_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/cluster_settings_integrations_light.png)) and the
  question ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_light.png)), a cluster whose
  integrations are found, manual, missing, forbidden and checking (window).
- **Checked on kind** (2026-10-17, `TestKindIntegrationsQuestion`): the kind cluster `cogpit` with
  its Metrics Server and the Prometheus `make kind-prometheus` installs, new to a Cogpit whose
  settings lived in a temporary folder: the first connect asked; the Metrics Server and
  `monitoring/prometheus-server:http` were found 0.21 s after the connect, with no drawer and no list
  showing metrics; the answer ended the question.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| How a choice is kept | an on-list; an off-list with "absent" for no choice; a block of booleans per integration | the off-list, absent while the user chose nothing (the lead's foundation) | "No choice yet", which the question needs, differs from "all on"; an integration a later Cogpit adds is on for the clusters decided before it, which is the owner's "alles an"; one name a later Cogpit wrote is dropped, not the others |
| The Metrics source kept before | keep both fields; move it into the switches once | moved: `prometheus`, `metrics-server` and `none` become the cluster's choice; Automatic stays no choice | One truth: the dropdown and the two switches cannot disagree. A source the user chose is a choice the question need not ask again; Automatic was nobody's choice |
| Whether agents switch integrations, and which way | off only (as the renewal of a login and the restore of the last session, D-69 stage 3); both ways, as UI commands; a write with confirmation | both ways, UI commands (`cluster.settings.set`, `preferences.set`, the question's commands); **replaced 2026-10-19 by the owner's decision on H-126: off only, on a cluster the user chose for (the note above)** | A switch only changes what Cogpit reads, with the user's identity, from what the cluster runs, and never writes; reads run freely for agents (D-2), and agents could already set the Metrics source to Automatic. Where an integration is read from when it is not found by name, its address, stays the user's (A16, Prometheus's `cluster.setPrometheus`; Alertmanager's D-77). Every switch is in the audit log. What an agent can make Cogpit read so: [agents and MCP](../security/agents-and-mcp.md) |
| The section's place | first after General; last, as Cogpit's own Agents; right before Metrics | before Metrics: General, Proxy, Terminal, Namespaces, Integrations, Metrics, Node Shell, Agents (replaced 2026-10-18 by D-87: under a divider below Agents, a section per integration) | Which tools Cogpit reads, then the details of the metrics ones; Lens's relative order kept |
| The status line's words and colours | the states' names; sentences with the owner's two words | "Found automatically: <where>", "Configured: <where>", "Needs manual configuration: <what>", "Not in this cluster: <why>", "No permission: <what>", "Not answering: <where> (<why>)", "Checking…", "Off: nothing is asked of the cluster", "Not connected: found when the cluster is connected"; found and configured in the OK colour, manual in the warning colour, forbidden and not answering in the error colour, checking in the pending colour, the rest muted | The owner's "automatisch gefunden" and "Manuelle Konfiguration" are what the user must see at once; the status tokens carry the rest (rule 6) |
| Where a manual address is set | under the row on the Integrations section; where it lives now | Prometheus's on Cluster Settings › Metrics, where Lens has it, with a link "Set its address…" from the row; Alertmanager's under its row (D-77, through `integrationRowExtras`) | Prometheus's fields belong to the Metrics section by Lens's page; Alertmanager has no other place |
| When the question shows | once detection settled (bounded, 10 s: the ticket's proposal); at once, the statuses live | at once while the shown cluster is connected; "Checking…" turns into what was found | No timer and nothing waiting; the user sees the detection settle; the views load behind it |
| Which clusters are asked | contexts never connected before; every cluster without a choice; none but those added after this Cogpit | every cluster without a choice, those used before this Cogpit too (once each, until answered); not the demo cluster; not a session that keeps no cluster settings (the CLI's); a connected cluster not shown when it is shown | No file says which clusters are new; marking the known ones decided at the update would hide the new integrations from every user who updates. The demo cluster is generated, its metrics are its own and it runs nothing to find; the CLI has nowhere to keep an answer |
| The question's form | a dialog over the window; a panel in the workspace; a notification with a link | a dialog (Fyne's, as the confirmations), its views loading behind it | The owner asks to be asked; a panel or a toast is easy to miss. It holds up no connect: the connect has finished when it shows, and Later is one click; closing it otherwise counts as Later |
| Later | not asked again this run, asked again at the next start; asked again at the next connect; never (the default kept as the choice) | not again this run (a reconnect included), again at the next start's connect, until answered | A reconnect within the run would nag; never asking again would decide without the user. Meanwhile the default applies and Cluster Settings › Integrations chooses |
| The checkbox | on by default; off by default | off until ticked; it saves the cluster's answer as the default for new clusters | Saving a default is a choice beyond this cluster, so the user makes it |
| The dialog's switches | applied at each click; the dialog's own until Apply | the dialog's own until Apply; an integration off now and switched on in the dialog reads "Looked for once you apply" | Nothing changes before the answer; while an integration is off nothing is looked for, so its status cannot be known yet |
| Whether agents answer the question | the user only; agents too | agents too (`cluster.integrations.answer`, `cluster.integrations.later`), and the dialog closes whoever answered; **replaced 2026-10-19 by the owner's decision on H-126: the user only (the answer GUI-only), Later still the agents'** | They can reach the same with `cluster.settings.set` and `preferences.set`; refusing the answer would be a barrier with a way around it |
| Detection for the question and the section | lazy as before ("Checking…" until a drawer opens); at every connect; once when the question or the section shows a connected cluster | once when shown (`metrics.Hub.DetectUnknown`), bounded as detection is, a cut-short one not again before the retry TTL | Every connect would send the probes to clusters nobody looks at; lazy would leave the owner's "direkt ersichtlich" unmet |
| Where the default lives and is changed | the question's checkbox only; also a Preferences row | both: the checkbox, and Preferences › Kubernetes › Integrations of new clusters (five switches, beside the other cluster-wide defaults) | A default the user saved once should be visible and changeable without connecting another new cluster |
| The parameters' form | a list of names on or off; an object of name → on | an object (`{"alertmanager": false}`) in `cluster.settings.set`, `preferences.set` and the answer; names left out stay as they apply now | One form for every place; one call switches some on and others off |
| The demo cluster's Prometheus row | "Checking…"; "Not in this cluster" | "Not in this cluster: the demo cluster's metrics are its own" | Its hub has no Prometheus detection, so "Checking…" would never end |
| The parity pages | rows in ui-parity's Cluster settings; rows in beyond-lens | beyond-lens, a section "Cluster integrations"; ui-parity's Cluster settings introduction points to it, and its Metrics provider row says the source is the two switches | ui-parity's rows are Lens's and count toward Lens parity; these are Cogpit's own |

**Not verified:** a real window (renders and tests only); the real test cluster; Alertmanager's,
Trivy's and Kyverno's statuses, which their own probes give (D-77 to D-79): until they land, their
rows say "Checking…". The CLI's headless engine does not apply a cluster's switches
([H-120](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-120-the-clis-headless-engine-does-not-apply-a-clusters-integration-switches)).


## D-78: Trivy Operator's image ratings

**The owner's words (2026-10-17, the ticket's I6, verbatim):** "Eine weitere Integration ist Trivy,
ich will an allen Pods das schlechteste Image-Rating aller Container. Im Pod Drawer das Image Rating
pro Image angezeigt bekommen, wenn verfügbar. Ist die Trivy-Integration ausgeschaltet, werden diese
Informationen nicht eingeblendet."

**Status (2026-10-17): built.** A first phase built the integration's reads and its state, the
rating and the pod drawer's "Image Ratings"; a second, the same day, the Pods list's column "Image
Rating" with each pod's worst rating, on the integration overlay and the trimmed scopes the Kyverno
integration (D-79) built, so that both integrations share one mechanism each
([architecture › The integration overlay](architecture.md#the-integration-overlay-d-79-built-2026-10-17),
[§5 › Trimmed scopes](architecture.md#trimmed-scopes-d-79-built-2026-10-17)). Cogpit installs nothing: it reads what a running Trivy Operator wrote (AGENTS.md, D-61). Lens's
paid Security Center reads the same reports
([resource-parity › Paid Lens Desktop views](../parity/resource-parity.md#paid-lens-desktop-views),
G18); a rating on the pods is Cogpit's own
([beyond Lens › Cluster integrations](../parity/beyond-lens.md#cluster-integrations)).

- **The source** (seen on kind 2026-10-17: Trivy Operator 0.35.0, its chart 0.37.0, Trivy 0.75.0):
  one `VulnerabilityReport` (`aquasecurity.github.io/v1alpha1`, namespaced) per workload and
  container, in the workload's namespace, named `<kind>-<workload>-<container>`, labelled
  `trivy-operator.resource.kind`, `.resource.name`, `.resource.namespace` and
  `trivy-operator.container.name` (a name longer than a label value goes into the annotation of the
  same key, the label then `trivy-operator.resource.name-hash`, as Trivy Operator's source writes
  it), controlled by the workload (an owner reference with `controller: true`), with
  `report.artifact.{repository,tag,digest}`, `report.registry.server`,
  `report.summary.{critical,high,medium,low,unknown,none}Count`, `report.updateTimestamp` and
  `report.vulnerabilities` (each with its CVE id, title, description and links). A Deployment's pods
  are rated by their current ReplicaSet's reports, a CronJob's Jobs' pods by the CronJob's, a bare
  pod by its own.
- **The rating** ([`model/imagerating.go`](../../internal/model/imagerating.go)): `ImageRating`,
  `VulnerabilityCounts`, `RatingText`, `ParseVulnerabilityReport`, `VulnerabilityReport.Matches`.
- **The reads and the index** ([`engine/trivy.go`](../../internal/engine/trivy.go)): the
  integration's follower (registered in its file's `init`, D-76's contract) puts its overlay
  (`trivySource`, a `rowOverlay`) on the backend of each connected cluster while the integration is
  on and the cluster serves the reports' kind, a new one when their namespace plan changes, and
  takes it off when it is switched off. The overlay holds one cache handle on the reports, as the
  plan says (in all namespaces, or in each namespace the user named for a user who may not list
  them everywhere, nothing while the access reviews have not said which, then the session reads
  again), in a trimmed scope of its own (`Scope.Trim` "trivy-summary", `trimVulnerabilityReport`):
  the cache keeps each report without `report.vulnerabilities`, while the reports' own view, YAML
  and editor read the untrimmed scope and keep them whole. The index (workload and container to the
  report's summary) is built from the cache on the first lookup after a change; a change of the
  reports tells the overlays (`overlays.changed`, at most once per snapshot interval), which wakes the
  open view and drawer. The probe says found ("aquasecurity.github.io/v1alpha1", "7 vulnerability
  reports"), missing ("Trivy Operator's reports are not served"), forbidden ("list
  vulnerabilityreports.aquasecurity.github.io"), unavailable (the list's error, or "the custom
  resource definitions cannot be listed"), checking, or off. The backend's close stops the overlay
  with the others ([`overlay.go`](../../internal/engine/overlay.go)).
- **The Pods list** (the second phase): a column "Image Rating" right after Containers, each pod's
  worst image rating with its count ("Critical · 39") in the rating's colour, of the type
  `model.ColumnRank` (its text sorts by its rank, `RatingRank`: the rating, then the count; a pod
  without a rating sorts last), empty for a pod none of whose images has a report; `view_rows`,
  `resources_list`, the search and the CSV read it as the window draws it. Off, the column is gone.
- **The drawer:** through the overlay's sections, after the pod's own: a group "Image Ratings", one section per image titled
  by the image as the pod names it: Rating ("Critical · 39", in the rating's colour), Vulnerabilities
  (the counts as coloured chips, "39 Critical", "123 High", …), Container or Containers (an init
  container marked "(init)"), Scanned ("3h ago (date)"), Report (a link to the report's object in
  its custom kind view). An image without a report: "Not scanned".
- **Tests:** `TestImageRatings`, `TestParseVulnerabilityReport`, `TestImageMatches` (model);
  `TestTrivyImageRatings` (the sections of a ReplicaSet's pod of two images and an init container, a
  CronJob's Job's pod, a Job's pod and a bare pod; a pod without reports has none; a changed report
  reaches the open drawer; switched off: no handle, no section, the state off; on again),
  `TestTrivyNotServedOrForbidden`, `TestTrivyNamespaceLimited` (the reports read in the user's
  namespace after the refusal in all namespaces), `TestTrivyWorkloadsOf`, `TestTrivyPodsColumn` (the
  column's cells, colours and order, a new report reaching the list, the column gone when off),
  `TestTrivyReadsTrimmedReports` (the integration's objects without the vulnerability list, the
  reports' own scope with it), `TestTrivyWorstImage` (engine, also under the race detector);
  `TestRenderPodImageRatingsDark`, `TestRenderPodImageRatingsLight`, `TestRenderTrivyPodsDark`,
  `TestRenderTrivyPodsLight` (window, offscreen, the list over the real engine); `TestKindTrivy` against a real Trivy Operator (`make kind-trivy`,
  [hack/kind](../../hack/kind/README.md#trivy-operator)).
- **Checked on kind (2026-10-17):** the integration found; the drawers of the five test workloads'
  pods rated as Trivy Operator's own table lists them (nginx:1.16.1 Critical · 39, busybox:1.37.0
  Clean for the init container and the second container, nginx:1.30.0-alpine High · 10, alpine:3.12
  Critical · 1 through the CronJob and through a bare pod's own report); switched off, the handle
  released. **What the reports cost** (`Cache.StatsWithMemory`): 7 reports, 745,569 bytes in the
  cache, of which nginx:1.16.1's (363 vulnerabilities, 186 KB of JSON) 480,797 and
  nginx:1.30.0-alpine's (179) 237,434; without `report.vulnerabilities` the same 7 reports take
  35,181 bytes, about 5 KB each (the cache's size estimate over the same objects): the vulnerability
  lists are 95 % of the weight, about 1.3 KB per vulnerability. A cluster of 500 workloads with old
  images would hold tens of megabytes for a summary of a few megabytes at most: the number behind
  the second phase's trimmed scope. **The second phase, checked on kind the same day:** the Pods
  list rated the five pods as their drawers do ("Critical · 39", "High · 10", "Clean",
  "Critical · 1" twice); the integration's trimmed scope held the 7 reports in 34,789 bytes, the
  reports' own untrimmed scope, opened beside it, 745,585 (`TestKindTrivy`); switched off, the
  column gone.
- **Not checked on the real test cluster:** it runs no Trivy Operator (the ticket's check of
  2026-10-17).

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| What the rating is | a letter grade (A–F); a score (CVSS); the worst severity's word | the worst severity found: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Unknown, Clean (a report without vulnerabilities), Not scanned (no report) | The scanner's own vocabulary needs no legend; a grade would need a rule nobody can check from the report |
| Where Unknown ranks | below Low; above Low; apart | above Clean and below Low | Vulnerabilities without a severity are worse than none and not known to be worse than a low one; Trivy's own summaries list them last |
| The count beside the word | the word alone; the word and its count; all counts | the word and the count of that severity, "High · 3"; Clean and Not scanned alone; the drawer adds every severity's count as chips | One Critical reads apart from forty, and the column (phase two) stays short |
| Colours | one colour; per rating | the status tokens in Trivy's order: Critical error red, High warning orange, Medium pending yellow, Low succeeded blue, Unknown grey, Clean OK green, Not scanned none | Rule 6: the theme's tokens; Trivy's CLI colours its severities in the same order |
| Which reports are a pod's | its own; its controller's; by image across the cluster | its controller's as Trivy Operator resolves it (ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, ReplicationController, Job; a CronJob's Job's: the CronJob's; a bare pod or one another controller made: the pod's own) | A report is made for the workload, and the operator picks the same owner; a report of the same image elsewhere would rate the pod by another workload's scan |
| A Job's CronJob | read the Jobs (a watch of every Job while the integration is on); the Job's name | the Job's own reports first, then the CronJob the name says, "<cronjob>-<digits>", as the CronJob controller names its Jobs | No watch of Jobs for a rating. A Job made by hand from a CronJob under another name has no rating (not scanned) |
| A report of another image (the workload changed, not scanned again) | show it; leave it out | left out: the image "Not scanned" until the operator replaces it; compared are the repository (without registry and Docker Hub's `library/`) and the tag when both have one, not the digest (an image index's and a platform's differ) | A rating of another image would mislead |
| Init and ephemeral containers | containers only; with init containers | init containers count, marked "(init)"; ephemeral containers do not | An init container's image runs in the pod and Trivy Operator scans it; an ephemeral one is in no workload's template, so no report has it |
| Per image or per container | a section per container; per image | per image, naming the containers that run it | The owner: "pro Image"; two containers of one image share one rating |
| A pod none of whose images has a report | a section saying so; no section | no section; within a section, an image without a report says "Not scanned" | The owner's "wenn verfügbar"; a namespace the operator does not scan or a scan not done yet is no news per pod, and the integration's state says whether the reports are read |
| What a section shows | the vulnerability list; the summary | Rating, Vulnerabilities (chips), Container(s), Scanned, Report (a link); no CVE list, no scanner, OS, digest or end-of-life mark | "Sparsam": the report's own view and YAML have the rest one click away |
| Where the reports are read | per drawer, the pod's namespace; one read per cluster while on | one handle per connected cluster while the integration is on, as an open page reads its kinds, the index rebuilt from the cache after a change | The Pods column (phase two) needs every pod's rating at once |
| A namespace-limited user | read all namespaces; the plan's namespaces | the plan's (accessible namespaces, the filter's, else the context's); a pod in another namespace has no section | As every page reads its kinds ([`accessiblens_pages.go`](../../internal/engine/accessiblens_pages.go)) |
| A user who may not list the custom resource definitions | a curated profile of the reports' kind (discovery would name it); none | none for now: the state says Cogpit cannot tell ("unavailable", or "forbidden" when the refusal says so) | Discovery finds only curated kinds (A90); a curated profile of the reports would change their view's columns too, a change of its own |
| Agents | a structured field in `object_get`; the sections | the sections, as the window shows them, through `object_get`; no new command or tool | What the window shows, agents read (rule 1); the switch is D-76's |
| `ClusterVulnerabilityReport` | read; not | not read | Trivy Operator writes it for cluster-scoped workloads, not for pods |
| The Pods list's column: where and what it is called (second phase) | in the warning column, merged as Kyverno's marks are; a column of its own after Containers, after Status or last | a column of its own, "Image Rating" (the owner's word), right after Containers | A rating is a value to read and sort by, not a reason behind an icon; beside the containers' squares it reads as their images' rating, and it is on screen where the last columns may need a scroll |
| How it sorts | by its text; by a rank | by a rank: the rating, then the count of that severity (`model.ColumnRank`, a column type of its own: text that sorts by `Cell.Num`; a cell without text is empty and sorts last) | By text, "Clean" would sort beside "Critical"; a number column would show "0" for a pod without a rating |
| Its width | 110; 96 | 96 points | "Critical · 39" and the title fit; at a 1440-point window the Pods list's Age and ⋮ columns then need a horizontal scroll (the renders), as wider lists already do; a user who does not want it hides it in the ⋮ menu |
| When the column shows | while the integration is on and the cluster serves the reports; only while some pod has a rating | while the overlay is on, also before any pod has a rating | A column that comes and goes with the reports would move the columns after it; off, it is gone |
| A pod some of whose images have no report | its worst rated image's; "Not scanned"; a mark | the worst of the rated images; the drawer lists the others as "Not scanned" | Trivy Operator scans a workload's containers together, so a part rated is a scan under way or a report of another image; the column stays short |
| Other kinds (Deployments, Jobs) | the worst of their pods; none | none | The owner asked for the pods; a workload's pods carry theirs |
| The drawer's sections | a line in the drawer's model; the overlay's sections | the overlay's, after the pod's own sections and before Kyverno's (the integrations' order) | One mechanism for every integration that marks objects (D-79); the overlay's waitSynced gives an agent's read the reports a connect just started |
| What the trimmed scope keeps | the summary alone; the report without its vulnerability list | everything but `report.vulnerabilities` | The other fields (artifact, registry, scanner, OS) are a few hundred bytes; the list is 95 % of the weight |
| Which clusters read the reports (the lead's decision, 2026-10-17, after CI showed a background cluster that never went cold) | every connected cluster; the shown one only | the shown one only (`followTrivy`: the integration on and the cluster the one shown) | The ratings show only in the shown cluster's views; reading them for a cluster connected in the background keeps its cache warm, so it never goes cold (D-69), and watches reports nobody sees. Shown again within the cache's warm period (5 minutes) the reports are there at once; later they list again |

**What it does not cover, and not verified:** the real window (offscreen renders only:
[`trivy_render_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/trivy_render_test.go),
[`trivy_pods_render_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/trivy_pods_render_test.go)); with the reports'
own view open, the reports are watched twice, trimmed and whole (D-79's trimmed scopes); Trivy Operator versions
other than 0.35.0; a workload name longer than a label (the annotation is read, tested on a synthetic
report only); `DetailWait` (agents) does not wait for the reports' initial list, so a read right after
connecting may come without the section; switched off, the reports' watch stays open for the cache's
warm period (5 minutes) as after a closed view, and asks nothing new.

## D-77: Alertmanager, the alerts pill and the alert board

**The owner's requirement (2026-10-17, I4 and I5 of the cluster integrations' ticket, verbatim):**
"Dazu kommt jetzt Alertmanager um darauß ein Alert-Dashboard zu entwickeln. Ich habe einen
Screenshot vom Karma-Dashbaord angehängt, das sieht ungefähr so aus, wie ich mir ein
Alert-Dashbaord vorstelle. Aber ich hätte es gerne etwas aufgeräumter als karma, denn es ist ein
wenig überladen. Oben der Alert-Button in der Titelleister führt zum Alert-Board, wenn die
Integration eingeschaltet wurde. Der Button oben wird, Gelb einem Info Alarm, Orange ab einem
Warning Alarm, Rot ab einem Critical-Alarm, die Zahl daneben gibt die Gesamtzahl aller aktiver
Alarm an." His answer the same morning: "nur wirklich relevantes zeigen. Sparsam bei der
Darstellung": alerts of severity `none` (Watchdog, InfoInhibitor: meta alerts) are neither counted
nor shown; info, warning, critical (and `major` as orange) are. Lens has no alerts: this is Cogpit's
own ([beyond Lens › Alerts](../parity/beyond-lens.md#alerts)). It is one of the integrations of
D-76: switched off for a cluster, nothing of it is asked or shown.

**Built 2026-10-17** (the lead's brief, built by its agent AM):

- **Reading Alertmanager** ([`internal/alerting`](../../internal/alerting/), a new L2 package with
  its own `depguard` entry, [architecture §3](architecture.md#3-dependency-layering-enforced) and
  [§9 › Alertmanager](architecture.md#alertmanager-internalalerting-d-77)): Cogpit finds the
  cluster's Alertmanager among the cached Services by its well-known names, or reads the address the
  user set, and asks it for `GET /api/v2/alerts?active=true&silenced=false&inhibited=false`
  through the API server's service proxy, one request every 30 seconds while the integration is on
  and the cluster is shown and connected ([`engine/alerts.go`](../../internal/engine/alerts.go)).
  Cogpit installs nothing (D-61).
- **The pill** ([`fyneui/alerts.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/alerts.go); this changes D-54's
  pill, prepared without a source): red from a critical alert, orange from a warning (major and
  every other label too), yellow from an info alert, the bell's colour without alerts; its number
  every alert shown, "99+" beyond 99; its tooltip the counts by severity ("Alerts: 4 critical, 33
  warning, 1 info") or why there are none; a click opens the board (`alerts.open`). A dash in the
  bell's colour while nothing has answered; hidden while the integration is off for the shown
  cluster, while no cluster is shown and for the demo cluster. Engine state: `ui_state`'s
  `alerts` (`UIState.Alerts`).
  **Changed by the owner's look (2026-10-20, his screenshot of the pill at ⚠ 5):** "Das Dreieck ein
  bisschen größer bitte, ein wenig mehr Abstand zwischen Dreieck und Zahl. Die Zahl so groß wie das
  neue Dreieck. Ist die Alertmanager-Integration ausgeschaltet, kein Dreieck anzeigen. Ist sie
  eingeschaltet aber kann nicht verbinden, bitte grau und "warn" schreiben. Ist die Integration
  eingeschaltet aber alertmanager meldet keine Alarme befinden wir uns im grünen Zustand. (Zahl
  0). Die Inhalte dürfen nicht über die Pille hinausreichen." Built the same day: the sign in an
  icon the bell's side (18 points: drawn 16 × 14 pixels at scale 1, was 13 × 11), the number's text
  size the same (its digits 13 pixels tall, was 8; on v0.31.0 the owner: "Die Zahl doch etwas
  kleiner. Sieht schrecklich aus", so the views' text size since, 13 points, its digits 10 pixels,
  centred on the sign: the lead's pick of 13, 14 and 15 rendered side by side), a padding between
  them (6 pixels drawn, was 3), the pill the icon and a padding high (22 points, was 19), both inside it
  (`TestAlertsPill`), and on v0.31.1 ("die Pille ist mir zu eng", "5px rechts und links dazu")
  5 points more at each end (`alertsPillEnd`), 9 points from the pill's edge to the sign and from the
  number to the edge; green (the ok token) with "0" without alerts; grey (the unknown token) with
  "warn" while nothing answers (none found, forbidden, unavailable); off: hidden, as built. The
  lead's details, open to revision: a dash, grey, while the first look runs (a second, not "cannot
  connect" yet); a failing Alertmanager keeps its last answer's colour and number for its 5
  minutes as decided below, then turns grey with "warn" (the rule against a pill flickering grey at
  one failed poll stands); grey is the unknown token (the status of a state that could not be
  determined, the lists' grey).
- **The board** ([`engine/alerts_board.go`](../../internal/engine/alerts_board.go),
  [`fyneui/alertboard.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/alertboard.go)): a page (`alerts/board`,
  "Alerts"), its header a view's (the title, the count, the namespace filter and the search), its
  body a fold per severity, worst first, with its colour and count, in each a card per alertname
  with its count, and per alert one line: the summary (a click unfolds the description under it),
  since when it fires and a Runbook link at the right; under it the namespace and the object the
  alert is about, as links. Read only.
- **The address** ([`engine/alerts_settings.go`](../../internal/engine/alerts_settings.go),
  [`fyneui/clustersettings_alertmanager.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clustersettings_alertmanager.go)):
  "Alertmanager service address" (namespace/service:port, empty for detection by name), "Use
  HTTPS" and "Alertmanager path prefix", under Alertmanager's row on Cluster Settings › Integrations
  (D-76's hook for an integration's own controls; on the Metrics section for the hours before the
  two were merged); kept in `metrics.json` beside the Prometheus address. Since 2026-10-18 on
  Alertmanager's own section (D-87), headed "Service address" and "Path prefix"; the board's link to
  its settings opens that section.
- **Commands** ([`commands/alerts.go`](../../internal/engine/commands/alerts.go)): `alerts.list`,
  `alerts.board`, `alerts.refresh` (reads), `alerts.open`, `alerts.fold` (UI), `cluster.alertmanager`
  (read) and `cluster.setAlertmanager` (UI, an agent's always waits for the user); each an MCP tool.
- **Tests:** `TestClassify`, `TestDecodeAlerts`, `TestBoundLabels`, `TestCandidates`,
  `TestTargetWhere`, `TestPollerDetectsAndPolls`, `TestPollerStates`, `TestPollerFailures`,
  `TestPollerBackoffAndKeep`, `TestPollerCloseCancels`, `TestErrorText`,
  `TestPollerThroughTheServiceProxy` (alerting); `TestAlertmanagerIntegration`,
  `TestAlertmanagerOff`, `TestAlertmanagerAddress`, `TestAlertmanagerOnlyTheShownCluster`,
  `TestNoAlertmanager` (engine); `TestAlertCommands` (commands); `TestAlertsPill`,
  `TestTopBarRightOrder`, `TestAlertBoard`, `TestAlertmanagerAddressFields` and the renders
  `TestRenderTopBarAlertsDark`/`Light`, `TestRenderAlertBoardDark`/`Light`,
  `TestRenderAlertmanagerFieldsDark`/`Light` (window): the board
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/alert_board_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/alert_board_light.png)), the pill in each state
  (`topbar_alerts_<state>_<theme>.png`: none, info, warning, critical, notfound), the address
  fields (`settings_alertmanager_*.png`). The fixtures are synthetic, shaped like the
  real cluster's answer (`testkit.SampleAlerts`, a fake Alertmanager behind the fake API server's
  service proxy, `testkit.FakeAlertmanager`).
- **Checked on kind** (2026-10-17, `make kind-alertmanager`, `TestKindAlertmanager`): a real
  Alertmanager v0.28.1 found by its Service's name, the test's own alerts posted to it and resolved
  at its end: the pill's counts as posted (none and Watchdog left out, major as warning), an
  alert's Deployment linked, one GET per poll.
- **Checked on a cluster the owner provides for tests** (2026-10-17, read only,
  `TestRealAlertmanager`): kube-prometheus-stack's Alertmanager found by name; Cogpit counted 39
  (critical 4, warning 35 of the labels warning and major, info 0), Alertmanager answered 40 active,
  the one more its Watchdog.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision** (★ built):

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the client lives | (a) inside `internal/metrics` (its service-proxy GET, detection by cached Services, the probe bound of D-71); (b) a new L2 package with its own `depguard` entry | ★ (b) `internal/alerting` | metrics is 10,000 lines of providers, hubs and series, its Detector and Provider model made for polled series, not a list of alerts; a package of its own has its own tests and its own rule. Cost: some 60 lines of the proxy's GET and of the error classes repeated, with the same rule: what the proxied service answers is never quoted |
| Detection | (a) by the Services' names among the cached Services, as Prometheus is (D-71); (b) a probe of every Service on port 9093; (c) the Prometheus Operator's `Alertmanager` resources | ★ (a), at most 3 probes, names ranked: `<release>-kube-prometheus-alertmanager` (kube-prometheus-stack) 100, `alertmanager-main` (kube-prometheus) 95, `alertmanager-operated` (the operator's headless service) 90, `vmalertmanager-<name>` (VictoriaMetrics' operator, an upstream Alertmanager) 85, `<release>-alertmanager` (the alertmanager chart, the prometheus chart's bundled one) 80, `alertmanager` 70 in monitoring, prometheus or alertmanager, else 40; the port named `http-web`, `web`, `http` or `http-alertmanager`, else 9093, else 80, the gossip (`mesh`, `cluster`) and reloader ports never | As D-71's reasons: (b) sends requests to services that are none; (c) needs the right to list the operator's kinds and misses the charts' installs |
| The probe | (a) `GET /api/v2/status` (the ticket's proposal); (b) `GET /-/ready`; (c) the alerts request itself, its answer checked as Alertmanager's list | ★ (c) | (a)'s answer carries Alertmanager's whole configuration (`config.original`: receivers, routes, webhook URLs; Alertmanager masks its secret fields, not the rest), which Cogpit has no use for; (b) is answered by Prometheus too and tells nothing. (c) is one request per candidate instead of two; an empty list counts, from a service named like an Alertmanager |
| How often | (a) every 30 s; (b) every 60 s | ★ (a) | karma's and Alertmanager's own UI refresh, the `group_wait` of Alertmanager's default route; one GET (about 50 KB for 40 alerts). Budget [P17](testing.md#performance-budgets-proposed-not-measured) |
| Which clusters are polled | (a) every connected cluster with the integration on; (b) only the shown one | ★ (b) | The pill shows the shown cluster's; a background cluster whose login is held (D-69 item 4) would answer a poll with a 401. Shown again, it polls at once when its last poll is older than the interval. Cost: an agent's `alerts.list` of a background cluster reads its last answer (`asOf`) |
| A failing Alertmanager | (a) the pill turns grey at the first failure; (b) the last answer kept for a while; (c) kept forever | ★ (b): the polls back off from 30 s, doubling to 5 minutes; the last answer stands for 5 minutes of failures (the pill keeps its colour and number, the tooltip and the board say since when), then the next failed poll drops it; while the connection is interrupted it is kept (the banner says so, D-58) | (a) shows "no alerts" for a restarting Alertmanager; (c) leaves an old count standing as the cluster's |
| Bounds | – | an answer at most 16 MiB, 10,000 alerts kept (the lists' 10,000 rows), an annotation 4 KiB, 64 labels of 1 KiB each; a card shows 50 alerts, the rest counted under it for the search | A rule's template can render a log line into an annotation; thousands of widgets at a refresh |
| Severity | the owner named critical, warning, major, info and none | none, Watchdog and InfoInhibitor whatever their label: left out; critical red; info yellow; warning, major and ★ **a missing or any other label** (page, error, high) orange, its label kept and shown on the card ("major") | The owner's "Orange ab einem Warning Alarm": what a rule's author did not mark as only informational counts as a warning |
| The pill's colour for info | (a) a new theme token; (b) the yellow status token (Pending's, Solarized yellow) | ★ (b) | Already held to the palette's contrast tests in both themes (`TestPaletteContrast`); the brief's "new token if none fits": one fits |
| The pill without an answer | (a) hidden (not found, forbidden, failing from the start); (b) a dash in the bell's colour, the tooltip saying why | ★ (b), since the owner's look of 2026-10-20 grey with "warn" (above); hidden only while the integration is off, no cluster is shown and for the demo cluster | The owner: the button leads to the board while the integration is on; the board then says how to set the address. Cost: a cluster without an Alertmanager shows a grey dash until the integration is switched off for it |
| The pill in `ui_state` | (a) the counts and the state; (b) also when it was answered | ★ (a) | (b) would change the UI state's revision at every poll; `alerts.list` and `alerts.board` carry `asOf` |
| The board's place | (a) a page in the table view's frame, its header a view's, its body over the table; (b) a page like the Overview with the alerts as the table under it; (c) a workspace of its own beside the table view | ★ (a) | The header's title, count, namespace filter and search come with it, engine state (`ui.setFilter`, `ui.setNamespace`); (b) is a table, not karma's groups and cards; (c) would duplicate the header and the drawer's seam |
| The board's order | – | severities worst first; cards by alertname; a card's alerts newest first | New trouble on top; names found by reading |
| What an alert shows | karma's chips of every label, the description open, receivers, silences | the summary (a rule with only a description: its first line), since when (the lists' age), the Runbook link, the namespace and **the object it is about**: the most specific of the labels deployment, statefulset, daemonset, replicaset, cronjob, job_name, horizontalpodautoscaler, poddisruptionbudget, persistentvolumeclaim, ingress, persistentvolume, node; kube-state-metrics' custom resource labels (a Flux Kustomization); an x509 exporter's secret labels; else the pod with its container, unless the pod's name begins with the job's or the service's name (the exporter's own pod) | "Sparsam": the labels service, endpoint, instance, job, prometheus, cluster and environment name the scraped target or the cluster, and on a workload's alert the pod beside the Deployment is kube-state-metrics' own (seen on the real cluster). A namespace link narrows the board's namespace filter (as a list's Namespace column), an object link opens it (`ui.navigate`); an object of a kind the cluster does not serve is text |
| The runbook | – | only an absolute http or https URL without user info, checked in the engine and again in the window, opened in the browser | It comes from the cluster |
| Search and namespace filter | – | the UI state's search (terms or a regular expression, as the views') over alertname, severity, summary, description and the objects' names; under a namespace filter an alert that names no namespace is left out | The same search the lists have |
| Folding | (a) the window's; (b) engine state | ★ (b) `UIState.AlertBoard` with `alerts.fold`, as the navigator's groups (D-51) | Agents see what the user folded |
| The address's file | (a) `metrics.json` beside the Prometheus address; (b) `alertmanager.json`; (c) the cluster settings (`cluster-settings.json`, in `ui_state`) | ★ (a), the key `alertmanager` | The same kind of setting (a service read through the proxy), already owner-only, every backend carries it, no new wiring in either binary. Cost: the file's name says metrics |
| An agent's address | (a) as any UI command; (b) always asks | ★ (b), as the Prometheus address (A16) | Which service Cogpit asks with the user's identity is the user's |
| Silences, acknowledgements | – | not built: read only | A write to Alertmanager, outward-facing; the ticket's scope is the board |
| Alertmanager behind other names | – | VictoriaMetrics' VMAlertmanager is found (an upstream Alertmanager); vmalert is not an Alertmanager (it sends to one; it serves no `/api/v2/alerts`); Thanos Ruler is not one; Mimir's and Cortex's multi-tenant Alertmanager (`/alertmanager/api/v2` with a tenant header) not supported; an Alertmanager behind an authenticating proxy (OpenShift's port 9095) answers the proxy's 401 or 403: "not answering", its class shown | Not verified against any of them; none runs on the clusters at hand |

### What it does not cover

- **The board and the pill in a real window,** live: renders only (offscreen, dark and light), the
  owner's walk outstanding.
- **Alertmanager behind Mimir, Cortex or an authenticating proxy,** dormant until a cluster runs
  one: the address with a path prefix reaches Mimir's API, but without its tenant header.
- **A background cluster's alerts** are its last answer while it is not shown (by design, above).
- **Alert texts reach agents and the chat's LLM endpoint:** [agents and MCP](../security/agents-and-mcp.md).

## D-79: Kyverno's policy violations on the objects

**The owner's words (2026-10-17, verbatim, the ticket's I7):** "Eine weitere Integration ist
Kyverno, ich will an den K8S-Objekten sehen wenn sie gegen eine Policy verstoßen die auf Audit
läuft." His answer the same day: "Ob auch Verstöße gegen Enforce-Policies an Altobjekten
erscheinen, ja zählen": a fail of an Enforce policy on an object that existed before it (found by a
background scan) counts and shows as an Audit one's does. Off for a cluster (the integration
settings, D-76), none of it shows and nothing is read.

**Built 2026-10-17** (the lead's brief, built by its agent KYV). Lens Desktop shows no policy
violations; its paid Security Center reads Trivy Operator's reports, not Kyverno's (G18,
resource-parity › Paid Lens Desktop views), so this is Cogpit's own
([beyond Lens › Integrations](../parity/beyond-lens.md#integrations)). What the user sees while the
integration is on and the cluster serves Kyverno's reports:

- **The lists:** the warning column marks every object a Kyverno report names with a violation,
  its tooltip "Kyverno: 2 policy violations (require-team-label, disallow-latest-tag)". A kind with
  a warning column of its own (Pods, Nodes, Cron Jobs, Pod Disruption Budgets, the RBAC views,
  Resource Claims) gets the reason joined to its own ("Containers not ready: app; Kyverno: 1 policy
  violation (…)") and the worse colour; every other kind, built-in or custom, gets the warning
  column after Name while one of its objects violates a policy. The column sorts (violations
  together), the search finds "Kyverno", the CSV, `view_rows` and `resources_list` carry it.
- **The drawer:** a group "Policy violations" after the kind's own sections, one section per
  violation titled by its policy: Policy (a link while the cluster serves the policy's kind), Rule,
  Result ("Fail", or "Warn (the policy is not scored)"), Message (a sentence a line), Severity,
  Category, Found by ("Background scan", "Admission review"), Reported (the user's date format).
  None for an object without a violation.
- **Agents:** `object_get` carries the drawer's sections, `view_rows` and `resources_list` the
  warning cell, and `kyverno_violations` (a read, from the cache) lists every violation of a
  cluster or of some namespaces with its object's reference, for a triage in one call.
- **The reports' own views:** Policy Reports and Cluster Policy Reports (Custom Resources ›
  wgpolicyk8s.io) with curated profiles: Name, Namespace, Kind, Object (a link), Pass, Fail, Warn,
  Error, Skip, Age as Kyverno's printer columns, and a drawer with the object, the summary and every
  result.
- **The integration's status** (the settings page and the first-connect question, D-76): found
  ("wgpolicyk8s.io/v1alpha2"), "Kyverno's policy reports (wgpolicyk8s.io) are not served", "may
  not list policyreports.wgpolicyk8s.io", or still checking; a refused cluster report kind named in
  the detail while the namespaced ones read.

The code: [`engine/kyverno.go`](../../internal/engine/kyverno.go) (the probe, the follower, the
reads, the index, the overlay, `PolicyViolations`), [`engine/overlay.go`](../../internal/engine/overlay.go)
(the integration overlay: an integration's cells and drawer sections on the rows and drawers the
kind profiles build, [architecture §4.4](architecture.md#the-integration-overlay-d-79-built-2026-10-17)),
[`cache/trim.go`](../../internal/cache/trim.go) (trimmed scopes, [architecture §5](architecture.md#trimmed-scopes-d-79-built-2026-10-17)),
[`model/kinds/policyreports.go`](../../internal/model/kinds/policyreports.go) (the reports' shape
and the curated profiles), [`commands/kyverno.go`](../../internal/engine/commands/kyverno.go).

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| (1) Where the violations come from | (a) the wgpolicyk8s.io reports through the cache (list and watch); (b) Kyverno's policy-reporter REST API or its reports-server through the service proxy; (c) evaluate the policies in Cogpit | ★ (a) | Cache first (AGENTS.md): the reports are Kubernetes objects Kyverno keeps current, so one watch per kind holds them, and nothing is polled. (b) needs a component the cluster may not run and polls; (c) re-implements Kyverno |
| (2) A user who may not list reports in all namespaces | (a) the kind's namespace plan, as views read kinds (accessiblens_plan.go: the accessible namespaces and the filter's, one watch each; nothing while the access reviews have not answered); (b) all namespaces, and the refusal shows | ★ (a) | Kyverno grants namespace users read on their reports (its aggregated roles), and such a user is the one who wants to see their own objects' violations; a refused cluster-wide read is followed as for every kind (`followRefused`) |
| (3) Finding the reports for a user who may not list the definitions | (a) curated profiles of PolicyReport and ClusterPolicyReport, so that API discovery offers them (A90); (b) the generic custom kinds only | ★ (a) | A namespace-limited user rarely may list definitions; without (a) the integration would say "not served" to exactly the users of (2). The curated views also link each report's object |
| (4) Which results mark an object | (a) fail only; (b) fail and warn; (c) fail, warn and error | ★ (b) | Kyverno writes warn for a failed rule of a policy its author marked as not scored (`policies.kyverno.io/scored: "false"`): still a violation, shown as "Warn (the policy is not scored)". An error is Kyverno's failure to apply the rule, not the object's; it shows in the report's own drawer. Pass and skip are none |
