| (5) The policy's mode (Audit, Enforce) | (a) watch ClusterPolicies, Policies and the newer policies.kyverno.io kinds and show the mode; (b) not read; (c) read the policy when a drawer opens | ★ (b) | By the owner's answer every fail counts whatever the mode, so the mode only labels; (a) costs four watches and more (rules in large specs, per-rule `failureAction`, the namespace overrides, `validationActions`) for a label; the drawer's Policy item links to the policy, whose spec has the mode, and "Found by: Background scan" tells an Enforce policy's old object from a new one. The ticket's tooltip "(Audit)" became the policies' names |
| (6) Whose reports | (a) every report of the wgpolicyk8s.io API; (b) Kyverno's: its managed-by label, or a result whose source starts with "kyverno" (a Kyverno that set no label) | ★ (b) | Other engines write the same API (Kubewarden, adapters); their reports under "Kyverno" would mislead. Their results are dropped in the trim, so they cost no memory either |
| (7) Kyverno before 1.10 (a report per namespace naming each result's objects in `resources`) | (a) read both shapes; (b) the scope only | ★ (a) | Fifteen lines and a fixture (`TestPolicyReportResults`, `TestViolationIndex`); an object found by its UID, else by group, Kind, namespace and name |
| (8) Memory: reports hold every result, passes and skips too | (a) the cache keeps them whole; (b) a trimmed scope that keeps a Kyverno report's violations only (`cache.Scope.Trim`, a transform after managedFields') | ★ (b) | Measured with the cache's estimate (`StatsWithMemory`) on a real cluster the owner provides for tests (Kyverno 1.17.2, 165 reports, `TestRealKyverno`, 2026-10-17): **1,266,670 bytes whole, 511,426 trimmed (−60%)**; a cluster with many policies and objects holds mostly passes. The trimmed scope is an informer of its own, so the Policy Reports view, its editor and an agent's read still see whole reports (a second watch only while one of them is open). Trivy's reports, which hold full vulnerability lists, take the same mechanism (D-78) |
| (9) The index | (a) by the object's UID, else group, Kind, namespace and name; (b) by kind key, namespace and name | ★ (a) | A report's scope names the UID; a row and a drawer have the object, so one map lookup each, and a replaced object (same name, new UID) never inherits its predecessor's mark. Each event re-reads its report from the cache under the index's lock, so the last event's state wins whatever order the informers' goroutines deliver in |
| (10) A kind without a warning column | (a) the warning column added after Name while one of the kind's objects violates a policy; (b) added on every kind while Kyverno is on; (c) another mark (a coloured name, a badge) | ★ (a) | The owner asked for the lists' warning column, and one icon for "this object has a problem" reads the same everywhere and sorts; (b) puts an empty column on sixty views; (c) needs a new cell kind and does not sort. The column comes and goes with the kind's first and last violation, and the user may hide it, sort by it and move it like the kind's own |
| (11) The mark's colour | (a) warning for every violation; (b) by the result's severity (high and critical red) | ★ (a) | A violation does not break the object, and Kyverno's severities are the policy author's labels; the drawer names the severity |
| (12) The drawer's layout | (a) one table (policy, rule, result, message, …); (b) a section per violation in a group | ★ (b) | A drawer is narrow and messages are long sentences; items wrap a message onto lines (`messageLines`), a table cell would cut it |
| (13) The policy's link | (a) none; (b) a link while the cluster serves the policy's kind | ★ (b) | ClusterPolicy for a source `kyverno`, Policy for a policy named "<namespace>/<name>" (checked on a real cluster's Kyverno 1.17), ValidatingPolicy for the source `KyvernoValidatingPolicy` (seen on kind's Kyverno 1.19); Kyverno's other CEL kinds and a Kubernetes ValidatingAdmissionPolicy's results get no link: no report of theirs was seen |
| (14) Agents | (a) the drawer's sections and the rows only; (b) also a read command for every violation (`kyverno.violations`) | ★ (b) | A triage over every kind would otherwise read every view; the command reads the index the window uses and sends no request |
| (15) The status filter and the Overview's issues | (a) a Kyverno state in the status filter and the Overview's issues; (b) left as they are | ★ (b) | Both list the kinds' own states; a violation is not the object's state. Searching "Kyverno" and sorting by the warning column find the marked rows |
| (16) The real cluster's check | (a) violate the cluster's own policies; (b) Policies of the test's own, namespaced, in its own namespace, applied by background scans only (`admission: false`) | ★ (b) | The real cluster's ClusterPolicies are all mutating ones (no validate rule, so nothing can fail them); (b) changes no policy of the owner's and registers no webhook, and the namespace's deletion removes everything |
| (17) Which clusters read the reports (the lead's decision, 2026-10-17, after CI showed a background cluster that never went cold) | (a) every connected cluster; (b) the shown one only | ★ (b) | The marks show only in the shown cluster's views; reading the reports of a cluster connected in the background keeps its cache warm, so it never goes cold (D-69), and watches what nobody sees. `kyverno.violations` on a cluster that is not shown says so (`ErrKyvernoNotShown`). Shown again within the cache's warm period (5 minutes) the reports are there at once |

**Checked:** unit tests `TestKyvernoMarksViolations` (a Deployment's added column right after
Name, a Node's merged mark, another engine's report ignored, the drawer, agents, the trimmed
cache, a fixed object's mark and the added column going, off: no mark, no section, no handle),
`TestKyvernoMissing`, `TestKyvernoNamespaceLimitedUser` (a user with one RoleBinding: the reports read in its namespace after the refusal in all namespaces, the cluster reports named as refused), `TestViolationIndex`, `TestTrimPolicyReport`, `TestOverlayLayout`,
`TestMessageLines` (engine), `TestKyvernoViolationsCommand` (commands: `kyverno_violations`,
`resources_list`'s Warning cell, `ui_sort`, `ui_setColumns` by the added column, refused while off),
`TestTrimmedScope` (cache), `TestPolicyReportResults`, `TestPolicyRef`, `TestPolicyReportColumns`
and the curated goldens (model); **kind** (`make kind-kyverno`: Kyverno 1.19.1, chart 3.9.1, its
webhooks limited to the test's namespace; `TestKindKyverno`): an Audit fail on Deployments made
before and after the policy, an Enforce fail (`failurePolicy: Ignore`) on a ConfigMap from before
it ("Background scan"), a ValidatingPolicy's fail on a Service, an Audit fail on the Namespace (a
cluster report), every one marked and listed as the reports say, nothing else marked; **a real
cluster** the owner provides for tests (Kyverno 1.17.2; `TestRealKyverno`, 14.6 s, its namespace
deleted after): an Audit and an Enforce namespaced Policy's background fails marked and listed as
the reports say, a namespaced Policy linked as "<namespace>/<name>", the memory above. Renders,
dark and light, over the real engine (`TestRenderKyvernoDark`, `TestRenderKyvernoLight`): the
Pods' merged marks, the Deployments' added column, a Node's mark, a Deployment's drawer.

### What it does not cover

- **Kyverno's openreports.io reports,** not verified: a Kyverno that writes `openreports.io`
  Reports instead of wgpolicyk8s.io (off by default in Kyverno 1.19's chart, `openreports.enabled`)
  marks nothing, and while its cluster still serves the wgpolicyk8s.io kinds the integration says
  "found". The shape is said to be the same; reading both is a second pair of watches.
- **Reports in Kyverno's reports-server** (an aggregated API in place of the definitions), not
  verified: whether its wgpolicyk8s.io API serves watch as the definitions do.
- **The policy's mode** is not shown (decision 5); the policy's link shows it.
- **Kyverno's other CEL kinds** (NamespacedValidatingPolicy, ImageValidatingPolicy and their
  sources): their violations mark and list, their policy is not linked.
- **A real window:** the marks, the added column and the drawer were rendered offscreen, not seen
  in a window.
- **Policy messages reach agents and the chat's LLM endpoint:** they are cluster data a policy's
  author writes, and a message may quote the object's own fields through Kyverno's variables
  ([agents and MCP › H-11](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-11-instructions-hidden-in-cluster-data)).


## D-80: A cluster's accent colour

**The owner's words (F26, 2026-10-17, verbatim):** "Zusätzlich zum Icon braucht ein jeder Cluster
auch eine Akzentfarbe, die man konfigurieren kann, damit wollen wir später noch verschiedene Teile
der GUI markieren um während der Arbeit schnell sichtbar zu machen ob wir uns in einer Dev oder Prod
Umgebung aufhalten. Um zu vermeiden, dass ein User aus versehen Aktionen in einer Prod umgebung
durchführt, die er dort eigentlich nicht machen sollte, weil er unaufmerksam ist, und annimmt in
einer Dev umgebung zu sein. Wo wir die Akzentfarbe einsetzen, bleibt erstmal offen."

**Built 2026-10-17: the setting; where the window uses it is open.** Lens has no accent colour:
this is Cogpit's own ([beyond Lens › Everyday use](../parity/beyond-lens.md#everyday-use)).

- **The setting** ([`engine/accentcolor.go`](../../internal/engine/accentcolor.go),
  [`engine/clustersettings.go`](../../internal/engine/clustersettings.go)):
  `ClusterSettings.AccentColor`, kept per context as `accentColor` in `cluster-settings.json`,
  none by default; one of the icon colour's eight accent names (`IconColors`) or a free
  `#rrggbb` (`IsCustomIconColor`), drawn in the theme's legible shade as the icon colour is (A93).
  A value outside them is refused, and dropped from a file that holds one.
- **The window** ([`fyneui/clustersettings_accent.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clustersettings_accent.go)):
  Cluster Settings › General, a row "Accent colour" below the icon: None (an empty, crossed square,
  first), the eight swatches, the free colour's swatch while one is set, and the palette button
  (Fyne's colour picker, the icon's); a click sets it at once; the help line "Your mark for this
  cluster, red for production, say. Only you set it; agents read it."
- **Agents** read it as `accentColor` in `ui_state`'s `clusterSettings` and in
  `cluster_settings_get`. `cluster.settings.setAccentColor {context?, color}` (empty: none) is
  GUI-only (`Spec.GUIOnly`, `ErrAccentColorGUIOnly`): `Dispatch` refuses external agents, the
  built-in agent and the CLI before anything is read, written or asked, also where the user allowed
  agent writes, and audits the refusal; `cluster.settings.set` has no field for it, and
  `cluster.settings.resetIcon` leaves it ([agents and MCP](../security/agents-and-mcp.md)).
- **Not used yet:** nothing in the window shows the accent colour but its own row: not the tab
  bar, the title bar, the navigator, the hotbar, the status bar or a confirmation. It marks nothing
  until the owner decides where it goes; until then a cluster's name and icon colour are what the
  window shows of it, the user's alone since 2026-10-19 (below)
  ([H-125](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-125-until-the-accent-colour-shows-a-clusters-name-and-icon-colour-are-agents-to-change)).
- **Tests:** `TestAccentColorKept` (engine: the choices, a refused value, a file's value dropped,
  kept across a restart, in the UI state and the view); `TestAccentColorIsTheUsers` (commands:
  agents and the CLI refused setting and clearing, with and without agent writes, nothing written,
  nobody asked; `cluster.settings.set` has no field; the user's icon changes leave it; the user's
  colour kept, a free one, an unknown one refused, none again), `TestGUIOnlyCommandsRefuseOtherOrigins`,
  `TestClusterSettingsEqualComparesEveryField`; `TestClusterSettingsAccentColor` (window: None at
  first, a swatch's tap kept and shown, the free colour's swatch, None again, the icon colour
  untouched) and the PNGs
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/cluster_settings_accent_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/cluster_settings_accent_light.png)).

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who sets it | everyone, as the icon colour (a UI command, D-2); agents may only clear it (as the login's renewal); the user alone | the user alone, in Cogpit's window: agents and the CLI are refused setting and clearing it (the lead's decision, given with the brief) | The colour is the user's own mark against acting in the wrong cluster: an agent that could change it could make a production cluster look like a development one, and clearing a production cluster's red does the same harm as painting it green. Agents read it, so an agent can tell which cluster the user marked as production |
| The command's shape | a field `accentColor` in `cluster.settings.set` with a `Refuse` for other origins; a command of its own | `cluster.settings.setAccentColor`, GUI-only, as `cluster.settings.setAgentWrites` | The GUI-only mark is enforced for every origin before `Enabled`, a confirmation or `Run`, and its MCP tool says "GUI only", so an agent learns to ask the user; a field in the agents' own settings command would make that command half GUI-only |
| The choices | the eight accents; named meanings (dev, staging, prod); the icon colour's choices | the icon colour's: the eight names or a free `#rrggbb` (the brief's proposal) | One palette and one picker for both of a cluster's colours, each drawn legibly on both themes already; the owner named no scale, the meaning is the user's |
| The default | none; the icon colour; the theme's accent | none | An unset colour must not look like a mark: a cluster without one is neither "dev" nor "safe" |
| Beside the icon colour | the icon colour doubles as the accent; a field of its own | a field of its own; neither changes the other | The owner: "Zusätzlich zum Icon"; the icon colour stayed agents' to change (D-2), the accent did not (the icon colour the user's alone too since 2026-10-19, below) |
| Where on the page | a section of its own; General below the icon | General, below the icon and before the kubeconfig | It is part of the cluster's identity; a section for one row would hide it |
| How None shows | a "None" button; a swatch | a swatch, first in the row: an empty square crossed by a line in the muted colour, ringed while no colour is set, its tooltip "None" | The row keeps one shape, and None is selected as the others are; first because it is the default |
| A question before a change | ask, as turning on the allowance of agent writes asks; not | not | The allowance grants agents rights and asks with an armed button because an agent may open the page for the user; a colour grants nothing, and the page shows the result at once |
| Where the window uses it | tabs, the title bar, a frame, the confirmations | not decided | The owner: "Wo wir die Akzentfarbe einsetzen, bleibt erstmal offen" |

**The name and the icon too (2026-10-19).** Decided (owner, 2026-10-19 afternoon, H-125 option (b):
"Nein, sollen sie nicht können.") and built the same day: what the window shows of which cluster
this is, the display name and the icon, is the user's alone, as the accent colour is.
`cluster.settings.set`'s `name` and `iconColor` are refused to external agents, the built-in agent
and the CLI, set or cleared, before anything is written or asked, also where the user allowed
agent writes (`engine.RefuseClusterIdentity`, `ErrClusterIdentityGUIOnly` in
[`engine/clusteridentity.go`](../../internal/engine/clusteridentity.go)); `cluster.settings.resetIcon`
is GUI-only (`Spec.GUIOnly`, the same reason); `cluster.settings.uploadIcon` was already. Agents read
both (`cluster.settings.get`'s `name` and `iconColor`, `ui_state`'s `clusterSettings`). Tests:
`TestClusterIdentityIsTheUsers` (set and cleared, alone and with another field, refused for the three
origins with and without agent writes, nothing written, nobody asked; the user's name and colour
kept, an agent's terminal directory beside them; the user's reset; the tools' descriptions),
`TestGUIOnlyCommandsRefuseOtherOrigins`; turned: `TestAccentColorIsTheUsers` and
`TestClusterSettingsCommandsNeverTouchTheKubeconfig` set the name, the colour and the reset as the
window, `TestAccessibleNamespacesCommand`'s agent sets the terminal's namespace where it set the name. **The lead's decisions (2026-10-19), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The command's shape | a command of its own for the name and the icon colour, GUI-only, as `cluster.settings.setAccentColor` (the 2026-10-17 row above); refusing the two fields in `cluster.settings.set` | the two fields refused in `cluster.settings.set` (`Refuse` and `Run`), `cluster.settings.resetIcon` GUI-only | The window keeps the command it dispatches (unchanged, as the decision asks), and agents keep the command for the other fields; the command already refuses fields to some origins (a proxy from the CLI, the login renewal turned on), and each field's description says it is refused for agents, as `preferences.set`'s shell does. The reset has no other parameter, so it is GUI-only whole, its MCP tool "GUI only" as `uploadIcon`'s |
| Set only, or cleared too | agents may clear them (back to the context's name, the initials); neither | neither | Clearing a production cluster's "PROD" or red icon is the same harm as renaming it, as for the accent colour |
| A call that names a refused field and others | apply the others; refuse it whole | refused whole, before anything is written | One call, one outcome |
| The error | `ErrAccentColorGUIOnly` widened; `ErrIconGUIOnly` reused; one new error for the name and the icon | one new error, `ErrClusterIdentityGUIOnly`: "only the user, in Cogpit's own window, can change a cluster's display name or its icon (Cluster Settings › General): they are how the window shows which cluster this is, and an agent that could change them could make a production cluster look like a development one; agents and the CLI read them in cluster_settings_get and ui_state" | The upload keeps its own reason (it also reads a file; its text no longer offers the icon colour instead); the accent colour's tests and text stay as they are |

**What it does not cover:** where the colour shows (the owner's open question), so it protects
nothing yet ([H-125](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-125-until-the-accent-colour-shows-a-clusters-name-and-icon-colour-are-agents-to-change));
`cogpit-cli` has no way to set it (GUI-only) and nothing that shows it; not tried in a real window.

## D-81: Reconnect, and what Log in again does

**The owner's findings F28 and F29 (2026-10-17, verbatim):** "Nach einem Verbindungsabbruch zu
einem Cluster aufgrund eines abgelaufenen Zertifikates, kann kein Reconnect erfolgen. Das
Zertifikat auf Dateiebene ist bereits ausgetausch, auch ein Login Again führt nicht zum gewünschten
Ergebniss. Außerdem fehlt mir ein Button in der Clusterübersicht, für einen Reconnect, bei einem
reconnect wird die aktuelle Session unterbrochen und eine neue Verbindung mit aktuellem kube-config
file incl einem evl anstehendem token neu ausstellen usw. durchgeführt ohne die Tabs zu schließen.
Die Tabs werden nach dem neuaufbau aktualisiert."

**F28, the cause (verified 2026-10-17):** a connection keeps the credentials it read from the
kubeconfig at its connect. `cluster.Connect` builds the connection's `rest.Config` once: a client
certificate and key in the file (`client-certificate-data`, `client-key-data`, as a cloud's
kubeconfig download holds them) or a static `token` are copied into it, and nothing reads the file
again. client-go re-reads only a certificate and a key that are both files (every 5 minutes,
`transport/cert_rotation.go`) and a token file (every minute); an embedded certificate never. Log in
again (D-58, `connWatch.login`) renewed the login on the same connection: it let the next 401 reach
the context's credential plugin and checked the connection again. A context without a plugin had
nothing to renew it, so the check was rejected (401) again, as long as the old certificate was the
one presented. Seen on the owner's running Cogpit (read only, 2026-10-17): the context logs in with a
client certificate in its kubeconfig, no plugin; the file already held the renewed certificate
(D-75 reads it from the file at every listing) while the connection still presented the expired
one, and two Log in again after the renewal were rejected. Reproduced against the fake API server
(`TestLogInAgainUsesTheRenewedCertificate`: the in-place login stays rejected) and on kind with a
certificate of the kind cluster's own CA (`TestKindReconnectWithARenewedCertificate`).

**Built 2026-10-17** (the lead's brief, built by its agent RC): **Reconnect** ends a cluster's
connection and connects it anew from its kubeconfig file as it is now, the tabs kept; **Log in
again** reconnects where only the file can renew the login; and a login renewed in the file is
picked up by itself once the old one is rejected. Lens has no Reconnect of its own (its cluster menu
connects and disconnects, captured 2026-10-12): Cogpit's own
([beyond Lens › Standby and lost connections](../parity/beyond-lens.md#standby-and-lost-connections)).

- **The engine** ([`engine/reconnect.go`](../../internal/engine/reconnect.go)): `Session.Reconnect`
  makes the new connection first, as any connect makes it (the connector: the file read again,
  the cluster's proxy, the approvals of credential plugins and unchecked certificates, D-26 and
  A28), while the old one goes on showing its cache; once the new one stands it takes the old one's
  place in the pool (D-69) under a connect number of its own, and the old one closes. The UI state
  stays (tabs, view, filter, sort, selection, drawer, dock); the views follow the new backend and
  list anew, and the selection drops what the new cache does not hold. `connection.reconnecting`
  says it runs, `connection.credentialPlugin` whether the context logs in through a plugin.
- **The login in the file** ([`cluster/loginfile.go`](../../internal/cluster/loginfile.go)): at
  the connect the connection notes a fingerprint of the context's login as the file holds it (the
  user entry's credentials, its plugin's configuration, the cluster entry it is sent to, the size
  and modification time of the files they name); `Conn.LoginInFile` reads the file again and says
  whether it differs. The fingerprint is an HMAC under a key made for the process: it says nothing
  about a credential and never leaves the process.
- **The command** `cluster.reconnect` {context} ([`commands/connection.go`](../../internal/engine/commands/connection.go)),
  "Reconnect", `Cluster/Reconnect`, a UI command: it only reads from the cluster.
  `cluster.login` reconnects for a context without a plugin, or one whose login in the file changed.
- **The window** ([`fyneui/reconnect.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/reconnect.go)): a ↻ on every
  connected cluster's row in the navigator's list of all clusters, Reconnect above the cluster
  Overview's charts, in the window's Cluster menu and every menu of a cluster beside Disconnect, in
  the connection banner and the Connection Updates dialog, and in the palette; while it runs the
  cluster's dots blink as at a connect and its items say "Reconnecting…", greyed. Renders: the list
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/reconnect_section_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/reconnect_section_light.png)) and the banner of an
  expired certificate ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/reconnect_banner_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/reconnect_banner_light.png)).
- **Tests:** `TestReconnectKeepsTheUIStateAndSwapsTheBackend`, `TestReconnectRestartsLogsAndEndsShells`,
  `TestReconnectThatFailsKeepsTheConnection`, `TestReconnectingShowsWhileItRuns`,
  `TestReconnectWaitsForAJob`, `TestReconnectRestartsTheIntegrations`, `TestReconnectOfAClusterNotShown`,
  `TestLogInAgainChoosesHowToRenew`, `TestReconnectRefusedToAgentsForAnExpiredPluginLogin`,
  `TestLogInAgainUsesTheRenewedCertificate` (a fake API server that logs in by client certificate,
  `testkit.FakeAPIOptions.ClientCert`), `TestARenewedCertificateReconnectsByItself` (engine);
  `TestLoginInFileSeesARenewedLogin`, `TestLoginFingerprintNamesNoCredential`,
  `TestCredentialPluginIsNoted` (cluster); `TestReconnectCommand`,
  `TestPortForwardsCarriedAcrossAReconnect` (commands); `TestReconnectFromTheClustersList`,
  `TestReconnectInTheBanner`, `TestReconnectInTheConnectionLogAndOverview` (window);
  `TestKindReconnectWithARenewedCertificate` (kind: a client certificate of the kind cluster's CA,
  valid for 20 seconds, expires; the in-place login stays rejected; the renewed certificate written
  into the same file; Log in again connects with it, the tabs and the Pods view kept; then Reconnect
  of the working connection).

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the fix sits | a TLS callback that reads the kubeconfig's certificate at each handshake; a new connection from the file | a new connection from the file (Reconnect) | A callback covers certificates only, not a token, another server or another CA, and HTTP/2 keeps one connection, which would have to be closed anyway; a new connection is what a connect does, every approval included, and what the owner asked for |
| Old connection first or new first | end the old one, then connect (the owner's "die aktuelle Session wird unterbrochen"); connect the new one, then end the old one | the new one first, the old one ended the moment it stands | The tabs stay either way, as the owner asked; a reconnect that fails (the server down, a certificate rejected too) leaves the cluster as it was, its views showing the cache's last state, instead of disconnected |
| The command | a new id beside `cluster.reconnect` ("Reconnect now": try at once without credentials while interrupted); the same id with the new meaning | `cluster.reconnect` connects anew in every state of a connected cluster; "Reconnect now" leaves the window and the tools (`Session.TryNow` stays for the engine's tests) | Two items "Reconnect now" and "Reconnect" would ask the user to know the difference; connecting anew also "does not wait", and the connection's own attempts go on until the new one stands |
| What Log in again does | as before (the plugin once on the connection); always reconnect; reconnect where only the file can renew | the plugin once on the connection when the context runs a credential plugin and its login in the file is unchanged; else a reconnect from the file (a plugin whose program changed still asks first, D-26) | Without a plugin nothing else can renew the login (F28). With one, the in-place renewal keeps the cache, the streams and the forwards, which a reconnect relists or ends; the banner offers Reconnect beside Log in again for the case it does not help |
| A login renewed in the file, picked up by itself | never (the user clicks); whenever the file's login changes; when the connection's login is rejected and the file holds another | when the API server rejects the connection's login (Login expired) and the context runs no credential plugin: at the expiry, and when the kubeconfig sources' watch (every 2 s) sees the file change; each version of the file tried once; a connection that works is left alone | The owner's certificates last two hours: renewing them in the file is the user's act, and the old login already failed, so the new one is what any connect would use. A working connection is not relisted for a file change; its new login is used at its end. A plugin context never reconnects by itself: its program may open a browser (D-58) |
| Logs, shells, terminals, port forwards | end them all; restart them all; by their kind | a logs tab opens its stream again on the new connection (`DockTab.Session`); a shell, attach or node shell ends as at an interruption, its tab saying a reconnect ended it, with its Reconnect (`DockTab.Reconnected`); a local terminal runs on (it reads the file itself); a port forward that listened listens on the same local port again | A log can be read again without asking; a new shell runs a process in a container (`dock.reconnect` is a write and asks as it always does), so it is the user's click; a forward's redial is what it does after any lost connection, on the port the user's tools know. A stopped forward is not carried |
| A drain or a Helm action running | let the reconnect stop it (D-11's journal finishes it); refuse the reconnect while one runs | refused, with the job's title | A UI command never stops a write half-way; while the connection is interrupted or its login expired none runs anyway (they stop there, D-58) |
| The integrations and their question | restart them by hand; follow the new backend | they end with the old backend and their followers start them on the new one; the question of a new cluster's integrations is not asked again | The question follows the cluster's settings, not the connect (D-76) |
| Agents | GUI-only; a UI command for everyone; a UI command except where it is Log in again | a UI command (it reads only; no confirmation, audited), refused to agents and the CLI for a cluster whose login expired or lapsed while its context runs a credential plugin (`ErrReconnectLoginGUIOnly`) | An agent may connect a cluster already (an approved plugin may run then); renewing an expired plugin login, which may open a browser, stays the user's, as `cluster.login` is (never weaker than D-58) |
| A cluster connected but not shown | refuse; show it first; reconnect it in place | in place: its entry of `connections` gets the new connection, the shown cluster and the window stay; it is cold until shown | D-69: every command acts on its own cluster |
| Where the button is | the owner's "Clusterübersicht" read as the list of all clusters (the navigator's section, where each connected cluster has Show and Disconnect), or as the cluster Overview page | both: a ↻ on each connected cluster's row, and Reconnect above the Overview's charts; plus the Cluster menu, every cluster menu beside Disconnect, the banner (interrupted; an expired login, alone without a plugin and beside Log in again with one), the Connection Updates dialog and the palette | The word fits both; a button in each costs little and is where the user looks either way. The menus and the palette follow the registry |
| The connection log | the reconnect's lines in the old connection's attempts; an attempt of its own | an attempt of kind reconnect, "Reconnect · … · succeeded"; while it runs the old connection writes nothing to the log (its lines would end the reconnect's attempt) | One attempt that says what happened; a failed one says "the connection stays as it was" |
| The views after the swap | wait until the new cache listed the open view, then swap; swap at once | at once: the views list anew (a moment of loading), the dots blinking until then | Waiting for a namespace-limited user's lists could hold the swap for long; the owner's "die Tabs werden nach dem Neuaufbau aktualisiert" |
| The banner's text for a login without a plugin | as before ("Log in again runs the login program once; it may open your browser"); what renews it | "Renew the login in the kubeconfig file: Cogpit reconnects by itself once it changes, and Reconnect reads it again now", the button Reconnect | There is no login program; the old text sent the owner to a button that could not help. The reason "the API server still rejects the login (…)" no longer nests its own text twice |

**Not verified:** the owner's cluster and his real window (his walk); a real login program with
its browser at a reconnect; Windows and Linux; a reconnect while a drain runs end to end (refused by
the code path tested with a job of the test's own).

## D-82: A pre-choice before any integration is looked for, and Ask again

**The owner's words (2026-10-17, his walk on v0.23.0, verbatim):** WF5 (W49): "wir sollten über den
Integrationstool noch eine kurze Vorauswahl gestatten, schließlich werden hier "Suchen" mit User
privilage durchgeführt. Es soll eine Auswahl geben: "check all integrations", dann werden direkt alle
Integrationen sofort gesucht; "mark specific integration", dann sind alle abgewählt, die Suche
startet wenn der Nutzer die Integration markiert; "dont use integrations", dann bekommt der Nutzer
eine letzte Warnung angezeigt, dass ohne Integrationen auch keine Resourcen angezeigt werden können
und ob er das wirklich will, klickt er auf ja, dann wird der Cluster ohne Integration betreten, klickt
er auf nein, geht der Dialog zu und der Nutzer kann erneut die Vorauswahl beantworten, dort könnte
wieder auf "dont use integrations" oder eine andere Wahl treffen." WF4, after he applied the question
too fast: "Gibt es eine Möglichkeit den Dialog nochmal angezeigt zu bekommen?" (WF4's other half,
Remove from Cogpit forgetting a cluster's settings, is the lead's, not this decision.)

**Why it mattered (verified in the code before the change):** [D-76](#d-76-integrations-per-cluster-and-the-question-at-a-new-clusters-first-connect)'s
question detected the metrics providers as soon as it showed (`metrics.Hub.DetectUnknown`), and
until it was answered the default for new clusters, every integration on, applied: the Metrics
Server's discovery request, Prometheus's and Alertmanager's probes through the API server's service
proxy and the lists of Trivy's and Kyverno's reports ran with the user's identity before the user
chose anything, and kept running while the question was put off. Nothing brought the question back
once it was answered.

**Status: built 2026-10-17 evening** (the integrations agent, with the lead's decisions below, open
to the owner's revision). It changes D-76; D-76's note says which parts.

- **Consent before looking** ([`engine/integrationsconsent.go`](../../internal/engine/integrationsconsent.go),
  `integrationsOffOf` in [`engine/integrations.go`](../../internal/engine/integrations.go)): in a
  session that keeps cluster settings (the window's; `UIState.IntegrationsAskFirst`), a cluster
  without a choice of its own has every integration off, but those its question ticks while it asks
  (`UIState.IntegrationsLookFor`). No follower starts a read for it and its metrics source is No
  metrics: no discovery of `metrics.k8s.io`, no Prometheus or Alertmanager probe, no Trivy or Kyverno
  informer, before the question is answered, while it is put off with Later, and while the cluster
  is connected in the background. `Session.IntegrationsOffNow` is what applies now, the base an
  answer and a switch start from.
- **The question's steps** (`UIState.IntegrationsStep`): `preChoice` (the three choices, nothing
  looked for), `checkAll` (the rows, every integration the default for new clusters keeps on ticked
  and looked for at once), `choose` (the rows, none ticked; a tick looks for that one at once),
  `dontUse` (the warning over the pre-choice, nothing looked for). A question that starts, ends or
  turns to another cluster starts again at the pre-choice with nothing ticked
  (`syncIntegrationsStep`). `cluster.integrations.step {context?, step}` moves it (the pre-choice's
  buttons, the rows' Back, the warning's No); `cluster.integrations.lookFor {context?,
  integrations}` ticks and unticks the rows, on Check all and Choose only; the warning's Yes is
  `cluster.integrations.answer` with every integration `false`; Apply and Later as in D-76.
  A metrics provider ticked while another one's detection runs is looked for when it ends
  (`detectUnknownWhileShown`).
- **The window** ([`fyneui/integrationsask.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/integrationsask.go)): the
  dialog "Integrations for <name>" follows the step. The pre-choice: "Cogpit can read tools this
  cluster runs to show more: metrics, alerts, image ratings and policy marks. It looks for them with
  your identity and never writes to them. Nothing is looked for until you choose." and three
  buttons, each with a line of what it does: "Check all integrations" ("Check the default
  integrations" while the default switches some off, the line naming those it looks for), "Choose
  integrations", "Don't use integrations"; Later. The rows: a line of what happens, D-76's rows
  ticked as the engine says, an unticked one "Not looked for: tick it to look for it", a ticked one
  "Checking…" until its status comes, "Save as the default for new clusters", Back, Later, Apply.
  The warning: "Use <name> without integrations?", "Cogpit then shows no metrics, alerts, image
  ratings or policy marks for <name>; its resources still show. Cluster Settings › Integrations
  turns them on later.", No and Yes. Cluster Settings › Metrics of a cluster without a choice reads
  "No metrics" with "Not chosen for this cluster yet: no metrics are asked until you choose (here, in
  Integrations, or in its question)."
- **Ask again** (WF4): a button "Ask again" in Cluster Settings › Integrations under the section's
  help, with "Shows the question again from its first choice; nothing is read until you answer it."
  (not on the demo cluster), and `cluster.integrations.ask {context?}` (`AskIntegrationsAgain`): the
  cluster's choice and a Later of this run are forgotten, nothing of its integrations is read from
  then on, and the window asks from the pre-choice while the cluster is shown and connected. The
  section's note for a cluster without a choice: "Not chosen for this cluster yet: nothing is looked
  for until you tick one here or answer its question."
- **Agents:** `ui_state` carries `integrationsQuestion`, `integrationsStep`, `integrationsLookFor`
  and `integrationsAskFirst`; the five question commands are UI commands, MCP tools as every command
  is (216 commands). That an agent could so consent for the user was
  [H-126](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-126-an-agent-can-answer-the-integrations-question-for-the-user).
  **Changed 2026-10-19 by the owner's decision on H-126 ("Nein"), built the same day:** the step,
  the ticks and the answer (`cluster.integrations.step`, `.lookFor`, `.answer`) are GUI-only, and an
  agent's switch of a cluster the window still asks about is refused (it would answer the question);
  Later and Ask again stay the agents' (the lead's decisions, recorded in
  [D-76](#d-76-integrations-per-cluster-and-the-question-at-a-new-clusters-first-connect)).
- **The CLI and the demo cluster:** a session that keeps no cluster settings (`cogpit-cli`) asks
  nothing and reads every integration the default keeps on, as before
  ([H-120](../security/agents-and-mcp.md#h-120-the-clis-headless-engine-does-not-apply-a-clusters-integration-switches));
  the demo cluster is never asked and keeps the default.
- **Tests:** `TestIntegrationsOffUntilAnswered`, `TestIntegrationsQuestionSteps` (no metrics
  detection with a Pods view open before the pre-choice; Check all, Back, Choose and its ticks,
  Don't use and its Yes, Ask again after an answer and after Later), `TestIntegrationsAskAgainRefused`
  (engine); `TestIntegrationsQuestionLifecycle`, `TestIntegrationsConsentCommands`,
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionNotAsked`, `TestIntegrationSwitchCommands` (commands, as agents until
  2026-10-19, as the window since H-126; `TestIntegrationsOnAreTheUsers` the agents' refusals);
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionPreChoice`, `TestIntegrationsQuestionDontUse`,
  `TestIntegrationsQuestionLaterAndAgent`, `TestIntegrationsSection` (Ask again),
  `TestMetricsSourceLineUndecided` (window) and the PNGs of the pre-choice
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_light.png)), Choose with one row
  ticked ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_choose_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_choose_light.png)), the warning
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_warning_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/integrations_question_warning_light.png)) and the section
  with Ask again ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/cluster_settings_integrations_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/cluster_settings_integrations_light.png)).
- **Checked on kind** (2026-10-17 evening, `TestKindIntegrationsQuestion`, the kind cluster
  `cogpit` read only): the first connect asked on the pre-choice with every integration off and no
  metrics provider on; after Check all the Metrics Server and `monitoring/prometheus-server:http`
  were found.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17 evening), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| What is read before the answer | the default as before; detection only, the reads after the answer; nothing of any integration, also while put off | nothing, for any integration, until answered, also after Later and for a cluster in the background | The owner's point is consent before looking. Detection is a read with the user's identity itself (a discovery request, probes through the service proxy, report lists) |
| What a tick means while the question asks | detection only, the integration's reads after Apply; read as if on, behind the dialog | read as if on, until the question ends | For Alertmanager, Trivy and Kyverno the looking is the reading (the poller finds by name and asks; the reports are listed): a detection-only mode would be a second code path per integration. The user consented by ticking; the views behind the dialog show what was found |
| Where the steps and ticks live | the dialog's own; engine state with commands | engine state (`integrationsStep`, `integrationsLookFor`) and commands | Rule 2, UI state is engine state; a tick starts reads, which only the engine starts; agents see what the window shows |
| How many commands | one per button; the pages and the ticks, the answer and Later as before | two new ones, `cluster.integrations.step` and `cluster.integrations.lookFor`, and `cluster.integrations.ask` for Ask again | Fewest new tools; the step's values are `ui_state`'s; Don't use's Yes is an answer with every integration off, no command of its own |
| The warning's wording | the owner's ("ohne Integrationen auch keine Resourcen angezeigt werden können"); what actually goes | what goes and what stays: no metrics, alerts, image ratings or policy marks; the resources still show; Cluster Settings › Integrations turns them on later | Verified: the integrations feed only the metrics, the alerts pill and board, Trivy's ratings and Kyverno's marks; Pods, Deployments and the rest come from the API server either way. A warning that said otherwise would push the user to Check all |
| The warning's form | a page of the dialog; a dialog over the pre-choice | a dialog over the pre-choice, No and Yes; closing it is No | The owner: "geht der Dialog zu und der Nutzer kann erneut die Vorauswahl beantworten" |
| The three labels | the owner's ("check all integrations", "mark specific integration", "dont use integrations"); refined | "Check all integrations", "Choose integrations", "Don't use integrations", sentence case as the dialog's buttons, a line under each saying what it looks for | "Mark specific integration" reads as one; the lines make the consent explicit |
| The default for new clusters and its checkbox | dropped; a saved default skips the pre-choice; what Check all ticks, the label saying so; Choose prefilled with it | what Check all ticks: "Check all integrations" while it is all of them (the factory default), "Check the default integrations" naming them otherwise; Choose all unticked; the checkbox on the rows of both; Preferences › Kubernetes › Integrations of new clusters kept, its help saying what it does now | The owner asked for the checkbox as a default "für zukünftige Abfragen" (D-76): a default of the question, so skipping the question would drop it and dropping the default his ask; prefilling Choose contradicts his "dann sind alle abgewählt" |
| A way back from the rows | Later only; Back | Back to the pre-choice, nothing ticked | Nothing stays ticked behind the pre-choice, so its "Nothing is looked for" stays true |
| Later | as D-76, the default applying; nothing read | not asked again this run, nothing read meanwhile; the next start asks again | Consent before looking holds while the question is put off |
| The base of a switch or an answer for a cluster without a choice | the default for new clusters; what applies now | what applies now (`IntegrationsOffNow`): the question's ticks, or none | Cluster Settings › Integrations shows such a cluster's rows off; a tick there switches on that one, not the default's five. The window's Apply names all five anyway |
| Ask again | clear the choice, nothing read until answered; keep the choice until the new answer, the question prefilled | clear it, and a Later of this run with it | Taking a consent back has to stop the reads; a question that kept reading behind it would not be consent before looking |
| Where Ask again is | the Cluster menu; Cluster Settings › Integrations | a button under the section's help with a line of what it does, not on the demo cluster; the command for the palette and agents | The section is where the choice lives; the Cluster menu is crowded for a rare action |
| Ask again for a cluster without a choice | refused unless put off; allowed, changing nothing for a cluster that is asked anyway | allowed but while the window asks about it | The button needs no knowledge of Later, which `ui_state` does not carry |
| Agents | the user only; agents too, as D-76 | agents too: the five question commands are UI commands; the gap is H-126; **replaced 2026-10-19 by the owner's decision on H-126: the user only for the step, the ticks and the answer (GUI-only), Later and Ask again still the agents'** | D-76's "agents switch both ways" stands, and `cluster.settings.set` reaches the same; closing it means `AgentsAsk` for every switch on, a change of D-76 for the owner |
| The CLI and the demo cluster | ask; keep the default | keep the default; `integrationsAskFirst` says which session asks | The CLI has no window and keeps no cluster settings (H-120); the demo cluster's metrics are generated and nothing of it is looked for in a cluster |

| An unticked row's status in the question | the probe's (Kyverno's says found from API discovery even when off); "Not looked for" | "Not looked for: tick it to look for it" for every unticked row | The pre-choice and Choose promise nothing is looked for; a "found" there would read as if it was |

## D-83: One hotbar, and a drag that carries the tile

**The owner's findings WF7 and WF6 (his walk of 2026-10-17, verbatim):** WF7: "unsere Hotbar [hat]
am unteren Ende wie Lens so eine Pagezahl zum weitere Hotbars durchschalten, das wird nicht
benötigt. Es gibt nur eine Hotbar bei uns. Sie kann beliebig gefüllt werden, in ihr kann bei
entsprechender Größe gescrollt werden." WF6: "beim Ziehen von Icons in der Hotbar, dass Icon nicht
direkt an der Maus kleben bleibt, ich hätte für das Ziehen von Cluster bitte eine schicke Animation,
bei der man den Cluster quasi "mitnimmt" und die anderen cluster sich durch Ziehen ohne Loslassen
neu darum anordnen."

**Decided (owner, 2026-10-17): one hotbar.** Cogpit has one hotbar that holds as many clusters as
the user pins and scrolls when they do not fit. This is a deliberate deviation from Lens, whose
hotbar keeps banks of twelve behind a switcher ("‹ 1 ›" at the bar's foot, ⇧F1–⇧F12): the banks'
parity rows are not a target since ([ui-parity › Hotbar](../parity/ui-parity.md#hotbar)). **WF6**
replaces R2's look (the lead's of 2026-10-15: an outline where the tile was and an accent line in the
gap, nothing moving until the drop): the tile is carried under the pointer and the other tiles make
room for it while the button is held. Both built 2026-10-17 evening (the lead's brief, built by its
agent "hotbar"):

- **The engine** ([`engine/hotbar.go`](../../internal/engine/hotbar.go)): `HotbarState` is one list,
  `{clusters: [...]}`, without banks, a shown bank or a limit; `ui_state`'s `hotbar` carries that
  list, and so does `hotbar_list`. The commands keep their ids without a `bank` parameter
  (`hotbar.addCluster`, `hotbar.removeCluster`, `hotbar.moveCluster`, `hotbar.openCluster` by
  slot, `hotbar.list`); `hotbar.switchBank`, `hotbar.createBank`, `hotbar.renameBank` and
  `hotbar.removeBank` are gone, their MCP tools with them, and with `hotbar.removeBank` A65's wait
  for the user (an agent removing a bank with tiles). A `bank` field sent by an agent of the banks'
  time is refused as an unknown parameter.
- **The file** (`hotbar.json`): format 2, `{"version": 2, "clusters": [{"context": …}]}`. A file of
  format 1 (or without a version, as the first builds wrote it) is merged when it is read: the first
  bank's tiles in their order, then each further bank's in its order, a context pinned in several
  banks once, where it first appears; every bank is read, a bank's tiles beyond twelve too, so no
  tile is lost. The merged hotbar is written in format 2 at once, and the old file is kept beside it
  as `hotbar.json.v1` (owner-only); the log says how many banks became how many tiles.
- **The window** ([`fyneui/hotbar.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/hotbar.go)): the switcher is gone,
  the tiles fill the bar and scroll, the "+" below the last; F1–F12 open the first twelve tiles (the
  tooltip names the key only for them), a tile further down opens with a click, the palette's
  "Open *cluster*" or `hotbar.openCluster`; ⇧F1–⇧F12 are no hotbar keys any more (passed on as any
  key); the palette lists no bank entries; the welcome page's group is "Hotbar". A new hotbar list
  updates the tiles in place, one widget per context, so a tooltip or a drag survives it.
- **The drag** ([`fyneui/hotbardrag.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/hotbardrag.go)): past eight points
  a copy of the tile (the ghost) follows the pointer, held where it was grabbed, lifted (1.08 times
  the tile, on a card with a drop shadow); where the tile was, its empty slot (an outline); the slot
  travels with the pointer and the other tiles slide into the places a drop would give them, 150 ms,
  eased out, continuously; the drop is `hotbar.moveCluster`, as R2's, and the ghost glides into the
  slot. A drop outside the bar, on the tile's own place or after the bar changed under the drag
  moves nothing, the ghost gliding back; near the top or bottom edge of a bar that scrolls, the bar
  scrolls by itself; with Reduce motion (macOS's, and since 2026-10-20 Cogpit's own, D-107) nothing
  animates. The click that slipped (less than
  eight points) opens the cluster, as before. Renders: the drag
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/hotbar_drag_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/hotbar_drag_light.png)), the bar without its switcher
  ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/hotbar_tiles_dark.png),
  [light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/hotbar_tiles_light.png)).
- **Tests:** `TestHotbarStateOperations`, `TestHotbarNormalizesWhatItReads`,
  `TestHotbarMergesBanks` (three banks with the second shown, duplicates and an empty context; a
  file without a version and a bank of thirteen; the backup, the new file and the next start),
  `TestHotbarPersistsPrivately` (engine); `TestHotbarCommands`, `TestHotbarPastTwelveAndMissingTile`,
  `TestHotbarCommandsDeclareNoVerbs`, `TestPaletteListsWhatTheMenusOffer` (commands);
  `TestHotbarShowsItsTiles`, `TestHotbarUpdatesTilesInPlace`, `TestHotbarFunctionKeys`,
  `TestHotbarPastTwelveScrolls`, `TestHotbarParamsMatchTheRegistry`, `TestHotbarDragCarriesTheTile`
  (the ghost under the pointer, the slot, the tiles' places mid-drag, the order kept until the
  hotbar has the move, a drop on the "+"), `TestHotbarDragSlides` (the tiles and the ghost half-way
  through their animations; Reduce motion), `TestHotbarTileDragCancels` (own place, half a tile
  right of the bar, outside, the status bar, the bar changed under the drag, a failed move, the
  slipped click), `TestHotbarTileDragThroughTheCanvas`, `TestHotbarDragScrollsAtTheEdge` (window).

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17 evening), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The order of a merged file of banks | the shown bank first; the first bank first, then the others in order; the banks as sections with a divider | the first bank's tiles, then each further bank's in order, a context once where it first appears | The brief's rule: the order the user built reads top to bottom, and F1–F12 keep the first bank's tiles, the "Default" bank's, whichever bank was shown |
| When the old file is rewritten | at the first change of the hotbar; at the start, the old file kept beside | at the start, the banks' file kept as `hotbar.json.v1` | The merge happens once and the file says what the bar shows; the merge drops the banks' names, the kept file has them for a downgrade or for the user (an older Cogpit moves a format-2 file aside as unreadable and starts with an empty hotbar) |
| A limit to the tiles | 12 (F1–F12); 144 (twelve banks of twelve, so every old file fits); none | none; the file read stays bounded at 1 MiB, as every preference file | The owner: "beliebig gefüllt"; a tile is one per context, and only a context a kubeconfig source offers can be pinned |
| ⇧F1–⇧F12 | the same as F1–F12; tiles 13 to 24; no hotbar key | no hotbar key, passed on as any key | A habit of the banks' time should not open a cluster unexpectedly; a key for the tiles past twelve can come when someone asks |
| `ui_state`'s shape | the list itself (`hotbar: [...]`); an object with one field (`hotbar: {clusters: [...]}`) | the object | The tiles' field keeps its name, and a later field does not change the shape again |
| How the carried tile is drawn | the tile itself moved inside the bar; a copy in a layer over the whole window | a copy in a layer of the shell's root, above the window's content and below the tooltips | The bar's scroll would cut the tile at its 64-point edge, which the pointer leaves sideways easily; the copy carries its own lifted look and takes the pointer's hover, so nothing under it lights up |
| The lifted look | the tile as it is; scaled; scaled on a card with a shadow | 1.08 times the tile on a card of the bar's surface with a 1-point border and a drop shadow (Fyne 2.8's `canvas.Shadow`), the tile's tint at the hover's strength, its dot drawn without a target | The tile alone is translucent and unreadable over the navigator's text; scale and shadow are the common "picked up" cue (the Dock, Launchpad) |
| What stays where the tile goes | nothing (a gap); the tile faded; an outline | the outline of the tile's square in its colour at about 44% | The owner: the others arrange themselves around it; the outline shows where it lands while they slide |
| Which place a drop takes | R2's gap under the pointer between two tiles; the slot nearest the ghost's top, counted by the tiles' fixed pitch | the slot nearest the ghost's top | A rule that reads the tiles' drawn places flips back and forth while they slide; the fixed pitch does not, and the eye compares the ghost, not the pointer, with the slots |
| How the tiles slide | a Fyne position animation per tile; one animation per change moving every tile by its offset | one `fyne.Animation` per change, eased out, each tile's offset from its new place shrinking to nothing; a change mid-slide starts from where the tiles are drawn | The tiles move in step, and a fast drag stays continuous |
| Durations | 100 to 300 ms | the slide and the glide 150 ms, the lift 90 ms | Short enough that a fast drag never waits for the tiles, long enough to see where they go |
| Where a drop counts as on the bar | the bar's rectangle; with a margin | the tiles' area, and up to half a tile right of the bar | A drag that drifts a little into the navigator still drops; further out the tiles slide back, so the user sees before the drop that it moves nothing |
| The order between the drop and the engine's answer | the bar's old order until the hotbar arrives; the dropped order kept | the dropped order kept until the bar shows a hotbar after the move's answer; a failed move slides the tiles back and shows the reason | No flicker between the drop and the engine's state |
| The bar's own scrolling while dragging | none (the wheel, R2's); near the edges | within half a tile of the top or bottom edge of a bar whose tiles do not fit, up to 14 points per 16 ms (about 870 points a second), a quarter of that at the zone's inner border | An unbounded hotbar needs it; the speed grows with the depth into the zone, so a slow approach scrolls slowly |
| Reduce motion | slower animations; none | none: the tiles and the ghost jump, no lift | What the setting asks for, read as the connection dots read it ([`conndot.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/conndot.go)); since 2026-10-20 macOS's or Cogpit's own preference ([D-107](#d-107-the-navigator-slides-and-reduce-motion)) |
| The table header's column drag ([`columnorder.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/columnorder.go)) | the same carry; unchanged | unchanged, noted | The owner did not ask; the plan's note |

**Not verified:** the drag in a real window (the feel, the frame rate on the owner's Mac, Fyne's
drop shadow in the GL painter; the renders are the software painter's), a trackpad's drag, Windows
and Linux; the merge of the owner's own `hotbar.json` (tested with files of the format).

## D-84: Undo and redo in the YAML editor

**The owner's finding WF9 (walk of 2026-10-17, verbatim):** "Die Funktion cmd+z funktioniert
nicht. Ich [kann] versehentliche Vorgänge nicht rückgängig machen wie ich es gewohnt bin."

**The cause (verified 2026-10-17):** Cogpit's YAML editor ([`yamlview.View`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/yamlview/yamlview.go):
the Edit, Create resource, Helm Upgrade and Helm Install tabs, a Helm release's values, a Config
Map's and a Secret's values in the drawer) handled copy, cut, paste, select all and the navigation
shortcuts and had no undo. Fyne 2.8.2's desktop driver delivers ⌘Z to the focused widget as
`fyne.ShortcutUndo`, ⌘Y as `fyne.ShortcutRedo` and ⇧⌘Z as a `desktop.CustomShortcut` (Ctrl
instead of ⌘ on Windows and Linux; read in `internal/driver/glfw/window.go`, `triggersShortcut`),
and the editor dropped all three. The Edit tab's Undo Revert undoes a Revert only. Fyne's own text
fields (`widget.Entry`: the search fields, dialogs' and Preferences' fields, a drawer's new key name)
keep an undo stack of their own: ⌘Z and ⌘Y work in them, Cogpit's wrappers passing the shortcuts on;
⇧⌘Z does nothing there (verified on Fyne's test driver).

**Built 2026-10-17 evening** (the lead's agent "editor"): an undo and redo history in the editor,
the lead's decisions below, open to revision.

- **The history** ([`yamlview/history.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/yamlview/history.go)): every
  edit is one replacement, the text at a position and what replaced it, with the caret and the
  selection before and after. ⌘Z undoes, ⇧⌘Z and ⌘Y redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y on
  Windows and Linux). An undo or a redo is an edit like typing: `OnChanged` follows, so an Edit or
  Create tab sends the text to the engine after the typing pause and the drawer keeps a Config
  Map's values as it does after typing.
- **Text set from outside clears it** (`SetText`, and `UpdateText` with a different text): an object
  loaded, the object as stored after Apply, Revert and Undo Revert, a draft restored, a template
  chosen, an agent's text, the cache's newer value in an unedited drawer editor. An unchanged text
  keeps it.
- **⌘Z after a Revert** in an Edit tab is Undo Revert while the tab offers it (the editor's
  `OnNothingToUndo`, [`editortab_revert.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/editortab_revert.go)).
- **A Secret's values:** the history lives in the editor widget's memory only and goes when the
  drawer moves to another object or closes (`secData.close`); the values typed are kept in the
  window's memory as before (D-59) and come back without it
  ([credentials](../security/credentials.md#secret-values-edited-in-the-drawer)).
- Tests: `TestUndoTypingRun`, `TestTypingRunBreaks`, `TestUndoDeletions`,
  `TestUndoRestoresTheSelection`, `TestUndoPasteCutAndIndent`, `TestAnEditAfterUndoDropsTheRedo`,
  `TestTextFromOutsideClearsTheHistory`, `TestUndoReadOnlyAndNothingToUndo`, `TestHistoryBounds`,
  `TestUndoRedoRoundTrip` (random edits, undos and redos, then everything undone to the first text
  and redone to the last; 500 seeds tried once, 50 kept) in
  [`yamlview/history_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/yamlview/history_test.go);
  `TestEditTabUndoShortcuts`, `TestSecretDrawerKeepsUnsavedInMemory` in the window.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-17 evening), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| What one ⌘Z takes back while typing | a character; a word (Fyne's `widget.Entry`; Monaco, Lens's editor, inferred, not captured); the run of typing | the run, ended by a pause of a second, a caret move (a key, a click, a selection, the find widget), the focus leaving, a new line or an edit of another kind; a new line starts the next run, so one ⌘Z takes back a line typed with its line break | A macOS text view takes back the typing run (TextEdit, from use, not measured), which the owner expects ("wie ich es gewohnt bin"); the pause keeps one ⌘Z from taking back minutes of typing; a line is YAML's unit |
| The pause, and a run without one | 0.5 s (CodeMirror's and ProseMirror's default); 1 s; 2 s; a run unbounded or bounded | 1 s; a run also ends at 4 KiB of text | Half a second splits a slow typist's words into steps; two seconds lets a whole paragraph typed at a stretch go at once. Nobody types 4 KiB without a pause of a second; the bound keeps what a keystroke adds to its run a bounded copy, for a key held down for minutes too. Measured on the owner's Mac (Apple M1 Ultra, 20 cores; 50,000 operations, three runs each): a keystroke in the 5 MB document 15.2 µs before, 15.4 µs with the history (`BenchmarkKeystrokeLayout5MB`, P8's budget 16 ms); a new line 40.4 µs before, 43.8 µs with it (`BenchmarkNewlineLayout5MB`, a step each, the oldest dropped at the cap) |
| Deletions at the caret | each Backspace a step; a run | consecutive Backspaces one step (⌥⌫ and Backspace in the indentation among them), consecutive forward Deletes another, with the same pause | A held or repeated Backspace is one act, as typing is |
| A selection deleted or typed over, a paste, a cut, an indentation, a replacement | merged with the typing around them; a step each | a step each: a deleted selection (Backspace, Delete, ⌥⌫, Cut), a paste, Tab and ⇧Tab on a selection, the find widget's Replace and Replace all (one step for every match); typing over a selection is one step with the selection it replaced, the run going on | Each is one act the user takes back as one, and the most likely to be a mistake |
| The caret and the selection | the caret only; both | an undo restores the caret and the selection the step found, a redo those it left | A deleted selection comes back selected, as in macOS's text views: the user sees what came back |
| The cap | none (Fyne's `widget.Entry`, AppKit's undo manager by default); a number of steps; steps and bytes | the newest 1,000 steps and at most 32 MiB of text between them, the oldest dropped first; the newest step always kept, however large | The editor holds documents of 5 MB (S4): replacing one whole twice takes 20 MB, a thousand typing runs a few kilobytes; a select-all and delete of a large document must stay undoable |
| Text set from outside (see above) | keep the history; record the new text as a step; clear it | clear it, an unchanged text keeping it | The steps describe the old text. Recorded as a step, a Revert could be undone by ⌘Z with the older text now based on the newer version: Save would show the other party's change as the user's own lines without the stale warning, and Apply would overwrite it without the conflict ("never surprise a cluster"). Undo Revert brings the version back with the text |
| ⌘Z right after a Revert | nothing, the history being empty; Undo Revert | Undo Revert, while the tab offers it | The user's ⌘Z after a Revert clicked by mistake brings the text back, safely |
| The drawer's Revert of a Config Map's or a Secret's values | as the Edit tab's | clears each reverted editor's history; the drawer's Revert has no undo of its own, as before | Its base moves to the newest version as the Edit tab's does; an undo of it is a change of D-55 and D-59 not made here (open) |
| A command for agents | `editor.undo` and `editor.redo` in the engine; the widget's | the widget's: no command, no MCP tool | Undo and redo change the widget's text as typing, copy and paste do, none of which is a command (`TestCopyHasNoCommand`); the text reaches the engine as typing does. Agents set a text whole (`editor.setText`); a history in the engine would need every keystroke there, which holds the text only after a typing pause |
| A Secret's values in the history | as in any editor; memory only, dropped with the drawer | memory only, never on disk, in a draft, in `ui_state`, a log or the audit log, dropped when the drawer moves away or closes | AGENTS.md rule 9; the history holds every value typed, those deleted again too, and the kept values need none of it |
| An Edit menu with Undo and Redo | add one; none | none | Cogpit's main menu has none, Fyne 2.8.2 adds none on macOS (read in `menu_darwin.go`), GLFW's menu bar has the application and Window menus only; a new top-level menu is the owner's call, and its items would have to reach whichever widget has the focus. The keys go to the focused widget without one |
| ⇧⌘Z in Fyne's own text fields | a wrapper type for every field; leave them | leave them: ⌘Z and ⌘Y work there | Every field would need a type of its own; Fyne's entry ignores the custom shortcut ⇧⌘Z arrives as |

**Not verified:** the keys in a real window (Fyne's mapping read in its source and its test driver,
not pressed); Windows and Linux; how Lens's editor groups its undo steps (not captured).

The kind as the lists write it ("Config Map", was "ConfigMap") |

(since 2026-10-19 a pill "1 key removed" beside Save, D-100), "Saved 1 value at 14:02:05", an Edit tab "Config Map walk-cm · loaded at 14:02:05", "Changed on the cluster since your edits began: …"; the number in no window text, the draft notice included; it stays in the engine's results (`baseResourceVersion`), for agents, the CLI, the audit log and drafts on disk | The user needs to know whether the object moved since the edit began, which every conflict text says; the counter says nothing more to a person. ## D-86: The order of an object's YAML

**The owner's finding WF15 (walk of 2026-10-18, verbatim), on the Edit tab of a Config Map:** "Ich
mag die Formatierung vom Editor nicht. Ich will mindestens folgende Reihenfolge: apiVersion, kind,
metadata, metadata.name, metadata.namespace. So wie auch jedes Manifest in den Kubernetes-Docs
dokumentiert ist. Ich weiß, ein YAML hat keine Reihenfolge und das ist wahrscheinlich einfach
alphabetisch, aber es sieht einfach unschön aus. Das gilt für alle Kubernetes-Objekte."

**The cause (verified):** every object Cogpit showed as YAML went through `sigs.k8s.io/yaml`'s
`Marshal`, which sorts every map's keys: `apiVersion`, `data`, `kind`, `metadata` with
`creationTimestamp` before `name`.

**Built 2026-10-18** (the lead): [`model.ObjectYAML`](../../internal/model/objectyaml.go) writes an
object in the order the Kubernetes docs write a manifest, everywhere Cogpit shows an object's YAML:
the Edit tab (`EditableYAML`), the drawer's YAML tab, a Secret's YAML in the window, what agents read
of a manifest with credentials withheld (`agentview.go`) and the audit log's redacted manifests. The
lead's decisions, open to revision:

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The top level | apiVersion, kind, metadata, then the rest sorted; the rest by a list per kind (spec, data, type…) | **apiVersion, kind, metadata**, then the body's fields sorted, **status last** | The owner's three, and status last as the docs and `kubectl` users read it; a list per kind would have to know every custom resource |
| metadata | name, namespace, then sorted; the ObjectMeta order | **name, generateName, namespace, labels, annotations**, then the rest sorted (creationTimestamp, resourceVersion, uid…) | What a person reads first; what the server sets after it |
| Below that | sorted; the server's order | sorted, as before | A map's order below the top is not something anyone asked for, and sorted is stable |
| How | yaml.v3's node API; each top-level field marshalled on its own by `sigs.k8s.io/yaml` and joined (metadata's fields two spaces in) | **each field on its own by `sigs.k8s.io/yaml`** | yaml.v3 writes YAML 1.2: an annotation "on" or "yes" unquoted would turn into a boolean when the text is parsed (and applied) again; field by field the quoting is exactly the old one. Empty lines of a block scalar stay empty (`TestObjectYAMLRoundTrip`: the text parses to the same object for strings like "on", "0x1f", "~", block scalars with empty lines and leading blanks) |
| Drafts, "edited" and Revert | compare objects; compare texts | texts, as before: the base text and the text shown come from the same function | A draft kept before this change holds the alphabetical order: restored, its diff shows the moved lines too; applying it writes the same object |

The Create tab's templates already start with apiVersion, kind and metadata (checked).
Tests: `TestObjectYAMLOrder`, `TestObjectYAMLRoundTrip`.

**What it does not cover:** Lens's own order (inferred: the API server's JSON order, kind and
apiVersion first; not captured); Helm's values and manifests (a release's values are the user's
own text, shown as Helm returns them).
