## D-89: How a chart's line is drawn

**The owner's finding WF23 (walk of 2026-10-18, on a test cluster's node, verbatim):** "Die Linie
des Graphen sieht nicht so schick aus. Es scheint, als wäre sie an manchen Stellen dünner als an
anderen Stellen."

**The cause (verified 2026-10-18):** every chart (a pod's, each container's and a node's in the
drawer, the cluster Overview's three) drew a series as separate `canvas.Line` segments, one per
pair of points, 1.5 units wide. Each segment is antialiased on its own, at fractional positions,
and nothing joins it to the next: Fyne's GL painter draws each as a quad of its own, its software
painter (the test renders) rasterises each with butt ends (`painter.DrawLine`), so the joints
overlap or notch and the stroke's apparent width changes with the slope and where the joints fall.
Measured on a line of 40 points at fractional positions, as each pixel column's coverage against
the width across the slope (width × √(1+m²)): the separate segments 1.05 to 1.43 of it at 1× and
0.82 to 1.32 at 2×; one path 0.90 to 1.16 at both (what is left is a column cutting a round join
at a peak).

**Built 2026-10-18** (the lead's agent "charts"), the lead's decisions below, open to revision:

- **One path per run of points** ([`chartpath.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/chartpath.go)): each
  run of a series' points (a line between gaps, `seriesRuns`) is one stroke with round joins and
  round caps, 1.5 units wide, rasterised by rasterx into a `canvas.Raster` at the window's pixel
  size, so it is as thick on a slope as on the flat and as crisp at 2× as at 1×. A point alone
  stays a dot.
- **The fill is the same path** ([`chartfill.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/chartfill.go)): the run's
  points closed along zero, filled antialiased in a second raster, so its top edge lies exactly
  under the line. The order stays: the fills, the event markers, the reference lines, the lines,
  the hover's overlay.
- **Two layers a chart keeps** (`chartLayer`): the fills' and the lines', each with its raster
  object, its image and its scanner, redrawn into the same image while the size stays; a poll
  allocates nothing of the plot's size.
- **The hover repaints its overlay only** (`refreshOverlay`,
  [`chart_hover.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/chart_hover.go)): a refresh of the whole chart drops
  the textures of every object in it (read in Fyne's `common.Canvas.FreeDirtyTextures`), so each
  pointer move redrew the fills (and would have redrawn the lines); now the overlay's old and new
  objects are refreshed and the layers stay.
- Tests: `TestChartLineKeepsItsWidth` (every column of a 40-point line within the width across its
  slope, at 1× and at 2×; the separate segments fail it), `TestChartLayerReusesItsImage`,
  `TestChartFillsUnderTheSeries`, `TestReopenedDrawerChartBreaksAtTheGap` (two paths of 80
  points), `TestChartDrawsWhatItIsGiven`; the drawers' and the Overview's renders.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-18), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| How the line is drawn | (a) a stroke rasterised by rasterx into a `canvas.Raster` at the pixel size; (b) an SVG path in a `canvas.Image`, which Fyne renders with oksvg at the screen's scale; (c) Fyne 2.8's `ArbitraryPolygon` or `BezierCurve`; (d) the segments kept, a dot at each joint | (a) | rasterx is in the module graph already (Fyne's own rasteriser, a direct dependency for the chart icons since H-88): no `go.mod` change. (b) needs a new SVG text at every poll, parsed again on the main goroutine, and Fyne caches a rendered SVG by its resource's name, so a name per poll fills the cache and one name per chart needs its own invalidation. (c) `ArbitraryPolygon` takes 16 points at most and `BezierCurve` one segment: the joints stay. (d) dots thicken the joints on a 1× screen, and GL still antialiases each quad alone |
| The width | 1.5 units as before; 2 | 1.5 | The owner found it uneven, not thin; 3 pixels on a 2× screen |
| Joins and ends | miter, bevel, round | round joins, round ends | A metrics line has sharp peaks: a miter spikes past them, a bevel flattens them; round reads as one line |
| The fill | a raster per run with a test per pixel (as before); a filled path | a filled path, every series' in one layer | Antialiased like the line, its edge the line's own path, one texture for every run; the per-pixel test was not antialiased and drew a stair under a slope |
| The images | a new image at every draw; one kept per layer | kept per layer while the size stays | Fyne copies a raster's image into a texture at once and keeps nothing of it (read in `painter/gl/texture.go` and `painter/software/draw.go`), so reusing it is safe; a resize or a poll then costs no allocation of the plot's size |
| Where a layer sits | at the plot's fractional position; rounded out to whole units | whole units, the line's layer 3 units wider than the plot | Whole units are whole pixels at 1× and 2×, so the raster's pixels meet the screen's; the margin keeps the stroke and its ends at the plot's edge |

**Not verified:** a real window (Fyne's GL painter) at 1× and 2×: the renders are the software
painter's at scale 1 and 2, and GL draws the same image as a texture of its pixel size (read in its
source, not seen). At a fractional scale (1.25, 1.5 on Windows and Linux) the layer's origin, rounded
to whole units, may lie up to half a pixel off the grid's lines.

## D-90: A node's disks: a usage bar per real filesystem

**The owner's finding WF26 (walk of 2026-10-18, a test cluster's node drawer, verbatim):** "Disk
Usage hier wieder als Text, besser als kleine Visualisierung mit Tooltip für genaue Details. Hat
der Server vielleicht auch weitere Blockstorages, die wir einblenden sollten? Mein Main-Cluster hat
zum Beispiel eine SSD an /data gemountet. Bekommen wir diese Information vielleicht einfach
zusammen und können, wenn mehrere Blockstorage verfügbar und gemountet, auch übersichtlich
dargestellt?" He saw "Disk (/): 50.5 GiB of 122.9 GiB used (41%)".

**What was there (verified 2026-10-18):** [D-43](#d-43-where-the-nodes-disk-comes-from)'s root
filesystem alone (`mountpoint="/",fstype!="rootfs"`), a line of text under the node's chart.
node-exporter reports every filesystem the host mounts, by `mountpoint`, `device` and `fstype`.
**What it reports, read only on 2026-10-18:** on the owner's test cluster (kube-prometheus-stack's
exporter, four nodes; its names not recorded here) `/` (ext4 on a disk partition), `/boot` (ext4),
`/boot/efi` (vfat), `/run` and `/run/lock` (tmpfs) on each node, the kubelet's mounts already left
out by that chart's exporter flags; on the kind cluster (the `prometheus` chart's exporter) `/var`
and three files under `/etc` bind-mounted from the same disk, `/run`, `/tmp` and a systemd
credentials tmpfs. The owner's main cluster with its `/data` was not available to read: the
fixtures are made up, shaped like these.

**Built 2026-10-18** (the lead's agent "charts"), the lead's decisions below, open to revision:

- **One query per poll, as before, for every node's real filesystems**
  ([`metrics/diskfs.go`](../../internal/metrics/diskfs.go)): both gauges `max by (node, instance,
  device, fstype, mountpoint)`, the types and mountpoints that do not count left out in the selector
  (`fstype!~…,mountpoint!~…`) and again in Go on the answer. The query's text was run read-only
  against the test cluster's Prometheus and kind's: it parses, and answers `/` alone for each node
  of the first and `/var` alone on kind.
- **The model** ([`model/usage.go`](../../internal/model/usage.go)): `NodeDisk.Filesystems`, each a
  `NodeFilesystem` (mountpoint, device, type, used and size bytes; free is the size less the used),
  the root first, then by mountpoint; `NodeDisk.Mountpoint`, `UsedBytes` and `SizeBytes` are the
  fullest of them.
- **The drawer** ([`metricsdisk.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/metricsdisk.go)): under the node's
  chart a row per filesystem: "Disk" before the first, the mountpoint, a small usage bar in the
  table's bar colours (the accent, the warning colour from 80 %, the error colour from 90 %;
  `model.UsageBarStatus`) and the share; each row's tooltip "/data · /dev/sdb1 · xfs", "Used 172.0
  GiB of 200.0 GiB (86%)", "Free 28.0 GiB". Without a disk, the reason as before, muted, one line.
- **The Nodes list's Disk column shows the fullest filesystem**, its bar's tooltip naming it ("/data
  · 172.0 GiB of 200.0 GiB (86%)"), the header's tooltip "Disk: the fullest of the node's
  filesystems as node-exporter reports them, read through Prometheus (…)". On kind the column
  shows `/var` since (before: empty, no `/` series there).
- **The demo cluster** ([`demo/disks.go`](../../internal/demo/disks.go), development builds only)
  makes up every node's disks: a root on each, `/data` on about half the workers, `/srv/backup` on a
  few; its metrics provider is a disk provider, and `metrics.Fixed` lets the hub know it before
  its first poll (`Hub.DisksPossible`), so the demo's Nodes list shows the Disk column (before:
  empty) and a worker's drawer more than one bar.
- **Agents** read the column's cell, the fullest filesystem with its mountpoint in the detail,
  through `view.rows`; the drawer's per-filesystem rows are in no tool's answer (not built).
- Tests: `TestNodeDisksFromNodeExporter` (the query, the root of each node), `TestNodeDiskFilesystems`
  (a node shaped like a real one: `/`, `/data`, `/srv/backup` kept; `/boot`, `/boot/efi`, `/run`,
  `/run/lock`, a pod's volume, a container's layers, a file under `/etc` and the root's device
  bind-mounted at `/var/lib/kubelet` left out; the fullest), `TestNodeDiskCell`,
  `TestNodeDrawerShowsTheDisk` (rows, colours, aligned bars, fills, the tooltip, the note),
  `TestNodesListDrawsUsageBars`, `TestDemoDisks`, `TestNodesListDiskBudget` (still one disk query
  per poll); renders `node_drawer_disk_*.png` and the demo's `TestRenderDemoNodeDisks`.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-18), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which filesystems count | every series node-exporter reports; only block devices (`device` under `/dev/`); every one but those that hold none of the node's own data | the last: not a filesystem in memory or of the kernel (tmpfs, ramfs, devtmpfs, proc, sysfs, cgroup, nsfs, …), not a container's layers (overlay) or an image (squashfs, erofs, iso9660), not under `/boot`, `/dev`, `/proc`, `/run`, `/sys`, `/snap`, not a file under `/etc`, not under `/var/lib/kubelet/`, `/var/lib/docker/`, `/var/lib/containerd/`, `/var/lib/containers/`, `/var/lib/rancher/` | Every series shows `/run` and, with node-exporter's defaults, a tmpfs per pod's volume (hundreds on a busy node). Block devices alone would leave out a network filesystem the host mounts for its data, and LVM and ZFS devices do not all sit under `/dev/`. A disk mounted at `/var/lib/kubelet` or `/var/lib/containerd` itself counts: it is where the kubelet's disk pressure is measured |
| `/boot` and `/boot/efi` | show them; leave them out | leave them out | They are the firmware's and the boot loader's, a few hundred MiB sized by the installer, on every node; two more bars per node that say nothing about the cluster's data. A `/boot` that fills up stops kernel updates, which node-exporter's own alert rules watch |
| A device mounted twice (a bind mount, a btrfs subvolume) | a bar each; one | one, at `/` when it is the root, else at its shortest mountpoint | The same space twice reads as twice the disk |
| Order | by mountpoint; by share; root first, then by mountpoint | root first, then by mountpoint | The owner's "root first, then the others"; an order that stays put across polls |
| The Nodes list's Disk column | (a) the root, as D-43 and Lens; (b) the fullest; (c) the root's share with the fullest's colour | (b), the mountpoint in the bar's tooltip | The column answers which node runs out of disk; a `/data` at 95 % under a root at 40 % would stay unseen in the list with (a), and sorting by Disk finds the fullest disks with (b). (c) shows a number and a colour of two different disks. On a node with one real filesystem, the usual case, (a) and (b) are the same |
| The drawer's look | a line of text per filesystem (as before); a bar per filesystem with the numbers in a tooltip | the bars, the share beside each, the numbers in the tooltip | The owner's words; the bars' colours and their thresholds are the lists', so a warning reads the same everywhere |
| Where the rules live | the query only; Go only; both | both, from the same text | The query keeps the answer small where the exporter excludes nothing; Go keeps the same filesystems out of an answer from a store that reads the expressions differently, and is what the tests check |
| The query's cost | one query for every node (as before); one per node | one for every node, per poll at the list's 60 s | The brief's one query per node is met by one for all of them, and no poll beyond today's |

**Not verified:** the owner's main cluster's `/data` (not available; the fixtures are made up,
shaped like the test cluster's answer); an exporter with node-exporter's own defaults on a node
with many pods (the rules were checked on synthetic series of such mounts); a real window.

## D-91: The Kubernetes version and upstream end of life

**The owner's finding WF30 (walk of 2026-10-18, W55, verbatim):** "Außerdem hätte ich hier gerne
die Angabe, welche API-Version dieser Cluster nutzt. Die API-Version kann ja zu den Nodes
(kubelet-version) unterschiedlich sein. Ich will dort auch ein Warning-Symbol haben, wenn die
Version EOL ist. Auch an den Nodes soll es eine Warning geben, wenn ein Node in einer Version
betrieben wird, die bereits EOL ist. Schön wäre diesbezüglich als Tooltip zur API-Version in diesem
Feld die Angabe, wie lange die Version noch hat, bevor sie EOL wird. Wie wir an diese Infos kommen,
musst du bitte erst noch recherchieren."

**The research (2026-10-18, a research agent of the lead's; its sources in `plan/`, not re-checked
by the lead):** upstream publishes the dates machine-readable in `kubernetes/website`:
`data/releases/schedule.yaml` (the maintained minors: release day, maintenance mode, end of life)
and `data/releases/eol.yaml` (the ended minors: end of life, final patch), kept by
`schedule-builder`, changed about monthly, CC BY 4.0; a minor is supported about 14 months (12 and
2 of maintenance mode), the newest three; a final end of life can slip weeks against the plan.
endoflife.date mirrors them (MIT, a third-party host, one data error seen). Managed services (EKS,
GKE, AKS, STACKIT SKE) support minors longer or shorter, their dates behind their own APIs or
pages; nothing in a cluster says when its version ends. The version skew policy: a kubelet never
newer than the API server, at most three minors older (two for a kubelet older than 1.25).

**The owner's decisions (2026-10-18, verbatim):** "Woher die EOL-Daten kommen: gerne aus
gepflegter Tabelle, aber mit Estimation, falls unsere Tabelle outdated ist. Kubernetes released
doch relativ regelmäßig oder, so dass eine offline Estimation möglich wäre? Können wir den Fetch in
der Build-Pipeline zur Buildtime machen und damit automatisch pflegen? Es zählen nur die
offiziellen Upstream-Termine. Termine von Drittanbietern wie STACKIT sind für uns irrelevant." So:
(1) a table built into each release, fetched from upstream's two files at build time, never at run
time (the app makes no new connection); an offline estimate where the table has no date;
(2) upstream's dates only: no distribution's table, no distribution detected.

**Built 2026-10-18** (the lead's agent "eol"), with the lead's decisions below, open to revision.
Lens shows neither ([beyond Lens › Everyday use](../parity/beyond-lens.md#everyday-use)).

- **The table** ([`internal/model/k8seol`](../../internal/model/k8seol/k8seol.go), L0, no I/O):
  [`releases.json`](../../internal/model/k8seol/releases.json) embedded with `go:embed`, one minor a
  line (1.2 to 1.37 on 2026-10-18; the ended minors' end of life and final patch, the maintained
  ones' release day, maintenance mode and end of life), its source and the day it was fetched.
  `SupportOf(version)` reads a minor from a gitVersion (`v1.34.2-gke.1234`, `v1.31.4+k3s1`), and
  says its days, `StateAt(now)` supported, maintenance, endOfLife or unknown on now's day in now's
  zone (the end of life's day itself still supported), `DaysLeft`, and the texts the window and
  agents show; `KubeletSkew` the skew policy's verdict. A version that holds no minor of
  Kubernetes 1 is unknown; a minor older than the table's oldest ended "before" the oldest's day.
- **The estimate** for a minor newer than the table: its release four months per minor after the
  table's newest (the first of that month), its end of life the 28th of the month fourteen months
  after its release month, maintenance mode two months before; shown as "about …, estimated: this
  Cogpit's table ends at 1.37". Checked against upstream's own dates since 1.19
  (`TestEstimateRuleAgainstUpstream`, release days from the project's GitHub releases): from a
  minor's own release month the rule gives 13 of 19 ends of life exactly, five within 18 days
  (1.27 +18, 1.30 +17, 1.31 +14, 1.28 −6, 1.34 −1, upstream later or earlier), 1.22 41 days early
  (upstream extended it); estimated one minor ahead of a known one, 10 of 18 exact, at most 41 days
  early and 31 days late (1.25 from 1.24: 1.24 came five months after 1.23, 1.25 three after 1.24);
  two and three ahead −41 to +29 and −41 to +12. It only matters for a build older than the table's
  newest minor, about a year.
- **The generator** ([`hack/k8seol`](../../hack/k8seol/main.go), `make k8s-eol`): downloads both
  files from `raw.githubusercontent.com/kubernetes/website/main/data/releases/`, merges them and
  checks the table (dates parse; the minors follow one another without a gap; the ends of life in
  their order, each 12 to 18 months after its release; the newest with a release day), then against
  the committed one (no minor lost, the newest not older, no known minor's end of life moved by more
  than 120 days); prints what changed and writes the file. `-fallback`: a failed download or check
  keeps the committed table, warns and exits 0.
- **The release pipeline** ([`build.yml`](../../.github/workflows/build.yml), the job
  "Cogpit.app (macOS arm64)") runs `make k8s-eol K8SEOL_FLAGS=-fallback` before `make dist-app`:
  every release carries the table of its day, or the committed one when GitHub fails
  ([releasing › the Kubernetes release table](releasing.md#the-kubernetes-release-table)). The data
  is upstream's and unreviewed in that job: [H-130](../security/updates.md#h-130-the-releases-kubernetes-release-table-is-fetched-unreviewed),
  an accepted risk (the owner, 2026-10-19 afternoon: "lassen"; the release notes' diff not wanted for now).
  [ATTRIBUTION.md](../../ATTRIBUTION.md) names the source (CC BY 4.0).
- **The engine** ([`engine/k8sversion.go`](../../internal/engine/k8sversion.go)): the API server's
  version is the one each connect read (`cluster.Conn.ServerVersion()`, its `GET /version`; the demo
  cluster's `v1.36.1` from `demo.ServerVersion`, `Backend.Version`): no request of its own. Every
  connect (the window's, one in the background, a reconnect's) records it (`learnVersion`) and puts
  Cogpit's own overlay on the backend (`overlays.putOwn`, after the integrations'; D-79's
  mechanism): the Nodes list's Version cell merged with the kubelet's colour, ⚠ and tooltip
  (`model.Cell.Tip`, new; `mergeCell` joins tooltips, and an overlay cell in parts redraws the
  cell). `UIState.ClusterVersion` is the shown cluster's version and support while it is live,
  derived after every change; `ui_state` assesses it again as of the read. The node drawer's
  Kubelet version takes the colour, "Upstream support" and, outside the skew policy, "Version skew"
  follow it (`MarkKubeletVersion`). `Options.K8sReleases` lets tests pass a table of their own.
- **Agents** read `ui_state`'s `clusterVersion` (version, minor, released, maintenanceFrom,
  endOfLife, estimated, before, tableNewest, tableFetched, state, daysLeft), `view_rows`' and
  `resources_list`'s `tips` (the tooltip of each cell that has one), `object_get`'s drawer items.
- **The window** ([`fyneui/clusterversion.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clusterversion.go)): the
  version on the navigator root's third line, under the user, while a version is known: muted while
  supported, amber (the pending colour) in maintenance mode, orange with "⚠" past the end of life;
  its tooltip "Upstream support until 28.06.2027 (253 days)", "…, maintenance mode since …",
  "Upstream end of life since 28.06.2026", then "Upstream dates as of <the table's day>"; dates in
  the computer's format (D-31), written as days, never moved into a zone. A list cell with a tooltip
  of its own shows it on hover (`tableview.go`).
- **Tests:** `TestEmbeddedTable`, `TestParseVersion`, `TestSupportOf`, `TestStateAtTheEdges`,
  `TestKubeletSkew`, `TestValidateRefuses`, `TestEstimateRuleAgainstUpstream`
  ([`k8seol_test.go`](../../internal/model/k8seol/k8seol_test.go)); `TestBuild`,
  `TestBuildRefuses`, `TestCompare`, `TestRun` (the generator, a test server, a failed download
  keeping the table; [`main_test.go`](../../hack/k8seol/main_test.go));
  `TestClusterVersionInUIState`, `TestNodesVersionCheck`, `TestNoVersionNoCheck`,
  `TestMergeCellTipAndParts` ([`k8sversion_test.go`](../../internal/engine/k8sversion_test.go)), the
  demo's version in `TestClusterConnectorContextsAndDemo`, `TestKindClusterVersion` (the kind cluster, [`k8sversion_kind_test.go`](../../internal/testkit/integration/k8sversion_kind_test.go)); `TestRootRowShowsTheClusterVersion`,
  `TestTableCellShowsItsTip` and the PNGs `navigator_version_*`, `nodes_versions_*`,
  `node_drawer_versions_*` ([`clusterversion_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clusterversion_test.go)).

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-18), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the table lives | in `model`; in `internal/kubectl` beside `MaxMinorSkew`; a new L0 package | `internal/model/k8seol`, L0, embedded | The engine, the window and both binaries read it and it does no I/O; L1 `kubectl` is the terminal's download. depguard's `**/internal/model/**` rule already holds it to L0: `.golangci.yml` needs no change |
| The file's format | upstream's YAML as fetched; a JSON of Cogpit's own | JSON of Cogpit's own, the fields Cogpit reads, one minor a line | A change is one line of the diff; the binaries parse it with `encoding/json`; a change of upstream's schema breaks the generator, which keeps the last good table, never the app |
| The generator's checks | parse only; the lead's three (dates, order, no minor lost); more | the three, plus no gap, ends of life in order, 12 to 18 months of support, the newest's release day, no known end of life moved by more than 120 days | Upstream moved ends of life by weeks (1.31 14 days, 1.22 41); a move of months or a support outside the policy's range is a broken or altered file, and every bound narrows what a changed file can do ([H-130](../security/updates.md#h-130-the-releases-kubernetes-release-table-is-fetched-unreviewed)) |
| A failed fetch at a release | fail the release; keep the committed table | keep it, with a warning on the run | The owner's design: GitHub's hiccup must not stop a release; the estimate covers a newer minor |
| Keeping the committed table fresh | a scheduled workflow committing to `main` (the lead's first design); by hand | `make k8s-eol` by hand, committed as `chore:` when it changed | A bot pushing to `main` is outward-facing and was not asked for; every release fetches its own table anyway, and the committed one only serves local builds; the tests carry their own tables, so a refresh moves no expectation |
| Where the release fetches it | the Makefile's `dist-app`; a step of its own before it | a step of its own in the app's job | `make dist-app` stays offline and reproducible locally; the step's log shows the table's changes; the job holds no secret |
| When support ends | on the end of life's day; the day after | the day after: the end of life's day is still supported ("today") | upstream's date is the last day of support; days counted in the Preferences' zone, the table's days written as they are |
| A softer mark before the end | none; the last 30 days; upstream's maintenance mode (two months) | maintenance mode: the version in amber (the pending colour), no ⚠ | upstream's own boundary (critical fixes only) instead of a number of Cogpit's; amber says "soon", the ⚠ stays "past" |
| The ⚠ | the warning column's icon (theme); the glyph | the glyph "⚠" after the version, in the status colour's run | it travels with the text into the CSV, agents' rows and the search; Fyne draws it from its emoji font, as the column drag's chip does |
| Where the root row shows the version | beside the user; after the name; a line of its own | a third line, under the user, while a version is known | at the navigator's default width (216 pt) both other places cut the name or the user (rendered: "prod-…", "alice@exampl…"); a disconnected cluster's row stays two lines |
| The nodes' mark | the warning column; the Version column | the Version column and the drawer's Kubelet version | the warning column says the node's health (conditions, Kyverno); an old kubelet is the version's matter, and the owner asked for it at the version |
| The skew (the lead's decision given with the brief) | none; the policy's kubelet rule | ⚠ on a kubelet newer than the API server or more than three minors older (two below 1.25), the tooltip naming which | the version skew policy's own rule, read from what the cache and the connection hold; kube-proxy and the control plane's components are not checked |
| How the rows get the marks | the kind profile (no clock, no API server version); a pass of the row cache; an overlay | Cogpit's own overlay (`overlays.putOwn`), merged into the Version column | the existing seam for cells a profile cannot know (D-79); the CSV, `view_rows` and `resources_list` see it as the window does; a row's overlaid copy is remade when the Node changes, at least every five minutes (the kubelet's status report), so a day passing shows within minutes |
| A cell's tooltip | in the text; a field `Tip` | `model.Cell.Tip`, shown on hover, joined by overlays, agents' `tips` | the text stays the version for sorting, search and the CSV; agents get the same sentences |
| Distributions | detect them (gitVersion, providerID) and say "upstream"; nothing | nothing, the tooltip says "Upstream" | the owner: only upstream's dates count |
| The demo cluster | no version; its kube-apiserver's | `v1.36.1`, its kube-apiserver image's tag | agents and renders see the line on the demo too; its kubelets (1.36.1, 1.35.5) are supported until 2027, so no ⚠ shows there |

**Verified against a real API server** (2026-10-18, `TestKindClusterVersion`, the kind cluster
`cogpit`, read only): its `v1.36.1` in `ui_state`'s `clusterVersion`, supported until 2027-06-28
(253 days), the node's tip "Upstream support until 2027-06-28 (253 days)" in `view_rows` and
`resources_list`, the drawer's Upstream support.

**Not verified:** a real window (offscreen renders only); a cluster whose API server is past its end
of life (the kind cluster runs 1.36.1); the release job's step (it runs at the next release); the
gitVersions of managed services beyond the parse tests; the table's refresh of a minor moving from
`schedule.yaml` to `eol.yaml` (1.34 on 2026-10-27).

## D-95: The window comes back where it was

**The owner's finding WF11 (2026-10-17, after the walk, verbatim):** "Ich habe festgestellt, dass
sich cogpit nicht die letzte eigene Position vor dem Schließen merkt und auch nicht wie groß es
skaliert war. Es öffnet immer gleich, ganz gleich wie es skaliert war und wo es auf dem Bildschirm
war als es geschlossen wurde. Das ist ein Makel."

**The cause (verified 2026-10-18):** `Run` set the window to 1440 × 900 at every start
(`w.Resize` in [`fyneui.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/fyneui.go)), and GLFW centred it (`[window
center]` when no position is asked for, GLFW 3.4's `cocoa_window.m`); nothing kept its size or place:
`workspace.json` ([D-41](#d-41-what-survives-a-restart)) keeps the tabs, the layout and the restore
plan, no frame. Fyne 2.8.2's `fyne.Window` has no position; its `desktop.Window` (since 2.8) has
`RequestPosition(x, y)`, which GLFW applies when it creates the window (`window_desktop.go`'s
`create`), and nothing reads a position back.

**Built 2026-10-18** (the lead's agent "window"), the lead's decisions below, open to revision.

- **At start** the window opens with its last size, on its last display at its last place, and in
  full screen if it was, whatever Preferences › App › Restore the last session says
  ([`windowplace.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/windowplace.go)). Before the window exists the
  kept frame is fitted to the displays (`placeFrame`) and given to Fyne as the content's size (the
  frame less the title bar GLFW's window starts with, over Fyne's canvas scale) and to GLFW as the
  content's top left (`RequestPosition`, `glfwPlacement`), so the window opens there without a
  jump; once it runs, after Cogpit's own title bar took its room, the frame is set exactly (no
  change when it is right already), full screen entered and the window followed
  ([`windowplace_darwin.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/windowplace_darwin.go),
  [`.m`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/windowplace_darwin.m)).
- **Kept** in `<user config dir>/Cogpit/window.json`, owner-only (0600 in a 0700 directory,
  replaced whole and atomically, `engine.WritePrivateFile`): the frame in AppKit's screen
  coordinates (points, origin at the primary display's bottom left), the display it was on (its id,
  name and frame then) and whether it was in full screen, with the frame it leaves full screen to.
  Written half a second after the last move, resize, change of display or of full screen (AppKit's
  notifications), and what is pending when Cogpit quits; nothing is written while nothing changed,
  so the first start leaves no file until the window is moved or resized. A file that does not load,
  or a newer Cogpit's, gives the first start's window and is replaced by the next change.
- **Fallbacks:** the kept display found by its id, else by its name when one display alone has it,
  the frame moved with the display's top left if the display is arranged elsewhere now; else the
  display whose visible area the frame overlaps most; the frame fitted into that display's visible
  area (without the menu bar and the Dock): clipped when larger, moved in when it hangs over an
  edge. A frame on no display (an unplugged one) gives the first start's window, 1440 × 900 in the
  middle of the primary display, clipped to it; the file keeps the old frame until the window
  moves, so with the display plugged in again the window goes back to it.
- **Full screen** is entered once Cogpit is the active app: measured on macOS 26, AppKit takes an
  inactive app's window into the full-screen style at `toggleFullScreen:` and then gives up on it;
  the kept full screen waits for `NSApplicationDidBecomeActiveNotification` and stays kept
  meanwhile. A transition AppKit gives up on (no did notification reaches anyone but the window's
  delegate, GLFW's) is recognised by the window's style every half second, at most 5 seconds.
- **Windows and Linux:** the canvas's size and full screen, kept when the window closes and given
  back at start through Fyne (`Resize`, `SetFullScreen`;
  [`windowplace_other.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/windowplace_other.go)); no position (below); a
  crash keeps the size of the start before. Type-checked for both, not run there.
- **Not engine state:** no command, no MCP tool, no `ui_state` field (below). A `--perf` run opens at
  1440 × 900 and keeps nothing.
- Tests: `TestPlaceFrame` (kept, on another display, unplugged, larger, over an edge, under the
  Dock, rearranged, an id changed, names not unique, off every display, nonsense), `TestGLFWPlacement`,
  `TestCanvasScaleFor`, `TestSizePlace`, `TestWindowPlaceKeeper`, `TestWindowPlaceKeeperUnreadable`
  in [`windowplace_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/windowplace_test.go); the AppKit side built
  with a native harness in a process of its own and run, CI's macOS job
  (`TestWindowPlaceFollowsTheWindow`, [`windowplace_darwin_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/windowplace_darwin_test.go),
  [`testdata/windowplace_harness.m`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/windowplace_harness.m)): the
  displays, GLFW's title bar, the exact frame, one report per move and resize, the frame before full
  screen kept through it, one observer however often installed, nothing after the close, full screen
  waiting for an inactive app. Once, not committed, on Fyne's real GLFW driver (macOS 26, the
  owner's Mac, a window in a test process of its own): a kept frame of 1000 × 700 at (300, 200)
  opened at exactly that frame before anything set it; a move was in the file half a second later; a
  frame on a display that is gone opened at 1440 × 932 (900 and macOS 26's 32-point title bar) in the
  middle of the primary display's visible area; full screen was refused while the process was not
  active and kept for the activation.

**The lead's decisions (2026-10-18), open to revision:**

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whether Restore the last session decides it | follow the preference (off by default); always | always | macOS apps come back where they were, and the owner calls the opposite a flaw. The frame names no cluster and sends no request, so what keeps the session behind the preference (D-69 item 8: never surprise a cluster) does not apply |
| Where it is kept | a field in `workspace.json`; AppKit's frame autosave (`setFrameAutosaveName:`, in the app's defaults, `~/Library/Preferences/io.guided-traffic.cogpit.plist`); a file of its own | `window.json` in Cogpit's configuration directory | The frame is the window's, not engine state: in `workspace.json` the engine would carry a field it never reads and an API for the window to set it, and that file's tabs follow the preference while the frame does not. AppKit's autosave keeps no full screen, has no rule of ours for a display that is gone, nothing on Windows and Linux, and tests could not use it without writing the defaults of their process in the developer's `~/Library/Preferences`; whether it holds against GLFW, which sets the window's size again at the end of its creation (Fyne's `create`), is not verified. A file of its own: tests give a path in a temporary directory, and none keeps nothing (`Options.WindowPlace`); it survives a reinstall as Cogpit's other files do (the app moved to the Trash leaves Application Support); deleting it is the reset |
| When it is written | at quit only; at every change; half a second after the last change, and what is pending at quit | the last | A crash ([D-11](#d-11-crash-stance)) loses at most the last half second, at quit only the whole run's place; every step of a drag or a live resize would write tens of times a second |
| Before or after the window shows | set the frame natively once the window runs; give Fyne the size and GLFW the position before it exists, and set the frame exactly once it runs | before, and exactly after | Set after, the window shows at 1440 × 900 in the middle and then jumps; before, it opened at the kept frame exactly (measured once, above). The exact frame after covers a rounding or a Fyne scale, and is no change otherwise |
| The display | the frame as kept, in global coordinates; the display by id, then by a unique name, the frame moved with its top left; else the display it overlaps most | the latter | Displays are rearranged in System Settings › Displays, and an external display's id can change with the port it is plugged into (inferred, not tried): the window stays on its display, at its place from the display's top left |
| A frame on no display | as kept (AppKit would leave the window where it cannot be reached); on the nearest display; the first start's window | the first start's: 1440 × 900 in the middle of the primary display, clipped to it | The owner's case ("ganz gleich … wo es auf dem Bildschirm war"): predictable; the old frame stays in the file, so the external display plugged in again brings the window back to it |
| A frame over its display's edge, or larger | as kept; clipped to the visible area and moved in | clipped and moved in, wholly onto one display | A title bar under the menu bar or behind the Dock cannot be grabbed. The cost: a window that overlapped the Dock comes back just above it, and one that spanned two displays comes back wholly on the one that had its larger part |
| A frame that is not Cogpit's | take it; the first start's window | under 320 × 200, a number not finite or beyond a million: the first start's | A hand-edited or damaged file must not hide the window |
| Full screen | not restored; at once; once the app is active | once the app is active | Measured: AppKit gives up on an inactive app's full screen; Cogpit started from the Finder or the Dock is active at once (not tried), one started from a terminal only once the user clicks it |
| Windows and Linux | size and position (Fyne's `RequestPosition` exists there); size and full screen | size and full screen, kept when the window closes | Fyne can ask for a position there but cannot read one back (no API; GLFW's position stays inside its driver), so there is no position to keep; nor are there AppKit's notifications to follow a change: the size is read from the canvas when the run ends |
| Agents | a `ui.window.*` command and a `ui_state` field; none | none | The frame is where the user's desktop has Cogpit, not what Cogpit shows: agents read and drive the window's state (AGENTS.md rule 2: view, filter, selection, drawer), and a window moved by an agent would be a surprise; the window is the only reader and writer of the file |
| Fyne's canvas scale | 1; as Fyne's driver computes it | as Fyne's driver: `FYNE_SCALE` unless empty or `auto`, else Fyne's scale setting, else 1, to a tenth | Fyne sizes the window in its units times the scale; with `FYNE_SCALE=2` and scale 1 assumed the window would open twice as large for a moment |
| The `--perf` run | keep the place; 1440 × 900 | 1440 × 900, nothing kept | The spike's and the gate's measurements were made at that size ([spike](spike-fyne.md)); a measurement at the user's last size would not compare |

**Not verified:** Cogpit's own window (no app launch: the logic, the AppKit side in a harness, and
Fyne's GLFW driver once in a window of a test process); full screen entered after the activation
(a harness started by a test is not activated under macOS 26's cooperative activation, and
`activateIgnoringOtherApps:` did not activate it); a kept frame on the second display of a real
two-display Mac (the geometry is a unit test); AppKit's frame autosave against GLFW (not built);
Windows and Linux in a real window (type-checked with `GOOS=linux` and `GOOS=windows`; its tests
run on Windows since 2026-10-21, D-111); Lens Desktop restoring its window (inferred, not captured:
[ui-parity › Layout](../parity/ui-parity.md#layout)). No security gap: the file holds a frame and a
display's name, owner-only.

## D-96: The service proxy's port spelled by its number first

**The owner's finding (2026-10-18 evening, verbatim):** "Gegen mgmt-p (pinniped) kann Lens die
Prometheus Metriken mit meinem Permission anzeigen, Cogpit kann es es nicht. Finde heraus wieso."

**The cause (verified on that cluster, read only, the owner's identity through Pinniped's
impersonation proxy):** the user's role grants `get` and `create` on `services/proxy` in
`monitoring` only for the `resourceNames` `kube-prometheus-prometheus:9090` and
`prometheus-operated:9090` (`kubectl auth can-i --list`). RBAC matches a service proxy request's
name `[scheme:]<service>[:<port>]` as the URL writes it: `…/kube-prometheus-prometheus:9090/proxy/…`
answered (Prometheus 3.15.0), `…:http-web`, `http:…:9090` and the bare name were refused
("decision made by impersonation-proxy.concierge.pinniped.dev", the impersonation proxy checking
the user's RBAC). Cogpit spelled the port by its name when the Service names it `http-web`
([`promdetect.go`](../../internal/metrics/promdetect.go) `pickPort`) and ended detection at the first
403, before `prometheus-operated:9090` was asked. Lens writes the number (its providers take the
Service's port number; the owner's Lens settings name `monitoring/prometheus-operated:9090`), and the
role was written for it.

**The owner's choice (2026-10-18, of three options):** "Nummer zuerst, dann Name" — over "only the
number" (a role granting only the name would stop working) and "leave the code, set the address"
(every cluster with such a role runs into it).

**Built 2026-10-18** (the lead's details, open to revision):
- Prometheus ([`promdetect.go`](../../internal/metrics/promdetect.go)) and Alertmanager
  ([`alerting/detect.go`](../../internal/alerting/detect.go), [`poller.go`](../../internal/alerting/poller.go)):
  each candidate carries its port's spellings, the number first, then the name (`Candidate.Ports`).
  A 403 or 401 under one spelling asks the next spelling, then the next candidate; a candidate that
  answers anything else under a spelling (found, not a Prometheus, no endpoints) is not asked under
  the other, which reaches the same server. Forbidden only when nothing answered, naming every
  refused target ("…:9090 nor …:http-web"). At most 3 candidates, so at most 6 probes.
- An address the user set is asked exactly as set.
- The target found keeps the spelling that answered: the status lines read
  `monitoring/kube-prometheus-prometheus:9090` where they read `…:http-web` before.
- The test fake's service proxy resolves a port's number and name to the same handler when it holds
  the Service, as the API server does (`FakeAPIServer.proxyBySpelling`).

Tests: `TestDetectTriesThePortsNumberThenName`, `TestDetectARefusedCandidateDoesNotStopTheNext`,
`TestDetectForbiddenIsAState`, `TestPollerTriesThePortsNumberThenName`, `TestCandidates*`.

**What it does not cover:** the owner's role grants no Alertmanager, so the alerts pill stays "No
permission" on mgmt-p whatever the spelling; each refused spelling is a 403 in the cluster's audit
log, again at every detection (every 2 minutes while nothing is granted); not yet tried against
mgmt-p from Cogpit's window.

## D-97: A connect goes on when another cluster is shown; a failed one stays

**The owner's findings (walk of 2026-10-19 on v0.26.1, verbatim).** WF39: "ich bin in den stage
cluster gegangen und walk-login-hang blinkt hier nicht." — a connect that waited for its login was
ended by showing another cluster ("Superseded by a newer connect", its plugin ended), its dot grey,
without a word. WF40: "Er wurde rot, ist dann aber automatisch in meinen vorherigen cluster zurück
gesprungen […] man wartet auf den Login, dieser dauert ewig, verlässt den Rechner und auf einmal
ist man in einem anderen Cluster. A: man ist unaufmerksam und merkt es nicht. B: man hat vergessen,
dass man sich gerade auf einen anderen Cluster verbinden wollte um etwas zu tun und vergisst das
gleich mit." Asked whether only after a long wait or always: **"Immer"** — a failed connect never
shows the cluster shown before; the window stays on the failed one with its error and a retry.
Both replace lead decisions of [D-69](#d-69-several-clusters-connected-at-once) (stage 1: "a connect
under way to another cluster: superseded"; stage 2, item 7: "a failed connect shows the cluster
shown before again").

**WF40, the owner's decision, built 2026-10-19:** a failed connect leaves the window on its cluster:
`UIState.Context` names it, `Connection` is `error` with the message, its dots are red, the cluster
shown before stays connected behind it. The workspace's placeholder says "Could not connect to
<cluster>: <error>" with **Connect Again** (the welcome page's connect of that cluster, a credential
plugin's review included) and **Show Connection Updates** (its connection log); the welcome page,
when it shows, says it in its status line and its row's warning icon opens the log. The window's
`followSwitch` and its memory of the cluster shown before are gone; a hotbar tile's failed connect
says it in a toast as any failed connect from a tile did.

**WF39, the lead's decisions, open to revision:**

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A connect waiting for its login when the user shows or connects another cluster | end it (as built); ask before ending it; go on in the background | go on in the background: its entry of `Connections` stays `connecting`, its dot blinks, its waiting line is in the dot's tooltip, Cancel Connecting is in its menus; the window shows the cluster the user chose | Ending a browser login or an MFA push the user is in the middle of costs the login; a question in the way of every switch is noise; stage 2 and 3 already gave a connect nobody watches a state the user sees (the restore's), so D-69's reason for superseding is gone |
| How it is built | keep the window's connect and detach it on a switch; make every connect a run of its own that the window's connect waits for | every connect a run of its own (`connectRun`, [`connect_run.go`](../../internal/engine/connect_run.go)), the restore's too: the window's connect starts one, or joins the one under way for that context, and waits; a switch ends only the wait | One path for the window's and the restore's connects; nothing holds the connect lock while a login waits, so a switch is at once; the wait, not the login, is what a switch supersedes |
| When the run ends nobody waits for | connected silently; a toast | the cluster joins the pool as one the window left (its warm period, then cold), a toast "Connected to <cluster> in the background."; a failure says "Could not connect to <cluster>: …" in a toast, its entry gone; a cancel says nothing | The user left it waiting; the toast is the one place that says it came; the window's shown cluster never changes by itself |
| Connecting a context again whose connect runs (in the background or shown) | a new connect beside it; join it | join it: the window shows it connecting with what it waits for, and shows its end | A second plugin run would race the first for the login (H-118); the user's second click means "show me that one" |
| `cluster.connect`'s result when the user (or an agent) showed another cluster while it waited | an error ("superseded"); `connecting` | `{state: connecting}` without an error; the window shows no error toast | The connect did not fail, it goes on; an agent reads its end in `ui_state`'s `connections` and the connection log |
| The caller's own context ends (an MCP request given up) | the run goes on; the run ends | the run ends with it, as the connect did before | Nothing else changes for agents; only the window's switch keeps a login alive |
| The connection log of a run nobody waited for at its end | as any connect; marked | "Connected to <cluster> in the background: another cluster was shown meanwhile" (the restore's keeps "… in the background"); a cancel "Connecting cancelled (Disconnect)"; Cogpit's close "Ended: Cogpit closed"; "Superseded by a newer connect" no longer occurs for a connect | The log says where the connection came from |

**Built 2026-10-19:** `connectRun` in [`connect_run.go`](../../internal/engine/connect_run.go) (`state.runs`
replaces the restore's `background` and `bgCancel`), `Session.connect` and `ConnectBackground` on it,
`DisconnectContext` cancelling a run in the background or the window's, `ConnectedCluster.running`
(was `restoring`) keeping a run's entry while another cluster is shown, `ErrConnectInBackground`;
the window's [`tableview.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/tableview.go) placeholder after a failed connect,
[`clustermarks.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/clustermarks.go) without `followSwitch`. Tests:
`TestShowingAnotherClusterLeavesTheConnectRunning`, `TestALeftConnectThatFailsSaysSo`,
`TestConnectAgainJoinsTheRun`, `TestCancelALeftConnect`, `TestAFailedConnectStaysOnItsCluster` in the
engine; `TestAFailedConnectStaysOnItsCluster` in the window; PNGs
([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/connect_failed_stays_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/connect_failed_stays_light.png)).

**Not verified:** a real browser login (OIDC, Pinniped) left in the background and finished there;
the walk's fake plugins on kind against this build; several runs in the background at once against
real clusters.

## D-98: What holds a Terminating namespace, and Remove finalizers

**The owner's wish (walk of 2026-10-19 on v0.26.1, WF43, verbatim):** "ich hatte in der
Vergangenheit immer mal wieder das Problem, dass sich ein Namespace nicht hat Löschen lassen, weil
darin noch Objekte waren, die Finalizer hatten die einfach nicht abgeräumt wurden. Ist es möglich
solche Objekte automatisch zu finden? Diese Objekte bei einem Delete des Namespaces im Drawer
aufzulisten und Links aufzubauen, gelöschte Objekte verschwinden dann aus der Auflistung und wenn
keines mehr zusehen ist, kann auch der Namespace gelöscht werden? Ich bin mir unsicher, es könnten
Permissions fehlen um alle Objekte zu sehen. Recherchiere das mal"

**The owner's answer (Q1, 2026-10-19, verbatim):** "ja gerne", to: besides the read-only list of
what blocks a Terminating namespace, a destructive **Remove finalizers** on one object, its
confirmation naming the object, its finalizers and that the owning controller's cleanup is skipped
(a cloud disk or DNS record may stay); agents only with the user's acceptance
([D-2](#d-2-agent-interface-scope)); never the namespace's own `kubernetes` finalizer
through `/finalize`.

**What it builds on (the lead's research, live on kind v1.36.1, 2026-10-19):** the namespace
controller writes on the Namespace itself why it is stuck: `NamespaceContentRemaining` ("Some
resources are remaining: configmaps. has 1 resource instances, secrets. has 1 resource
instances"), `NamespaceFinalizersRemaining` ("… example.com/x in 2 resource instances") and
`NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure`, kinds by resource and group and finalizers by name with
counts, never an object's name and no pairing of the two. A user who may only read namespaces reads
them in full while `list configmaps` there is Forbidden. After the last finalizer goes the
namespace is gone within seconds (2 s in the research, 4.9 and 5.1 s in two runs of `TestKindTerminatingNamespaceBlockers`):
no second Delete is needed.

**Built 2026-10-19** (package I), the lead's decisions, open to revision:

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the list is made | (a) the Namespace profile's `DetailWith` with `DetailNeeds`; (b) the engine's drawer model, reads that follow the namespace's conditions | **(b)**, [`engine/nsblockers.go`](../../internal/engine/nsblockers.go); the condition parsing is L0, [`kinds/namespacedeletion.go`](../../internal/model/kinds/namespacedeletion.go) `NamespaceDeletionOf` | The kinds come from the condition at run time, any kind, custom ones too; `DetailNeeds` are fixed per profile |
| How a named kind is read | (a) the kind's own scope, as its view reads it (cluster-wide and whole for a user who may list it everywhere); (b) a scope of its own: metadata only, in that namespace | **(b)**: `cache.Scope{GVR, Namespace, MetadataOnly}` per kind the condition names | Name, deletionTimestamp and finalizers are metadata: no Secret value crosses the wire for the list, and opening a namespace's drawer never starts a list of every Secret or custom resource of the cluster. Cost: a second watch of that namespace while the kind's own view runs too. Measured (`TestBudgetTerminatingNamespaceBlockers`): one metadata-only streaming list of Config Maps in the namespace, nothing for the Secrets the rules deny, nothing more while the drawer stays open |
| How long it is held | for the call; while the drawer shows the namespace | **while the drawer shows the namespace and the condition names the kind** (`drawerWatch.blockers`): a kind the condition drops, and every kind when the drawer closes, goes back (the cache's warm period as for any consumer); an agent's `object_get` reads for the call and waits, bounded, for the first lists | Cache first: a watch makes an object whose finalizers go vanish from the list by itself |
| Which objects are rows | every object of a named kind; those being deleted and held by finalizers | **those with a deletionTimestamp and finalizers**, by name, at most 100; the kind's other objects counted ("1 more without finalizers, not gone yet") | What holds the namespace is a finalizer; the others go without anyone's help |
| A kind the user may not list there | (a) try and show the refusal; (b) the namespace's rules review first | **(b)**: the namespace's `SelfSubjectRulesReview` (started if not asked yet); denied: a counted row from the condition, "1 remaining; you may not list secrets in walk-fin", and no request; unknown: read, and a 403 the same row, not asked again while the drawer shows the namespace | Discover, don't assume (rule 3); the access reviews exist to spare the API server refused requests |
| A kind Cogpit has no profile of (a custom kind of a user who may not list the definitions, a kind curated nowhere) | (a) map it through discovery and read it; (b) a counted row | **(b)**: "3 remaining; Cogpit has no view of this kind (its definition is not listed)" | Without a profile there is no view to link to; discovery in the drawer's read could block it |
| `NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure` | the condition's text only; the API services that are not available | **the API services whose `Available` is not True**, each with its reason and message and, linked, the Service that serves it ("Served by kube-system/metrics-server"); read whole, cluster-wide, while the condition is True, only when the access reviews do not deny listing `apiservices` (else a row saying so) | The unavailable aggregated API is the classic cause; Cogpit has no API Services view, so the link goes to what the user fixes next, its Service (Lens's form not verified) |
| Nothing left | — | "Nothing blocks the deletion any more: the namespace controller removes the namespace by itself; no second Delete is needed.", once the controller reported and the cache holds nothing of the kinds it names (its condition lags by its requeue, about 6 s); before its first report "has not reported what remains yet" | The owner's "dann kann auch der Namespace gelöscht werden" happens without the user |
| Where in the drawer | after Status; **right after Properties** | right after Properties | Status's five raw conditions would push the list below the fold |
| A row's form | a table; a section renderer of the window's own; **the drawer's items** | "Config Map  walk-cm  Remove Finalizers" (the name a link, the action a button), then "Finalizers" as chips | No code of the window's own; agents read the same items in `object_get`, the action with its params |
| The command | id `object.removeFinalizers` (no id in the parity pages), label "Remove Finalizers" | offered in the list's rows (the item action, with the object's finalizers), and on every kind between Edit and Delete (`Order` 950) in the row menu, the drawer's toolbar (scissors) and the Object menu, while the object is being deleted and holds finalizers; otherwise not applicable (hidden), the reason in `Enabled` | The other action about an object's deletion sits beside Delete; an object not being deleted is no case for it |
| The write | (a) a merge patch `finalizers: null` with the resourceVersion; (b) a JSON patch: `test /metadata/uid`, `test /metadata/finalizers` equal to the finalizers confirmed, `remove /metadata/finalizers` | **(b)**, [`cluster/finalizers.go`](../../internal/cluster/finalizers.go) `FinalizersPatch` | It refuses exactly what the user did not see (another object under the name, a finalizer added or removed since) and nothing else: a controller's status update meanwhile does not refuse it. A failed test is 422 Invalid without causes (seen on kind v1.36.1, the message says nothing more), mapped to `ErrTargetsChanged`. The patch names `metadata.finalizers` only, never `spec.finalizers` or a subresource |
| What binds the confirmation to the write | (a) a required `finalizers` parameter, the window reading them before it dispatches; (b) optional: the confirmation's row "Removes finalizers" shows the given ones, else the cached object's, and Run removes exactly that row's (`engine.ConfirmedFinalizers`) | **(b)** | The row the user read is what the patch tests; no code in the window; an agent may pass them (then they must equal the object's) or not |
| Namespaces | — | **never**: not applicable to the kind `namespaces`, and `/finalize` is never called | The owner's condition; a namespace's own finalizer is the controller's, which removes it once nothing is left |
| Custom resource definitions (the builder found the question open; the lead decided it at the merge, 2026-10-19) | allow as any object; never, as a namespace | **never**: not applicable to the kind `customresourcedefinitions`, refused before anything is resolved (`errDefinitionFinalizers`, `TestRemoveFinalizersRefusals`) | Its `customresourcecleanup.apiextensions.k8s.io` finalizer is the API server's own and guards the definition's custom resources in etcd as a namespace's own guards its content: removed, they would stay in etcd and come back with a definition of the same name (inferred from how the finalizer works, not verified). The narrower choice needs no owner's answer; the owner can widen it. Open to revision |
| Its confirmation | — | Destructive for every origin, agents' included (D-2); Context › Namespace › Object ("Config Map → walk-cm", D-100), "Removes finalizers" a line each (lost), "Skips" "the cleanup of the controllers that own them (a cloud disk or a DNS record may stay)" (warning), "This cannot be undone." | The owner's words; the rows of D-100 |
| Its verb | — | `patch` on the object's resource (`patch *`, resolved per object by the access reviews, greyed "not permitted" on a denial) | The JSON patch is a `patch` |

Tests: `TestNamespaceDeletionFromTheControllersConditions`, `TestNamespaceDeletionFailuresAndEdges`,
`FuzzNamespaceDeletion` (kinds); `TestRemoveFinalizersSendsTheGuardedPatch`,
`TestRemoveFinalizersFailedTest` (cluster); `TestTerminatingNamespaceListsWhatBlocksIt`,
`TestBlockingListForAgents`, `TestBlockingListDiscoveryFailure` (engine);
`TestRemoveFinalizersConfirmsWhatItRemoves`, `TestRemoveFinalizersRefusals`,
`TestRemoveFinalizersOfAKindWithoutAProfile` (commands); `TestBudgetTerminatingNamespaceBlockers`
(the fake API server); on kind `TestKindTerminatingNamespaceBlockers` (a ConfigMap and a Secret with
a dummy finalizer, the namespace deleted, the drawer's rows and `object_get`'s, the API server's
refusal of other finalizers and of another UID, Remove Finalizers through the engine with its
confirmation, each object gone from the list, the namespace gone about 5 s after the last). Renders:
`namespace_blocking_{dark,light}.png`, `confirm_remove_finalizers_{dark,light}.png`.

**What it does not cover:** Lens's behaviour (not verified); a kind without a profile is counted,
not listed; Remove finalizers binds the UID through the kind's own cache, as Delete does, so from
the list, with no view of the kind open, its confirmation reads the kind as its view would (for a
user who may list it everywhere, every object of the kind, once, then warm for five minutes);
`NamespaceDeletionGroupVersionParsingFailure` and `NamespaceDeletionContentFailure` stay in Status,
the section only says they are reported; what a finalizer guards Cogpit cannot know
([H-9](../security/privilege-footprint.md#h-9-force-finalize-skips-cleanup), live since); seen in
offscreen renders only, not yet in a real window.

## D-99: Selecting and copying a log tab's text and a toast's

**The owner's findings (walk of 2026-10-19, verbatim):**
- WF36, a pod's followed log: "Ich habe auch festgestellt, dass ich aus dem Log nichts selektieren
  und kopieren kann. Das ist schlecht." Verified in the code: the log view was a `widget.List` of
  rows, a click selected a row and copied nothing; Download was the only way out.
- WF41, an error toast: "Ich sehe den Toast aber musste auch hier wieder feststellen, dass ich in
  diesem nichts markieren und kopieren kann, auch schlecht für einen toast in dem Fehler stehen
  können." Verified: the toast's text was a `paragraph`, drawn only; the bell's list neither.

**Built 2026-10-19** (the lead), the lead's decisions, open to revision. Code:
[`termview/logselect.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/termview/logselect.go) (the log's selection and
the surface that makes it), [`termview/logview.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/termview/logview.go)
(a row's part of it), [`selparagraph.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/selparagraph.go),
[`toastcopy.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/toastcopy.go), `showToast` in
[`shell.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/shell.go), the bell's rows in
[`notifications.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/notifications.go).

| Question | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| What a log tab's selection is | the drawer's `textSelection` (rune offsets into the one string a widget holds); a range in the tab's lines | **a range in the lines**: each end a line's absolute number (as the rows count lines, prepended ones below zero) and a byte offset into the line's text as the tab shows it | The list is virtualized and recycles its rows as it scrolls; a selection held by a row goes with the row. The drawer's gestures stay: a drag, a double click, ⌘C |
| What takes the pointer | each row; a layer over the list | **a layer over the list** (`logSurface`), all of it but the scroll bar, which keeps its drag; no Hoverable, so the row under the pointer still shows | Fyne sends a drag's events to the object it began on, and a recycled row moves away under a drag that scrolls the view |
| The gestures | the spec's; a triple click for a line | a drag (beyond the view's top or bottom it scrolls a row per 50 ms, faster the farther, at most 8 rows a step); ⇧-click extends from where the selection began; a double click selects a word (a run without white space); ⌘A every line the tab shows, its sources and its filter applied, as Download saves them (A84); ⌘C copies; Escape drops the selection; a right-click offers Copy (greyed without a selection), Select All and Copy All Lines Shown; no triple click | The macOS idiom and the drawer's; Copy All Lines Shown is Download's lines on the clipboard, for a bug report or a chat; the head row (Load older lines) still acts on a click |
| What a copy holds | the lines as they came; as the tab shows them | **as the tab shows them**: resource names and timestamps as toggled, the timestamps in your format (D-31), one line per line joined by "\n", no line ending after the last; a wrapped line as one line, a line cut for its row whole | What you see is what you paste, as Download saves it; a selected line break after the last line is copied as one ("\n" at the end) |
| Following | keep following; stop at any selection; stop at one made with the pointer | **a selection made with the pointer (a drag, ⇧-click, a double click) turns Follow off**, as a jump to a time does; ⌘A does not | At 10,000 lines a second a followed view carries the selection out of sight within a second; the selection stays on its lines when Follow is turned on again |
| New lines, wrapping, a search, a filter | drop the selection; keep it | **kept on its lines**: new lines, Wrap and another width, a search, a filter and the pod and container selectors leave it where it is; a copy takes the lines the tab shows within it | The selection is in the lines, not the rows |
| Lines the scrollback drops (10,000 lines, 32 MiB) | drop the selection; keep the rest; stop dropping while something is selected | **their part of it goes, the rest stays selected**; a selection wholly in dropped lines goes | Memory stays bounded (P5); the highlight shows exactly what a copy holds |
| A view that shows the lines' text differently (Resource names, Timestamps, the time format) | keep the offsets; map them; drop the selection | **drops it** | Its offsets would point at other characters |
| The focus | drop the selection when the focus goes, as the drawer's lines do; keep it | **kept**: the context menu and the toolbar take the focus without dropping it; a press in the tab begins a new one; ⌘C copies while the tab has the keys (after a press in it, and again once the context menu closes) | The context menu takes the focus, and its Copy is what the selection is for |
| Keys the focused log does not use | swallowed, as the list did; passed on | **passed on to the window's**: F1–F12 (the hotbar), Escape without a selection, `/` focuses the search; other shortcuts reach the window's shortcuts | A focused widget that takes shortcuts keeps them otherwise (A55) |
| A search's matches and the selection, which both used the selection colour | the selection in another colour; the matches in another | **the matches in a find colour**: the theme's warning hue at 38 % opacity (`findColor`), as editors and browsers mark what a search found; the selection keeps the theme's selection colour, as the drawer and the YAML editor | A double-clicked word looked like a match; the selection keeps the one colour selected text has everywhere in Cogpit |
| A toast's text | widget.Label made selectable; Cogpit's paragraph made selectable | **the paragraph with the drawer's `textSelection`** (`selParagraph`): a drag over its lines, a double click, ⌘C, Escape drops the selection; the selection in the text as shown, its wrapped lines joined by a space | The paragraph is told its width, which a Label is not, and which mis-sized toasts before; tests still find a toast's paragraph |
| A toast's copy icon | in the title line; beside the ×; on hover only | **always shown, left of the ×**, of a text line's height; it copies the message as it came, a checkmark for 1.5 s, no toast | A toast lives seconds: an icon that shows only under the pointer is found late; in the title line it sat 6 points above the ×; a "Copied" toast would push the toast under the pointer up |
| Holding a toast | the pointer on the card (as before); also its icons and a selection | the pointer on the card, on its × or on its copy icon; while its text holds a selection or a drag makes one; the full time again once neither holds | "Must not vanish while you select"; before, the pointer on the × let the time run |
| A toast's selection colour | the theme's selection; a token of its own | **`cogpit.toastSelection`**: dark #1d6870, light the selection #dfca88 | The dark selection (#274642) is barely apart from the dark toast (#0b4556); `TestPaletteContrast` holds the text 4.5:1 on it and it 1.25:1 against the toast |
| The bell's list | nothing; a copy icon per entry; selectable text | **both**: each notification's text selectable, and a copy icon after its time while the pointer is on its row, its room kept so the time does not move | The list is where a toast that went is read again |
| A copy toast (the drawer's "Copied to the clipboard") | an icon on it too; none | **every toast has it**, that one too | One rule per toast; not worth a case |
| Engine state | the selection in `UIState`; the window's | **the window's**: no command, no `ui_state`, no audit line, as the drawer's selection (D-25) | Rule 2 covers what an agent drives (view, filter, row selection, drawer); a text selection only feeds the clipboard, and agents read a log tab's lines through `dock.read` (D-44) and a notification through `notifications.list`. No new GUI-only exception (conventions › Commands, not handlers): D-25's, the owner's ("text in Cogpit can be selected and copied … agents get no copy command"), covers it |

The copies go through `shell.copyText` as plain copies (D-25): they cancel a pending clearing of a
Secret value copied before. Tests: `TestLogSelectionDragAcrossRows`,
`TestLogSelectionWordAndShiftClick`, `TestLogSelectAllIsWhatTheViewShows`,
`TestLogSelectionKeepsItsLines`, `TestLogSelectionDroppedWithItsLines`,
`TestLogSelectionAutoScroll`, `TestLogSelectionHeadRowActs`, `TestLogSelectionLongLine`,
`TestLogSelectionKeysGoOn`, `TestLogTabCopiesThroughTheShell`, `TestToastCopyIcon`,
`TestToastTextSelectable`, `TestToastHoverOnItsIcons`, `TestNotificationRowCopy`,
`TestSelParagraphShownText`, `TestPaletteContrast`; `TestLogsP5` unchanged (the slowest batch 2.3 ms
at 10,000 lines a second). Renders: a log tab's selection
([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/logs_selection_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/logs_selection_light.png),
[termview](../../internal/ui/fyneui/termview/testdata/logs_selection.png)), toasts with their copy
icon and a selection ([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/toasts_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/toasts_light.png)), the bell's list with a hovered row
([dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/notifications_panel_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/notifications_panel_light.png)).

**What it does not cover:** not tried in a real window: the drag's feel, the auto-scroll's speed,
the order in which the desktop driver sends a toast's and its icons' hover events (read in Fyne
2.8.2's source and replayed in the test driver), and the shortcuts a focused log passes on to the
window (the test driver's canvas has no `TypedShortcut`); ⌘A in a toast's or the drawer's text does
nothing (Fyne hands a disabled selectable text only Copy); a selection does not survive the tab's
stream opening again (another container, Previous, a Reconnect); the terminal tabs select as their
own widget does (D-14).

## D-100: Objects and effects in one form, and a drawer's edited state beside Save

**The owner's findings (walk of 2026-10-19 on v0.26.1, verbatim):**
- WF32, a Config Map's save review: "Save Dialog schon viel übersichtlicher, aber ich möchte dass
  Config Map noch klarer vom Namen getrennt wird: "Config Map -> walk-cm" oder etwas ähnliches".
  It applies to every confirmation's Object(s) row ([D-85](#d-85-dialogs-as-tables-and-an-objects-state-without-its-resourceversion)).
- WF33, the Edit tab's "Apply?": "Auch hier wieder: Removes key added. Ist wieder als Satz
  geschreiben anstatt einer technsich präzisen schnellansicht." The removed key was named `added`:
  in the sentence it read as a word of it. The drawer's save review showed the same fact as a row
  "Removes  new2", red and bold.
- WF31, a Config Map's drawer: "Die Statuszeile ist absolut übersehbar. Wäre mir nicht aufgefallen,
  dass es dort eine Zeile mit Changes / Status gibt wenn du es nicht gesagt hättest." The line,
  "Edited: 1 value.", sat small and muted under the footer.

The rule that follows is in [conventions › Dialogs, reviews and status lines](conventions.md#dialogs-reviews-and-status-lines).

**Built 2026-10-19** (for the lead), the lead's decisions, open to revision:

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| How a dialog names an object (WF32) | (a) "Config Map → walk-cm" as text, the owner's example; (b) the kind muted, the name bold; (c) the kind as a chip; (d) kind and name in two columns | **(a), (b) and (d) together**: the kind muted with the arrow, the name bold, each in a column of its own ([`objectnames.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/objectnames.go) `objectNames`, `objectsRow`); where only plain text fits (a dialog's title) "Config Map → walk-cm" (`objectText`) | The owner's own form; colour and weight set the kind apart where the arrow is not read; the name bold as the review's keys are bold, what a dialog acts on stands out. A chip per object would make a list of twelve pods twelve badges |
| Several objects (Delete of a selection, Restart, Argo CD's and Flux's selections) | the kind on every line (before); grouped by kind, the kind once; a count per kind | **grouped by kind**, the kinds in the order they first appear, the kind on its group's first line, the names under each other; the row "Objects (12)", a single object "Object" (a confirmation said "Objects" for one) | Twelve pods read as twelve names, not twelve "Pod"s; the review said "Object" already |
| Which dialogs | the confirmation only; every dialog that names an object | **every dialog**: the confirmation (Delete, Scale to zero, Drain, Helm, Apply, the node shell, an agent's write), the Config Map's and the Secret's save review (row and title), Rollback, Helm's install review (its head as rows; what it creates: "Deployment → web/api", a hook's "Pod (hook)", a CRD's "(stays after an uninstall)"), Argo CD's Sync and Refresh, the parameter dialog's title ("Scale Deployment → web"), the resources a prune deletes, a binding's role and subjects ("ClusterRole → admin", "ServiceAccount → shop/ci") | One form everywhere, as asked; `placeRows` (Context › Namespace › Object(s)) and `objectsRow` are what the next dialog (Remove finalizers, WF43) builds its rows with |
| The Rollback dialog's sentence ("Release x in namespace y (context z). Rolling back changes …; the current revision gives a new revision equal to it.") | keep it; rows | **rows** Context, Namespace, Object, To revision (the dropdown), Writes "a new revision equal to the chosen one" | D-85's rule; what helm writes holds for every choice, the current revision's too, so it stays said |
| The confirmation's effect (WF33) | keep the sentence in a row "Effect"; a list in that row; **a row per effect with its own name** | a row per effect: `engine.Effect`, a short name, a terse value and a tone (plain; names bold; lost bold in the error colour; warning in the warning colour); every command's sentence rewritten as rows, `Spec.Detail` replaced by `Spec.Effects`; a name fits the table's name column (128 px: "Runs as", "To prune"), a longer one wraps in it (`rowName`) instead of running into its value | The review's "Removes  new2" is the owner's model: a key in a cell of its own never reads as a word; the compiler makes the next command give rows |
| What each command's rows say | — | data keys: Removes (lost), Adds, Changes, Values "not shown"; Rollback: To revision; uninstall: Deletes (lost); upgrade: Chart "web 0.1.0 → 0.2.0" (", an older version"), Repository, Archive (not checked: warning), Values; install: Chart, Archive, Creates (a namespace), Values, Created as, Records (Helm's ConfigMaps driver: warning); drain: Loses and Evicts (lost), DaemonSet pods, Grace period; node shell: Creates and Access (warning), Image, Digest (none: warning), Pull secret, Ends; a binding: Grants, To (a subject a line), Takes effect ("immediately, cluster-wide" in the warning colour, the owner's A101 words); a role: Rules (a rule a line); a quota: Hard limits; a Secret: Type, Keys, Values; a port forward: Listens on, Forwards to, Identity, Reachable by (warning); a proxy: Proxy, For, Proxy sees (warning); Prometheus and Alertmanager: Metrics from or Alerts from, Through, Service sees (warning), Query format, Scheme; Argo CD: Syncs to, Prune and To prune (lost, a resource a line), Refresh; Flux: Runs as, Your rights; Restart: Replaces, OnDelete (warning); a `cogpit://` link: Opens, Shown now | A fact a row, read at a glance; what is lost red, what to weigh amber; an explanation that only repeated what a command is ("its objects change to the new manifest") dropped |
| What `ConfirmRequest.Detail` holds | a sentence beside the rows; the rows' text | **the rows' text** (`EffectsText`: "Removes: added. Adds: new."), with the rows in `ConfirmRequest.Effects` | One source: the Rollback dialog and the drawer's review bind their answer to that text, the upgrade and the node shell refuse when it no longer holds. Checked: no MCP client, CLI or log reads a `ConfirmRequest` (an agent gets the result or the refusal), so nobody outside the window reads either |
| A request with a Detail and no Effects | not shown; a row "Effect" | **a row "Effect"** | None of Cogpit's commands sends one now; a future one must never hide what the user confirms |
| The drawer's edited state (WF31) | (a) the line under the footer in a colour; (b) a banner above the data; (c) the counts in the footer beside Revert and Save; (d) a count in Save's label | **(c), a tinted pill per count**: "2 values edited" amber, "1 key added" green, "1 key removed" red, bold and in the text size of the buttons' labels beside them (a pill's caption size read as a footnote), between Add Key and Revert; on a line of its own above the buttons, at its end, where the drawer is too narrow for one ([`datakeys.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/datakeys.go) `editCounts`, `dataFooterLayout`); nothing while nothing is edited; the line under the footer keeps what the pills don't say (read-only, a newer version on the cluster, the drafts back, saved at) | Where the eye goes before Save, in the colours a diff marks lines with (modified, added, deleted) and the drawer uses already ("new" green, a removed key red); (a) stays a line under the footer; (b) moves the data; (d) hides which kind of change |

Tests: `TestObjectNamesSetTheKindApart`, `TestConfirmationEffectsAreRows` (the owner's Apply case),
`TestConfirmationShowsADetailWithoutEffects`, `TestDataFooterLayout`, the engine's
`TestDataKeysDetail` and the command tests that pin each command's rows (`argocd_test.go`,
`createdialogs_test.go`, `datakeys_test.go`, `editdatakeys_test.go`, `flux_test.go`, `helm*_test.go`,
`nodeshell_test.go`, `portforward_test.go`, `deeplink_test.go`), the drawers' (`configmapdata_test.go`,
`secretdata_test.go`, `datakeys_test.go`). Renders: `confirm.png`, `confirm_apply_removes_*.png`
(new), `delete_selection_*.png`, `node_shell_confirm_*.png`, `rollback_dialog_dark.png`,
`helm_install_preview_dark.png`, `argocd_*_dialog_*.png`, `scale_dialog_*.png`, the reviews
(`configmap_keys_review_*.png`, `secret_keys_review_*.png`, `configmap_save_*.png`, `secret_save_*.png`)
and the drawers' footers (`configmap_keys_drawer_*.png`, `secret_keys_drawer_*.png`,
`configmap_drawer_footer_dark.png`).

**What it does not cover:** the engine's `Message()` names an object "Pod web-0" still (only the
tests read it); the port-forward dialog's title ("Port Forwarding for web-0", Lens's) and the
create dialogs name no kind beside a name; the Edit tab's title ("Config Map walk-cm · loaded at
…") and the drawer's head keep their own form; the kind tests' expectations of the new texts were
edited, not run (kind is not up); seen in offscreen renders only, not yet in a real window;
Windows and Linux not tried.

## D-102: Debug containers added from the drawer, shown in blue, reached by Logs, Shell and Attach

**The owner's words (2026-10-19 evening, verbatim, after a look at a debugged pod in the staging
cluster):** "Ephemeral Containers werden ja temprär an einen laufenden Pod gehängt um ihn debuggen zu
können, richtig? Er ist dann so lange da, bis der Pod neu gestartet wird. Diese Container sollen mit
einem blauen Icon in der Pod übersicht am Pod auftauchen, um sie von den anderen regulären containern
abzuheben. Für das attachen eines Ephemeral Containers muss es einen Default in den Cogpit Settings den
der Nutzer konfigurieren kann. Wir liefern nicolaka/netshoot:v0.16 aus. Im Pod-Drawer muss es dazu auch
