ein Icon geben um an einen Pod einen solchen Container anzuhängen. Der Nutzer wird dann gefragt, welches
Image, und bekommt den konfigurierten Standard voreingestellt angezeigt. Er kann das Feld aber
bearbetien, markieren, kopieren oder einfügen." To "Logs und Attach erreichen keinen Ephemeral
Container" and "Das Ziel aus --target fehlt": "Fix bauen". The danger level, asked as one question the
same evening: **Destructive** ("Destructive (Recommended)"): a confirmation for every origin, the
window's included, as a table Context › Namespace › Pod, Target, Image; agents always need the user's
acceptance.

**Kubernetes' behaviour (answered in the same session, for the docs and the dialog):** an ephemeral
container lives as long as the pod object, not until a container restart: a crash or liveness restart
of the pod's containers keeps it, a deleted or replaced pod (a rollout, an eviction, a lost node) takes
it away. It is never restarted itself (a finished one stays Terminated in
`status.ephemeralContainerStatuses`), and the API cannot remove or change it
([ephemeral containers](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/ephemeral-containers/)).

**Built 2026-10-19**, the lead's decisions, open to revision:

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The squares' colour | (a) `StatusSucceeded`, the palette's blue; (b) a token of its own in that blue; (c) another blue | **(b)** `model.StatusEphemeral`, the same RGB as Succeeded in both themes ([`theme.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/theme.go); `TestStatusColoursAreDistinct` names the pair as wanted) | The token says "kind of container", not "finished well"; a container's square is never Succeeded (a finished one is Stopped), so the two blues never meet in one cell |
| A finished ephemeral container's look | (a) red for a non-zero exit code; (b) dimmed; (c) a blue outline whatever the exit code | **(c)**, `CellMark.Hollow`, the outline inset so that it is as large as a filled square | An interactive shell's exit code (130 after Ctrl+C) says how the user's last command ended, not that the pod is unwell; red would alarm on a healthy pod. The drawer keeps the state's colours (Terminated: Error in red), which say what happened |
| Running, starting, failing to start | — | blue filled while it runs or waits to start (ContainerCreating, no status yet); **red** while it waits on an error (ImagePullBackOff and the other reasons the squares already call errors) | A container that will not start as it is needs the user, as any container's red square says |
| The order in the cell | the spec's order; the live ones first | **after the regular containers, the live ones first, then the finished ones**, each group in the spec's order ([`pods.go`](../../internal/model/kinds/pods.go) `ephemeralMarks`) | A pod debugged often collects finished ones (they stay as long as the pod): with the live ones first, the count a narrow cell shows (F24) hides the finished ones, not the running debug shell |
| A cap on the squares | the cell's width alone (F24); a cap on finished ephemeral containers only; a cap for every cell | **at most 12 squares a cell**, the rest counted "+N" as F24 counts what does not fit, the count blue when the hidden ones are ephemeral (`maxCellMarks`, `moreStatus`) | One rule for every pod; a widened column does not grow a strip of twenty outlines; 12 is above any pod Cogpit has met with regular containers |
| The ratio, the restarts, the pod's status | count ephemeral containers; leave them out | **left out**, as kubectl's READY, RESTARTS and STATUS leave them out | The ratio and the status stay what `kubectl get pods` prints |
| The tooltip | — | "debugger: ephemeral, running, target app", "dnscheck: ephemeral, terminated (Completed, exit code 0)" | Names the kind, the state and the target (the owner's "Fix bauen") in the form the other squares use |
| The drawer's Target | plain text; a jump to the target's section | **plain text, right after Status** (`containerSection`, "Target") | The drawer has no jump to a section of its own; Status, Target, Image read as the container's identity |
| The command | id, label, place | **`pod.debug`, "Debug", MenuPath Pod/Debug, Order 250**: after Shell, before Evict, in the row menu, the drawer's toolbar (a magnifier, `theme.IconNameSearch`) and the palette | Lens's pod menu has no Debug (its documentation, docs.lenshq.io › Pods, read 2026-10-19; the running app not checked); beside Shell, the other way into a container |
| Image dialog and confirmation | (a) the schema's generated dialog, then the engine's confirmation (two steps, the second repeating the first); (b) one dialog of the window's own that is the confirmation, as the Rollback dialog is; (c) the engine's confirmation with editable fields | **(b)**, [`debugdialog.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/debugdialog.go): the confirmation's rows (Context › Namespace › Pod, Target as a select, Sees, Image as an ordinary entry, Digest), "This cannot be undone.", Debug armed after the confirmation's delay and disabled while the image is empty; the answer bound to the command, the window, the pod, its UID as the dialog read it (the command's Prefill gives it), the target and the image (`confirmedByDialogOr`) | The engine's confirmation carries no fields (`ConfirmRequest`), and a field there would touch every confirmation; two dialogs would show the same values twice (the owner's rule against repeating what a table says, D-85). A pod created again under the name while the dialog is open is refused ("…replaced by another of its name while the dialog was open; nothing was added") |
| The target's choices | the pod's containers; with "None" | **the pod's containers, the first preselected, then None** (no shared processes); the engine also takes an init container, the API's rule; an agent's `target` left out is none, as kubectl's `--target` | The owner's dialog asks for a target; None is the narrower choice the API allows |
| The container | — | `debugger-<5 lowercase characters>` (kubectl's form, never a name the pod has), `stdin` and `tty` true, `terminationMessagePolicy: File`, the image's own command, `targetContainerName`, no security context, the pull policy left to the API server ([`engine/debugcontainer.go`](../../internal/engine/debugcontainer.go) `DebugContainer`) | What `kubectl debug -it --target` builds; stdin and a TTY keep the shell alive after a detach |
| The write | (a) a JSON patch appending to the list; (b) a strategic merge patch naming the new container | **(b)** on the `ephemeralcontainers` subresource with the pod's UID as `metadata.uid` ([`cluster/debugcontainer.go`](../../internal/cluster/debugcontainer.go)) | kubectl's; the list merges by name, so a container of the same name would be a change the API server refuses. The subresource keeps the patch's UID and refuses its change (422 on `metadata.uid`, read in the Kubernetes 1.36 source), verified on kind v1.36.1: another UID is `cluster.ErrReplaced` |
| After the add | return; open the Attach tab | **the Attach tab on it, for every origin**, as `kubectl debug -it`; Debug waits for the pod's watch to bring the container (at most 30 s) and returns without a tab, saying so, when it does not; the Attach tab waits through the cache (at most 3 minutes) while the container starts, "[cogpit] Waiting for <name> to start…", and fails at once on an image that cannot be pulled | Cache first: the container's stdin and TTY come from the cached spec, and the API server refuses an attach to a container that has not started. The wait applies to any container that has not started yet (`containerStarting`), a regular one too |
| A finished pod | leave it to the API server; refuse | **greyed with the reason** ("the pod has ended (succeeded)", also "the pod is being deleted") | The API server takes an ephemeral container on a finished pod (verified on kind v1.36.1), which would never run |
| The confirmation's rows | — | Target ("none" without one), Sees "<target>'s processes and files" (warning colour) with a target, Image and Digest (or "none: a floating tag…") as the node shell's (`imageEffects`); no row for the container's lifetime | "This cannot be undone." in red says it; no Kubernetes lecture (D-85) |
| The verbs | — | `patch pods/ephemeralcontainers`, `create pods/attach`: the access reviews grey Debug "not permitted" when either is denied | Debug's purpose is the shell; a container nobody may attach to is half of it |
| The preference | per cluster (as the node shell's); app-wide | **app-wide, Preferences › Kubernetes › Debug container image**, after the integrations of new clusters, Cogpit's default as the placeholder, a line saying pinned or floating ([`preferences_debug.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/preferences_debug.go)); `debugImage` in `preferences.set` and `preferences.get` | The owner's ("Cogpit Settings") |
| Who sets it | anyone; the user only | **the user only**: agents and the CLI may reset it (`ErrDebugImageGUIOnly`), as [D-38](#d-38-who-sets-the-node-shells-image) decides for the node shell's image | It decides what the user's next Debug runs beside a pod's processes, as root with netshoot; an agent's own `pod.debug` may name an image, which its confirmation shows |
| The default and its pin | the tag; pinned by digest | **`docker.io/nicolaka/netshoot:v0.16@sha256:b09d9b21381f47a79b3cbcb30da25266dc17186ea00ae65e99fdc51396f48e70`**, the multi-arch index's digest (read by the lead with a HEAD on registry-1.docker.io, 2026-10-19), shown as `nicolaka/netshoot:v0.16`, "pinned by digest"; Renovate moves tag and digest (a custom manager for `debugcontainer.go` in `.github/renovate.json`) and CI's kind job runs every change (`TestKindDebugContainer`; the test with the pull took about 20 s on a local kind) | As the node shell's default ([D-37](#d-37-the-node-shell)); the image's own banner reads "Version: 0.14", netshoot's text |
| Logs of a controlling resource | add the ephemeral containers; the template's containers | **the template's**: a workload's and an application's tabs stay with the containers of the pods' template; a pod's tab lists its ephemeral containers apart, under "Ephemeral containers" | An ephemeral container belongs to one pod and is in no template |

Tests: `TestEphemeralContainerMarks`, `TestEphemeralContainerSectionTarget` (kinds);
`TestAddEphemeralContainerSendsTheGuardedPatch`, `TestAddEphemeralContainerRefusals` (cluster);
`TestAttachAfterAWait`, `TestStartPodAttachAfterAFailedWait` (terminal);
`TestAttachOptionsOfAnEphemeralContainer`, `TestContainerStarting`, `TestWaitContainerStarted`,
`TestDebugContainerNamesAndEffects`, `TestPodEnded` (engine); `TestDebugAddsTheConfirmedContainer`,
`TestDebugNeedsEveryOriginsConfirmation`, `TestDebugRefusals`, `TestDebugPrefill`,
`TestDebugImagePreference`, `TestDebugContainerReachedByLogsShellAndAttach` (commands);
`TestContainersCellDrawsEphemeralMarks`, `TestDebugDialogIsTheConfirmation`,
`TestDebugDialogEmptyImageAndNoTarget`, `TestDebugDialogRefusesAReplacedPod`,
`TestPodMenusOfferDebugAndEphemeralContainers`, `TestDebugImagePreferenceField` (window); on kind
v1.36.1 `TestKindDebugContainer` (added with the default image, attached after the wait, the
target's `sleep` seen from the debug shell, `exit` leaving it Terminated, its log read through Logs,
another UID refused, Pod Security restricted's refusal shown, a finished pod greyed). Renders:
[`ephemeral_marks_pods_dark.png`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/ephemeral_marks_pods_dark.png),
[`ephemeral_containers_drawer_dark.png`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/ephemeral_containers_drawer_dark.png),
[`debug_dialog_dark.png`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/debug_dialog_dark.png),
[`confirm_debug_agent_dark.png`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/confirm_debug_agent_dark.png), and
the light ones beside them.

**What it does not cover:** a command for the debug container (kubectl's `-- <command>`): the image's
own runs; ending a debug container's shell when its tab closes (Kubernetes cannot stop an ephemeral
container from outside, [H-134](../security/privilege-footprint.md#h-134-a-debug-container-stays-in-the-pod-and-sees-its-target));
a real window (not verified).

**Checked on a real cluster (2026-10-19 night, the lead; the cluster the owner provides for tests,
Kubernetes 1.35, Kyverno 1.17.2):** `TestRealDebugContainer` (make test-real) added a debug
container with the default image to a running pod in a namespace of its own, attached in 2 s (the
image already on the node), saw the target's process, ended it with `exit`; the cache then gave the
Pods list a running green square and an outlined blue one ("debugger-…: ephemeral, terminated
(Completed, exit code 0), target tick") and the drawer the section with Target `tick`. A namespaced
Kyverno Policy (admission only, Enforce, matching `Pod/ephemeralcontainers`) made the next Debug fail
at once with Kyverno's own message, several lines long, shown unchanged ("admission webhook
\"validate.kyverno.svc-fail\" denied the request: resource Pod/…/target was blocked due to the
following policies …"), and added nothing. The pod debugged by hand that afternoon (`kubectl debug
--target`, two ephemeral containers, one finished) showed Target and squares as `kubectl` made them
(`COGPIT_REAL_DEBUG_POD`); its namespace was deleted afterwards. Kyverno's reports controller logged
that it may not read `Pod/ephemeralcontainers` (the cluster's RBAC, not Cogpit's).

## D-103: Fyne's thread check, a build parameter, off in releases

**The owner's words (2026-10-19 late evening, verbatim):** "Ich habe gerade festgestellt, dass das
scrollen bei besonders schnell scrollen springt. Es wirk nicht so flüssig wie bei Lens. Das bekommen
wir besser hin oder? Untersuche das und mach vorschläge wie wir schneller rendern können wenn der User
schnell scrollt." Of the measured proposals ([G16](../parity/gaps.md)), asked one at a time: proposal
1 "Prüfen, dann nur Releases (Recommended)"; 2–4 "Erst ansehen, dann (Recommended)". Then "Ich will
das ganze auf einem Branch" and "Dieser wird dann intensiv durch dich getestet und ich schaue auch
drauf. Wir müssen jederzeit zurück können mit nur einem Flag", refined the same evening: "Ich denke es
reicht ein Build-Parameter. Beim Bau entscheiden wir, ob wir das Scrollen beschleunigen wollen oder auf
Sicherheit gehen. Beim Release setzen wir auf Geschwindigkeit, beim Entwickeln und Testen auf
Sicherheit und Fehler schnell zu identifizieren. Jederzeit können wir auch für Releases zum alten
Verhalten zurück. Wenn wir wollen, können wir auch in der Entwicklung auf Geschwindigkeit gehen, zum
Beispiel um die Auswirkungen zu überprüfen bevor wir das releasen."

**Why it matters (measured 2026-10-19 late evening, Fyne v2.8.2, a 120 Hz display):** Fyne checks,
on every canvas refresh, that it runs on its main goroutine (`async.EnsureMain`, which reads the
goroutine's id from `runtime.Stack`) while an app has not declared itself migrated to `fyne.Do`.
Cogpit had not, so every `Resize` and `Refresh` of a table cell's rectangles and texts paid for it:
at 10,000 px/s the table drew 6 frames a second with the check and 60 without, the work of a frame
189 ms at the median against 7.9 ms; the YAML view spent 134 of 135 ms of a scroll step in the check.
Without the check, a call from another goroutine is no longer moved to the main goroutine: it races,
and a `fyne.DoAndWait` made on the main goroutine never returns. Hence the audit first.

**Measured again on the branch (2026-10-19 night, the same harness: the demo cluster's Pods list,
scroll events through Fyne's own path at 120 a second, a 2560×1409 canvas at scale 1 on the owner's
120 Hz display):**

| Pods list, Fyne's 60 Hz timer | 1,500 px/s | 4,000 px/s | 10,000 px/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frames per second: check on → off (metadata, chosen) → off (Fyne's tag) | 60.0 → 60.3 → 60.3 | 56.3 → 60.3 → 60.3 | **6.3 → 60.3 → 60.3** |
| A frame's work p50 / p99 (ms), check on | 11.3 / 18.7 | 14.1 / 26.2 | 184 / 208 |
| … off by the metadata (chosen) | 5.7 / 7.3 | 6.4 / 7.6 | 7.9 / 11.1 |
| … off by Fyne's tag | 5.5 / 7.3 | 5.9 / 7.3 | 7.0 / 9.2 |
| Frames over 16.7 ms: on → metadata → tag | 1.5% → 0 → 0 | 25.8% → 0 → 0 | 100% → 0 → 0 |

With the demo cluster's 1,000 watch events a second and the tag: 60.3 frames per second at every
speed, p99 6.9 / 7.3 / 9.6 ms. The YAML view (5 MB) at 10,000 px/s: p50 7.0 ms with the check, 2.2
without; the log view (20,000 lines): 9.4 and 8.9 ms (its cost is rasterising text, not the check).

**The owner's look (2026-10-20, verbatim, after scrolling a release build of the branch):**
"Deutlich besseres Ansprechverhalten. … Ich hätte das Feature gerne in Releases aktiviert." So it
reached `main` (PR #64, merged by the owner on 2026-10-20), and every release from v0.30.0 on is built
with the check off; v0.29.3 and earlier have it on.

**Built 2026-10-19 night on the branch `fast-scroll`, merged after that look**, the lead's decisions,
open to revision:

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The parameter | (a) Fyne's own build tag `migrated_fynedo`; (b) the app's metadata `Migrations["fyneDo"]`, set in `fyneui.Run` by a build tag of Cogpit's own, `nothreadcheck`; (c) a flag at run time | **(b)** ([`fyneui.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/fyneui.go) `appMetadata`) | Found at build: Fyne's tag does more than drop the check. It also swaps Fyne's internal caches and queues for single-threaded ones (`internal/async`: `map_migratedfynedo.go` a plain map, `mutex_migratedfynedo.go` a lock that does nothing, `queue_migratedfynedo.go`), used by the renderer, canvas, font, text-size, texture, theme-override and SVG caches, so a stray Fyne call, even a text measurement, could end the app with "concurrent map writes" instead of racing on one widget. The `-race` run below found exactly that path at quit. The metadata turns the same check off (`build.MigratedToFyneDo`, read once) and keeps those caches thread-safe, for about 0.4–0.9 ms more per frame (measured below); (c) the owner replaced it with a build parameter |
| Its name and values | — | **`FYNE_THREAD_CHECKS=on\|off`** in the [`Makefile`](../../Makefile); empty means the target's default: `on` for `build`, `app`, `run`, `run-demo` (safety), `off` for `dist-app` (speed); any other value stops make; off adds the tag `nothreadcheck` to `GO_TAGS` (`BUILD_TAGS`), which `internal/buildinfo` reads (`FyneThreadChecks`) and `fyneui.Run` turns into the metadata | One parameter, both directions overridable per build, as the owner asked |
| The release's way back | (a) edit the Makefile; (b) the repository variable `FYNE_THREAD_CHECKS`, which [`build.yml`](../../.github/workflows/build.yml)'s Build step passes to `make dist-app` | **(b)**, unset or `off`: off; `on`: the next releases keep the check (as before D-103) | No code change and no commit to go back; one switch in GitHub's settings |
| A release's check of itself | — | `dist-app` fails unless both binaries recorded `nothreadcheck` when off, and fails when they recorded it though `on` (`go version -m`); [`TestTheThreadCheckTag`](../../internal/buildinfo/threadchecks_test.go) fails when the Makefile's tag and `internal/buildinfo`'s differ, or when Fyne's build package no longer reads the `fyneDo` migration from the app's metadata (a Fyne upgrade, which Renovate brings) | A tag no file knows is ignored silently: a release would keep the cost and say "off" |
| Where the build says its mode | About, Diagnostics, the app log, `cogpit-cli version` | **the app log at every start** (`cogpit started … fyneThreadCheck="off (speed)"`) and **About when the build is not its kind's default** ("Fyne thread check on" in a release built with it, "Fyne thread check off" in a development build without it; [`about.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/about.go)) | A bug report then names the mode in every case (the default follows from release or development build) and About stays as the owner knows it; Diagnostics' first line already fills the tab at 1440 points (`TestSnapshotsOnlyInDiagnostics` measures it); `cogpit-cli` holds no Fyne |
| A development build's warning | (a) the app log only; (b) a warning toast per place besides the log; (c) a crash | **(b)**: a development build with the check on shows each place Fyne reported once, as a warning toast naming the file and line; a release built with the check keeps them in the app log ([`threadcheck.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/threadcheck.go)) | "Fehler schnell zu identifizieren": seen at once, without ending the session; the user of a release is not shown a developer's message. Verified first: Fyne's warnings already reach the app log (`cmd/cogpit`'s `slog.SetDefault` routes the standard log package there), so the earlier "lost on stderr" was wrong |
| The tests | Fyne's test driver has no thread check (it runs `fyne.Do` on the caller's goroutine); (a) a test driver of Cogpit's that checks the goroutine; (b) a scan that fails on every new goroutine until it is audited, plus the main-loop stand-ins failing on a `fyne.DoAndWait` made on the loop; (c) the race shards alone | **(b) and (c)**: [`TestEveryGoroutineSiteIsAudited`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/threadsites_test.go) against [ui-threads.md](ui-threads.md); the stand-ins of `termview` and of the terminal fork count such a wait and fail | (a) would replace the driver under some 600 window tests; the scan keeps the audit true where it is cheap, the race shards find what a test drives |
| The audit | — | every place below `internal/ui` where code runs off the main goroutine, in [ui-threads.md](ui-threads.md): **no stray call and no `fyne.DoAndWait` reachable from the main goroutine** in Cogpit's code | Three agents read it in three groups, the lead checked their rows against the scan |
| The race run | — | a `-race` development build with the check off ran Cogpit's own `--perf-mode gate` (start-up, fast scrolling, every view, typing into 5 MB of YAML) with no race report; then five runs of 8 minutes each, driven over MCP on the demo cluster at 1,000 events a second and a second, real cluster (630 to 650 rounds each: views, drawers, the filter, the palette, Edit tabs, log tabs, local terminals printing 20 lines a second, dock reads, about 64 cluster switches): no race while the window ran in any of them. At quit, before the terminals stopped at the window's close: 18 reports (Fyne's tag, quit by SIGTERM), 13 (the metadata, SIGTERM), 10 (the metadata, quit as ⌘Q quits), every one the terminal widget's reading goroutines running its own `fyne.Do` side by side after Fyne had drained its queue; after (`termview.Terminal.Stop`, the row below), two runs quit as ⌘Q quits: **none** | What a test cannot drive: the real GL driver, its timer and the window's own goroutines |
| The window's close | — | the shell's `stopped` flag is set when the window closes (on the main goroutine, for the close button, `a.Quit` and ⌘Q alike), not only after Fyne's loop has ended, and the dock's terminals stop drawing there (`termview.Terminal.Stop`: their output ends with the next read) | Once Fyne drains its queue it runs a `fyne.Do` at once on the caller's goroutine, check or not: a timer in that gap ran widget code off the main goroutine (found by the audit), and the terminal widget, which calls `fyne.Do` itself, did so side by side at quit (found by the race run); both true before D-103 too |

**What it does not cover:** the unevenness of fast scrolling, Fyne's 60 Hz timer against a 120 Hz
display (proposals 2–4 of G16, after the owner's look); a stray call on a path no test and no audit
reached (the toast of a development build is the net); Fyne's own code and the terminal fork's
(trusted to use `fyne.Do` as they say, `third_party/fyne-terminal/PATCHES.md`); a SIGINT or SIGTERM,
which Fyne's own handler turns into a quit without the window's close; Windows and Linux, where the
metadata means the same and nothing was run.

## D-104: Dialog fields, their hints and dropdowns (the gate walk's GW2, GW5, GW6)

**The owner's findings (gate walk of 2026-10-20, G16):**
- GW2, Scale of a Deployment: the Replicas field far too wide for a number up to 65535; he wants
  "Slider von 1 bis 30, höhere Zahlen eintippen" (the lead's record of his words). The lead's own
  look at the same screenshot: the hint under the field was the schema's text for agents ("the
  desired number of pods, 0 to 65535 (required to run; a dialog starts from the current count). 0
  stops every pod and is confirmed like a destructive action"), and the title read "Scale
  Deployment →   gate-web", a wide gap after the arrow.
- GW6, every parameter dialog: fields far too wide, and "Deine Texte sind echt hilfreich, aber sie
  überladen unsere Masken teilweise enorm." He wants a small question mark after each field's name,
  its tooltip carrying the hint.
- GW5, every dropdown: a Select's list shows the current entry again under the field (Rollback's
  "To revision": the field "3 - podinfo-6.15.0 …", the list 3, 2, 1), "verwirrend", noticed on other
  dropdowns before. The lead's options: (a) the list over the field, the current entry at the
  field's place with a check, as a macOS pop-up button; (b) the current entry checked, the list
  below as now; (c) the current entry left out; the lead recommended (a).

The rule that follows is in [conventions › Dialogs, reviews and status lines](conventions.md#dialogs-reviews-and-status-lines).

**Built 2026-10-20** (for the lead), the lead's decisions, open to revision:

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the slider's range comes from (GW2) | (a) the schema's bounds; (b) the window, by the field's name `replicas`; (c) the command, beside its schema | **(c)**: `Spec.Dialog`, a `DialogField` per parameter (`engine/menu.go`); Scale's replicas `SliderMin` 1, `SliderMax` 30 ([`workloads.go`](../../internal/engine/commands/workloads.go)) | The schema says 0 to 65535: a slider over that is useless, and the schema is what agents read, so it stays. (b) would put a command into the window ("the UI is thin and data-driven"); with (c) any command can give a whole number a slider, and `Register` refuses one on a non-integer, outside the schema's bounds or without room |
| How the slider and the count behave | — | the slider 1 to 30 and a count field beside it, five digits wide, bound both ways: a drag writes the count; a typed count moves the slider, beyond its range to its nearer end (50 at 30, 0 at 1); the count is what is sent; 0 is only typed, sent as before and confirmed as destructive by the engine (`Escalate`); empty or refused: the dialog says why under the field and greys Scale ([`paramdialog.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/paramdialog.go) `newBoundSlider`) | The owner's "höhere Zahlen eintippen": the count field holds every value, the slider the common ones; a slider field always has a value |
| What a hint says (GW6) | (a) the schema's description as it is; (b) a person's text in the window; (c) a person's text beside the schema, in the command (`DialogField.Hint`), the description where there is none | **(c)**: Scale's replicas and Drain's five options rewritten ([`nodes.go`](../../internal/engine/commands/nodes.go) `drainDialog`): "The number of pods. Drag up to 30 or type up to 65,535; 0 stops every pod and is confirmed first." | The descriptions speak to agents (kubectl's flags, "default true. false refuses", "required to run"); (b) would keep the two texts in two layers that drift apart; a test refuses a hint with "--", "kubectl", "default" or "required to run" (`TestDialogHintsSpeakToAPerson`) |
| Where the hint shows | under the field (before); the tooltip of a "?" after the name (the owner) | a "?" (Fyne's question icon, 14 points, muted) right after the field's name; the whole name cell (the names' column wide, the row tall) shows the tooltip after the usual 450 ms, so the pointer need not hit the icon; a click shows it at once, a second hides it (`fieldName`) | The owner's; the cell as the target because a 14-point icon is hard to hit; no "?" where a field has no hint |
| A tooltip over a dialog | (a) the shell's tooltip layer; (b) an overlay of its own above the dialog; (c) a layer inside the dialog, its topmost object | **(c)**: `newDialogTooltip`, placed in window coordinates and kept inside the window ([`tooltip.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/tooltip.go)) | Found in Fyne 2.8.2: (a) lies under every overlay, unseen; (b) breaks hover and typing while it shows, since the driver looks for the pointer's object in the top overlay only (`FindObjectAtPositionMatching`) and the keyboard goes to the top overlay's focus |
| The dialog | Fyne's `dialog.NewForm` (before: bold labels, every field stretched to 420 points, a hint line under each) | Cogpit's `dialogFrame` ([`dialogframe.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/dialogframe.go)): Fyne's dialog rebuilt (a modal pop-up, the title top left, Fyne's own paddings as `sizeDialogPadX` and `sizeDialogPadY`, the buttons centred), the rows a table as every Cogpit dialog's (names muted, [D-85](#d-85-dialogs-as-tables-and-an-objects-state-without-its-resourceversion)), as wide as its rows and title | (c) above needs a layer above the buttons and the title needs two texts (next row); neither is reachable inside Fyne's dialog. Measured: every other pixel of a framed dialog within one level of Fyne's |
| Field widths | the dialog's width (before) | a number as wide as the largest the schema allows plus a digit and the entry's padding (65535: five digits; ten without a maximum); a string the search field's width (`sizeSearchWidth`); a check its own; no validation ✓ in the field | The owner's "viel zu breit"; Fyne's ✓ took a narrow field's room, and the problem line says what is wrong |
| The gap after the title's arrow (GW2) | (a) "->"; (b) "›", which Noto Sans has; (c) no space after the arrow; (d) the title as two texts, "Scale Deployment →" and " gate-web" | **(d)** in every dialog whose title names an object: Scale, Drain, Rollback, Debug, Install, the Config Map's and the Secret's save review, Argo CD's Sync and Refresh (`objectDialogTitle`) | Found: the arrow comes from Fyne's symbol font (InterSymbols), which has no space; go-text keeps a space after a glyph in that glyph's font (`ignoreFaceChange`), so it is drawn as the missing glyph, 13.9 points at 14 where Noto Sans's space is 3.6. Every space character is kept so, and Noto Sans has no arrow; (a) to (c) leave D-100's form, (c) runs the arrow into the name |
| How a dropdown opens (GW5) | (a), (b), (c) as the lead listed them | **(a)**: over the field, the current entry at the field's place, its text where the field's text is, a check before it; the entries before it above, the rest below; no entry twice ([`selectfield.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/selectfield.go)) | The owner's platform does it; (b) still shows the entry twice, (c) changes the list with every choice and hides where the current entry stands |
| One widget or a patch per place | Fyne 2.8.2's Select builds its `PopUpMenu` below the field in the unexported `showPopUp`, called from `Tapped` and `TypedKey`; the menu's scroll is unexported and its ↑ ↓ do not scroll, so a list taller than the window cannot be brought to its current entry | **one widget**, `selectField` (`newSelectField`), in all 19 places: it embeds Fyne's Select (the field, its look, `Options`, `Selected`, `SetSelected`, `OnChanged`) and replaces `Tapped` and `TypedKey` with a list of its own in a Fyne pop-up, a row per entry as tall as the field, scrolled so that the current entry still sits at the field when the window has no room (a chart's hundreds of versions) | Embedding keeps every call site's code; the list could not be placed or scrolled through Fyne's menu |
| Keys | — | as Fyne's: Space, ↑ and ↓ open, ← and → step without the list; in the list ↑ ↓, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End, a letter (the next entry starting with it), Return, Enter or Space choose, Escape closes; the field has the keyboard again after | Fyne's keys kept; a letter as a macOS menu takes it |
| What agents see | — | unchanged: a choice reaches the code through `OnChanged` as before, so the same commands and state | AGENTS.md rule 2 |
| What else closes the list | — | a click outside it, the field moving or changing its size, the field getting other entries (a chart's versions loaded) | The list would no longer lie over the field or show its entries |
| Select entries (an editable field with a list: the create dialogs' names, the time zone, the agent's model) | change them too; leave them | left as they are | An editable field's list stands below it on macOS too (a combo box); the owner's finding is the Select's double |

Tests: the engine's `TestDialogFieldHintsAndSliders`, `TestDialogFieldsAreChecked`,
`TestDialogHintsSpeakToAPerson`; the window's `TestScaleDialogPrefilled`, `TestScaleSliderAndCount`,
`TestScaleToZeroIsSent`, `TestParamHintIsATooltip`, `TestDrainDialogFields`,
`TestDialogTitleShapesTheArrowApart`, `TestSelectOpensOverTheField`, `TestSelectKeys`,
`TestSelectMouse`, `TestSelectWithoutChoice`, `TestSelectLongList`,
`TestSelectClosesWhenItsOptionsChange`. Renders: `scale_dialog_*.png`, `scale_dialog_hint_*.png`,
`drain_dialog_*.png`, `rollback_dialog_*.png`, `rollback_dropdown_*.png` (new), and the titles of
`debug_dialog_*.png`, `configmap_save_*.png`, `configmap_keys_review_*.png`, `secret_save_*.png`,
`secret_keys_review_*.png`, `helm_install_preview_dark.png`, `helm_install_preview_origin_dark.png`,
`argocd_sync_dialog_dark.png`, `argocd_refresh_dialog_light.png`.

**What it does not cover:** the "?" takes no keyboard focus: a hint is reached by the pointer, hover
or click; Drain's Grace period stays empty at first (its default 0 is left out of the prefill, as
before); a single text with a space after the arrow still shows the gap elsewhere (a toast's
"8080 → checkout-api:8080", an upgrade's Chart row "web 0.1.0 → 0.2.0", a Secret's "28 B → 27 B"):
the same Fyne cause, not changed; an open list closes, not moves, when the window is resized; seen
in offscreen renders and Fyne's test driver only, not yet in a real window; Windows and Linux not
tried.

## D-105: Reverse video as a state, and a key's modifiers from the key itself

**The owner's findings (gate walk of 2026-10-20, v0.30.0, [G16](../parity/gaps.md)):** GW7, zsh's
highlight of pasted text, which it keeps until Enter, drawn by Cogpit's terminal as broken blocks,
cell by cell: "Sieht echt komisch aus, muss angepasst werden." GW8, three lines pasted at once while
he took a screenshot with ⇧⌘4 (the shortcut confirmed by him the same day): `;23;2` landed in the
command line ("kubectl get pods -A | head -;23;2", run, failed), and Enter sent nothing until a click
outside the terminal and back in. Built with the lead's decisions below, open to revision; the
patches are the fork's ([PATCHES.md › Found in the owner's gate walk](../../third_party/fyne-terminal/PATCHES.md#found-in-the-owners-gate-walk-2026-10-20)).

**GW7, the cause (verified 2026-10-20):** zsh highlights a paste with reverse video (its
`zle_highlight` default `paste:standout`, SGR 7 and SGR 27 for `xterm-256color`). What macOS's zsh 5.9
sends, captured in a pseudo-terminal with a clean `ZDOTDIR`: alone, one run (`ESC[7m` the text
`ESC[27m`); with oh-my-zsh, SGR 7 again part way (`ESC[7mkubectl get ESC[7mp ESC[7mods -A | head
-3ESC[27m`); with oh-my-zsh and zsh-syntax-highlighting 0.8, SGR 7 before every character
(`ESC[7mk ESC[7mu ESC[7mb …`). Both plugins are installed in the owner's oh-my-zsh; his `.zshrc`
was not read. The terminal widget took each SGR 7 as "swap the current colours", so the second one
swapped them back: every other character plain, the owner's broken blocks (the render of that form
before the fix shows exactly them). In ECMA-48 and xterm, SGR 7 sets a rendition; it does not toggle one.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reverse video | (a) a state, applied when a character is written, as in xterm; (b) upstream's swap, but an SGR 7 while reversed ignored; (c) repeated SGR 7 dropped by Cogpit's escape filter | **(a)** (`reverse`, `cellColors` in the fork's [`color.go`](../../third_party/fyne-terminal/color.go)) | (b) still drops the colours set before SGR 7 at SGR 27 (upstream cleared both) and gives a colour set while reversed the wrong role; (c) leaves the widget wrong for every other source, and the filter does not track attributes |
| The default colours, reversed | (a) upstream's: the theme's text colour as the background, `DisabledButton` as the text; (b) the theme's background as the text | **(a)** | `DisabledButton` is a shade from the background in both of Cogpit's themes (#00212b against #002b36, #eee8d5 against #fdf6e3), and keeping upstream's choice keeps the patch narrow for offering upstream |
| An erase while reversed | (a) the current colours unswapped, as xterm erases (the background colour, not the inverse); (b) reversed, as upstream's swap left it | **(a)** | xterm's behaviour, which full-screen programs assume; under (a) it no longer depends on how SGR 7 is stored |

**Tests:** `TestReverseVideo` (the fork's: SGR 7 before every character and part way, colours kept
across it and set while it is on, SGR 0 and SGR 27, an erase; it failed on the old code with every
other cell swapped back); the renders `TestRenderTerminalPasteHighlightDark` and `…Light`
([`termhighlight_test.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/termhighlight_test.go)), PNGs
[dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/terminal_paste_highlight_dark.png) and
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/terminal_paste_highlight_light.png): a three-line paste in
the form oh-my-zsh and zsh-syntax-highlighting send, one run per line.

**GW8, the cause (verified in the code and with zsh 2026-10-20; the screenshot overlay itself not
seen):** the terminal widget kept ⇧, Ctrl and Alt itself, set by the KeyDown and cleared by the
KeyUp it saw, and reset only when it lost the focus. ⇧⌘4's ⇧ went down in Cogpit's window; macOS's
screenshot overlay then takes the keys, their releases included (it answers Escape and Space; inferred,
not seen), and the release never reached the widget, so ⇧ stayed held. With ⇧ held the widget sent ← and → as `ESC [ D ; 2` and `ESC [ C ; 2`,
which zsh reads as the arrow followed by the typed text `;2`, and it sent nothing for Return, which
had no form with ⇧. Fed to macOS's zsh in a pseudo-terminal after a paste of `… | head -3`, ← and →
give exactly the owner's `head -;23;2` (which keys he pressed is not known). A click outside the
terminal and back calls the widget's `FocusLost`, which reset the keys: the owner's cure. The other
two suspects are ruled out: ⇧⌘4 reaches a focused terminal only as a ⌘ shortcut, for which the
widget never sent anything (GLFW passes no character with ⌘), and a paste goes in one write with
both bracketed-paste markers. The window keeping the focus through the overlay is inferred from the
bug: had it lost it, GLFW's focus loss would have reset the keys.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where a key's modifiers come from | (a) each key's own event: the desktop driver's `CurrentKeyModifiers`, which Fyne writes from the event (GLFW: NSEvent's `modifierFlags`) before it hands the key on; (b) the widget's own state, also reset on a focus change and on a click; (c) both, the state checked against the event | **(a)**, the widget keeps no modifier state (`keyModifiers` in the fork's [`input.go`](../../third_party/fyne-terminal/input.go); `KeyDown` and `KeyUp` do nothing) | (b) only narrows the window: the bug shows the overlay came and went without a focus change the widget saw, and nothing tells the widget that a key went up elsewhere. (a) is exact while the key is handled, the rule Cogpit already follows for a click's modifiers (`tablecheck.go`, G16 2026-10-19). (c) keeps a second truth for nothing |
| A drag's block selection (⌥) | (a) ⌥ at the press, from `MouseDown`'s event; (b) the tracked ⌥ as before | **(a)** (`pressAlt`) | the last reader of the tracked state; the same stale ⌥ made every later drag a block |
| The sequences with ⇧ | (a) xterm's, as the terminfo entry Cogpit sets (`TERM=xterm-256color`) names them: `CSI 1;2 A`–`D`, `CSI 1;2 P`–`S`, `CSI n;2 ~`, `CSI Z` for ⇧Tab; a key without one (Return, Enter, Backspace, Escape) as without ⇧; (b) upstream's, with only Return added | **(a)** (`typeModifiedKey`) | upstream's `ESC [ A ; 2` is read by no program as one key and leaves `;2` in a shell's line whenever ⇧ is really held with an arrow; its ⇧F1–⇧F3 and nothing for ⇧Tab and ⇧Return did not match the terminfo either |
| Ctrl with a named key (found on the way: the widget sent the control character of the name's first letter, Ctrl+↓ and Ctrl+Delete `^D`, which ends a shell at an empty prompt and so a pod shell, Ctrl+↑ `^U`, Ctrl+← `^L`, Ctrl+→ and Ctrl+Return `^R`) | (a) xterm's sequence with the parameter 5, 6 with ⇧ (`CSI 1;5 B`, `CSI 3;5 ~`), nothing for a named key without one (Return, Tab, Backspace, Escape); (b) nothing for every named key; (c) left as it was | **(a)**, a commit of its own so that it can go alone; the lead's change at review: Return, Enter and Backspace with Ctrl go as without it (CR, DEL), as xterm and Terminal.app send them and as ⇧'s rule above does, so a Ctrl still held at Return runs the line; Tab and Escape with Ctrl send nothing | the terminfo Cogpit sets names these sequences (kDN5, kDC5 and the like), programs that read terminfo take them, and oh-my-zsh binds Ctrl+← and Ctrl+→ to word movement (`lib/key-bindings.zsh`); a shell without a binding types the sequence's tail (`;5D` in a plain zsh 5.9, measured), as with any terminal that sends xterm's sequences, which (b) would avoid at the price of the programs that use them. (c) keeps a key that ends a pod shell by accident |

**Tests:** `TestTypedKey_ShiftReleaseNeverSeen` (⇧ and ⌘ down, never up; ←, → and Return: on the
old code `ESC [ D ; 2 ESC [ C ; 2` and no Return), `TestKeyModifiers_FromTheDesktopDriver` (a
desktop driver's modifiers reach the key), `TestDragged_BlockFromThePress` (⌥ at the press makes a
block, an ⌥ seen going down long before does not; both failed on the old code),
`TestTerminal_TypedKey`'s ⇧ rows and `TestTerminal_TypedShortcut`'s Ctrl rows (xterm's sequences;
the Ctrl rows failed on the old code), `TestTypedShortcut_ScreenshotKeysSendNothing`
and `TestPaste_BracketedWithBothMarkers` (the two other suspects, which passed on the old code too).

**What it does not cover:** a real window: neither the screenshot overlay taking the keys nor the
window keeping the focus through it was seen, only the code of GLFW and Fyne read and the bug's
course matched; the renders are Fyne's software painter. The owner's own zsh configuration (not
read; the forms of GW7 come from the oh-my-zsh and plugins installed on his Mac). Highlighted text
written before a switch between dark and light keeps the old theme's colours, as before. ⌥ with an
arrow or another named key sends nothing, and Ctrl with Tab or Escape too
(PATCHES.md › Known and not patched). macOS's default keyboard shortcuts give Ctrl with the arrows
to Mission Control and Spaces, so on a Mac those keys may never reach Cogpit (not checked here).

## D-106: The gate walk's GW1, GW3, GW4 and GW9: the drawer, ⌘F, moving tabs, a deleted namespace

**The owner's findings (gate walk of 2026-10-20 on v0.30.0, the staging cluster;
[G16](../parity/gaps.md#g16-stability-and-the-user-bug-backlog)), built the same day with the
owner's go-ahead.** GW1: a click on the empty area below a list's rows should deselect the shown
pod, so that its drawer closes. GW3: ⌘F does not open the Helm Upgrade tab's find bar, only its
magnifier does. GW4: "Man muss Tab beliebig anordnen können." GW9: a list filtered to a namespace
that was deleted meanwhile shows "No pods match the filter." under the same filter button; the
owner's choice, "nur eine ganz kleine Anpassung": a namespace still selected but deleted is marked
red in the filter's list, like a crashing pod, and unticked it leaves the selection and the list; no
further button or logic.

Every choice below is the lead's decision (2026-10-20), open to revision.

**GW1, a click below a list's rows**

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| What the click ends | (a) the shown row and its drawer; (b) also the checked rows (the bulk actions' selection) | **(a)**: `ui.closeDrawer`, so the drawer's row is no longer marked; the checked rows stay ([`tableclick.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/tableclick.go)) | The owner decided in A73 that a click on a row keeps the checked rows; a click beside them keeping them too is the same rule. Checked rows are built up one by one for Delete or Restart, and a click below the rows is where one clicks to put the drawer away: (b) would throw them away by accident. The selection bar's Clear and the header's checkbox end them on purpose. Lens's behaviour is not captured |
| Where "below the rows" is | the table's own area under its last row; also the gaps between rows | **under the last row, in the table's body** (a short list, or an empty one under its header); the gaps stay Fyne's, which selects nothing there | A gap between two rows is a near miss of a row, not the empty area the owner meant |
| Without a drawer | send `ui.closeDrawer` anyway; nothing | **nothing** (`shell.closeDrawer` sends only while one is open) | No command, no audit entry for a click that changes nothing |

Tests: `TestClickBelowTheRowsClosesTheDrawer` (the drawer closes through `ui.closeDrawer`, the checked
row stays, the header and the last row are not below the rows, a full list has no such area).

**GW3, ⌘F in the dock's editor tabs**

Before: View › Search's ⌘F focused the list's search unless the focused widget took shortcuts; the
YAML editor did and ignored the key ("the editor keeps its ⌘F", A55, but it had no find of its own),
so ⌘F never reached a find bar; only the magnifier opened one.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Which tabs | the Helm Upgrade tab the owner named; every dock tab with a YAML editor | **every one: Edit, Create, Helm Upgrade, Helm Install** ([`findkeys.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/findkeys.go)); the Edit tab, which had none, gets the same find bar below its editor | One key, one behaviour in every editor; Lens's editor (Monaco) finds on ⌘F in each of them |
| The Edit tab's way in | ⌘F only; also a magnifier | **⌘F only** | The Edit tab has no toolbar (its buttons sit in the footer beside Save); a magnifier there would be a button the owner did not ask for. Lens's Edit tab has none either (Monaco's find is ⌘F) |
| When ⌘F is the editor tab's | (a) whenever the dock shows such a tab; (b) by where the keyboard is: in that tab, or nowhere | **(b)**: the editor (yamlview's new `OnFind`), another field of the tab (the Install tab's name, a find field) or no focus at all (after a click on the tab's buttons, which takes the focus away in Fyne) opens the tab's find bar; the keys in the list (its table, its search) keep ⌘F the list's search | (a) would take the list's ⌘F away for as long as an editor tab is open below it, after a click on a row too; (b) is how an IDE routes find, by the pane with the keys. "Whether or not the editor has focus" holds for the editor tab the user works in: nothing focused there is the common case after the magnifier, Save or a version |
| ⌘F on an open find bar | toggle it closed, as the magnifier does; keep it open | **keep it open, the keys back in its field** | ⌘F means "find", never "stop finding"; Escape and the bar's × close it |
| An Edit tab showing its review (the diff) | the find bar over the diff; the list's search | **the list's search** | The review has no editor to find in |
| How the key reaches it | per platform | macOS: the View › Search item's key equivalent asks the dock first (`windowKey.claim`), before the focused widget; Windows and Linux: the editor's own ⌘F (`OnFind`), else the window's shortcut (`shell.searchKey`); a focused text field there keeps the key as before | AppKit runs the menu item before the window sees the key, so on macOS a field of the tab cannot swallow it; elsewhere Fyne offers the key to the focused widget first |

Tests: `TestCmdFOpensTheEditorTabsFindBar` (each of the four tabs: the editor's keys by the key
equivalent and by the key itself, no focus by both ways in, the list's keys, the dock collapsed),
`TestCmdFInAnEditTabsReview`; `TestWindowKeysInTheViewMenu` unchanged. PNG: the Edit tab's find bar
opened by ⌘F, [dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/edit_find_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/edit_find_light.png).

**GW4, moving tabs** ([`engine/tabmove.go`](../../internal/engine/tabmove.go), [`commands/tabmove.go`](../../internal/engine/commands/tabmove.go), [`stripdrag.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/stripdrag.go))

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The command | one `ui.tab.move` with a place; also left and right | **`ui.tab.move` {id (empty: the active tab), index from 1}**, "Move Tab", `DangerUI`; and **`ui.tab.moveLeft`, `ui.tab.moveRight`** for the keyboard | The order is UI state, so every way of moving goes through a command agents see; `index` is the bar's place as `ui.tab.select`'s is. Left and right are commands of their own as next and previous are, so that a menu item carries the registry's label and shortcut |
| Which places count | (a) the place among every tab; (b) among the tabs the bar shows | **(b)**: among the shown cluster's tabs (`TabsShown`, GW11); the tab goes right before the shown tab that is to follow it, or right after the last shown one, so the other clusters' hidden tabs keep their places among the rest; a tab the bar does not show is refused | What the user drags is what the bar shows; an agent's `index` means what `ui.tab.select`'s does |
| The keyboard | none; a menu item; a key | **View › Move Tab Left and Right, ⌘⌥⇧← and ⌘⌥⇧→** (Ctrl+Alt+Shift off macOS), greyed with the reason at the bar's ends | Cheap beside ⌘⌥← and ⌘⌥→ (previous and next tab), the same keys with ⇧; they reach a tab beyond the bar's visible part, which the drag does not (below). The keys are not Lens's (not captured) |
| The dock | the tab bar only; the dock's too | **the dock's too**, by its own `dock.move` {id, index among the tabs the dock shows}, the same drag; no keys (the dock has no keyboard tab commands to pair them with) | The lead's detail of the finding; one strip behaviour in the window. The dock's tabs are not kept across a restart (D-41), so neither is their order |
| What survives a restart | — | the tab bar's order, with the tabs (`workspace.json` keeps them in their order; `TestMovedTabsSurviveARestart`) | Restored where tabs are restored, as the finding asks |
| How the drag looks | (a) the hotbar's ghost over the window; (b) the tab itself carried along the bar | **(b)**: past `minTileDrag` the tab follows the pointer in the bar's line, held where it was grabbed, raised as the active tab with a drop shadow, drawn over the others; the others slide aside (`tileSlide`, eased out) to leave the gap a drop fills; the drop sends the command and the tab glides into its slot; Reduce motion jumps | The hotbar's live movement and drop position (D-83), turned sideways; a tab bar is one row, so a card over the window would only cover the views |
| The drop position | the hotbar's fixed pitch; the tabs' own widths | **the slot whose left edge, counted over the other tabs' own widths, is nearest the carried tab's**, fixed for the drag | Tabs differ in width; computed from the widths, not from where the others are drawn, a tab sliding away never flips the choice back |
| What moves nothing | — | a drop more than the bar's height above or below it, on the tab's own place, or after the tabs changed under the drag (an agent moved, opened or closed one); a drag shorter than `minTileDrag` is the click that slipped: it shows the tab, or closes it when pressed on its × (Fyne starts a drag of the tab after 2 points, the × being no draggable of its own, and then taps nothing) | As the hotbar's drop outside the bar and its stale drag; a close that jittered must still close |
| Scrolling near the edge | scroll by itself as the hotbar does; no | **no** | A tab bar that overflows is rare and scrolls with the wheel or the trackpad; ⌘⌥⇧← and ⌘⌥⇧→ move the active tab past the edge. It would add a ticker and its audit row for little |

Tests: `TestMoveTab`, `TestTabStep`, `TestMoveDockTab`, `TestMovedTabsSurviveARestart` (engine);
`TestTabMoveCommands` (an agent's move, the bar's ends, the dock); `TestTabDragMovesTheTab` (carried,
the others aside before anything is sent, the drop's `ui.tab.move`, a drop below the bar, a stale
drag, a short drag as a click, on the × as a close), `TestTabMoveMenuItems`, `TestDockTabDragMovesTheTab` (window). PNGs:
a tab carried, [dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/tabbar_drag_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/tabbar_drag_light.png); after the drop,
[dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/tabbar_moved_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/tabbar_moved_light.png).

**GW9, a deleted namespace in the namespace filter** ([`nsgone.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/nsgone.go), [`nsfilter.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/nsfilter.go))

The owner's choice stands as he made it (2026-10-20, "Das wäre recht simpel und führt jetzt nicht zu
weiteren Button und Logik"): red in the list, unticked it leaves the selection and the list; no
notice line, no "Remove from filter", no automatic removal.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| A Terminating namespace | mark it as a deleted one; leave it plain | **red too**, selected or not; unticked it stays in the list, unchecked | Nothing can be created in it either, and it is about to go; it still exists, so it stays offered (its objects can still be watched while it drains, D-98) |
| Colour alone or a word too | red only, as the owner said; red and the state after the name | **red and the state**: "cogpit-gate · deleted", "orders · terminating", both in the status error colour (`colorStatusError`, a crashing pod's) | A mark that rests on colour alone is lost to a colour-blind user and asks "why red?"; a word in the row is no button and no logic |
| The filter's button | unchanged; red | **red label and arrow while a namespace it names is deleted or terminating**, one or several alike (a theme override on the button, `nsTintTheme`) | The owner's case was a closed filter reading "cogpit-gate" over an empty list: the button is where he looked. No tooltip, no text change: nothing beyond the colour he chose |
| Where gone and going come from | the API server; the cache's namespaces through `resources.list`; a new engine field | **the cache through `resources.list`**, as the list's names already came: a row whose status is `terminating` (the namespace's phase or its deletion time), a name the filter holds that the list lacks is deleted | Cache first, no new engine state: the mark is how the window shows data agents read the same way. Nothing is marked while the user may not list namespaces (`namespacesListable`), or before the shown cluster's names are read (`nsFor`), since nothing is known |
| When it is read | at the filter's opening only; on a timer; when the view's rows change | **at the cluster's showing and every opening (as before), and while the filter names namespaces after the view's rows changed, at most every 2 s** (`shell.recheckNamespaces`; a change within the 2 s is read once they are over) | Deleting a namespace deletes its objects, which changes the rows of every view filtered to it, so the button turns red with no click; a timer would poll what nothing changed. **Gap:** a namespace that goes while no row of the view changes (a filter to a namespace without objects of the kind in a quiet cluster) reads red at the filter's next opening or the next change of the rows |
| Untick of a deleted one | — | **`ui.setNamespace` without it**, as any untick; the open list is made again when what it offers changed, keeping the typed text and the keyboard | The owner's "leaves the selection and the list", through the engine so agents see it |

**The side finding, verified and fixed.** The filter's list came from one `resources.list` without
a limit, which answers 100 rows: a cluster with more namespaces offered only the first 100 by name
(`TestResourcesListPagesThroughEveryNamespace` on a fake cluster of 152 namespaces: total 152,
returned 100). Options: (a) ask for the command's most, 1,000, still a cap; (b) a command of its
own for the namespaces' names; (c) an `offset` on `resources.list`, read page by page. **Chosen (c):**
`resources.list` takes `offset` (rows to skip, in the name order; a negative one is refused), and
the window reads 1,000 a page until it has `total`; agents get the same way past 1,000 rows, and no
second command lists what `resources.list` lists (`TestNamespaceFilterOffersEveryNamespace` with
1,250 namespaces).

Tests: `TestDeletedNamespaceMarkedInTheFilter`, `TestNamespaceDeletedWhileFiltered` (the owner's
case: Terminating, then deleted, read after the rows changed, nothing read without a filter),
`TestTerminatingNamespaceMarkedInTheFilter`, `TestNamespaceFilterMarksNothingItCannotKnow`,
`TestNamespaceFilterOffersEveryNamespace`, `TestResourcesListPagesThroughEveryNamespace`; the
timer's row in [ui-threads.md](ui-threads.md) (`TestEveryGoroutineSiteIsAudited`). PNG: a deleted
and a terminating namespace selected, another terminating one not, the button red,
[dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/namespace_filter_gone_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/namespace_filter_gone_light.png).

**Not verified in a real window**, for any of the four: the drag's feel with the GL driver and a
trackpad, ⌘F and ⌘⌥⇧←/→ through AppKit's key equivalents, the red filter button on the owner's
display. A namespace that goes while no row of a view filtered to it changes reads red only at the
filter's next opening (GW9's gap above).

## D-107: The navigator slides, and Reduce motion

**The owner's requests (2026-10-20), built the same day and tried by the owner in a development build
before the commit ("Sehr cool, sieht gut aus"; "Stark, das passt für mich").** First: "Klickt man in
der All Clusters Übersicht auf einen Cluster, schiebt sich die Cluster Ansicht von rechts rein und
die All Clusters wird überdeckt. Klickt man in der Cluster Übersicht auf ‚All Clusters', schiebt
sich die aktuelle Cluster Ansicht wieder nach rechts raus." Second, with mixed environments (D-69,
GW11): switching from "Pods - wds18-stage" to "Pods - wds18-main" changes the cluster shown, and
that change slides vertically, in the order All Clusters lists the clusters: "wds18-main steht bei
mir unter wds18-stage, deshalb soll bei einem Wechsel von main nach stage: stage von oben
reinkommen und main nach unten rausschieben." Third: "ab jetzt einen Schalter in den Cogpit App
Settings für ‚weniger Bewegung' und diese Animationen zu deaktivieren. Ich mag sie, andere
vielleicht nicht."

Built in [`navigator_slide.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/navigator_slide.go) (the slides),
[`sidebar.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/sidebar.go) (`scopeChanged` starts them),
[`navigator_sections.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/navigator_sections.go) (`listedAbove`, the
order) and [`preferences_motion.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/preferences_motion.go) (the
preference's row and `shell.reduceMotion`); the preference `reduceMotion` in
[`engine/preferences.go`](../../internal/engine/preferences.go) and `preferences.set`. Fyne 2.8
gives what it needs: `container.NewClip` (since 2.7) keeps the moving tree inside the navigator,
`fyne.NewAnimation` moves it, its ticks on the main goroutine before each frame.

Every choice below is the lead's decision (2026-10-20), open to revision.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| What slides sideways | the level below the header; the header too | **the level below the header**: the clusters stay where they are, the cluster's tree (its root row included) moves over them and back; the header switches at once | The header reads "All Clusters" at either level (D-57), only its ‹ and + change; moving two nearly equal headers would show a flicker of the same words |
| Its timing | Fyne's default ease in and out; a quarter second easing out; longer | **250 ms, easing out**, a 12-point shadow on the tree's left edge while it moves | Easing out starts at speed, so the click answers at once; a quarter second reads as a push without making a cluster switch wait |
| What starts a slide | the click and ‹ only; every change of the scope | **every change of the scope**: a click, ←, ↵, ⌘P, the hotbar, an agent's `ui.setNavigatorScope`; not the first scope a window shows | The scope is engine state (D-57); what the window shows when it changes should not depend on who changed it. The first scope is no change the user made |
| A slide turned back halfway | finish it, then the new one; reverse from where it is | **from where it is**, in its share of the time; a slide of the other kind (sideways, vertical) first ends the one that runs | A second click on ‹ or a row while it moves answers at once; the end state is always the last slide's, since each says which level stays shown |
| Which cluster changes slide vertically | tab switches with mixed environments on only; every change from one cluster's tree to another's | **every one**: a tab of another cluster, a hotbar tile, an agent | The owner described what he sees: the cluster view changes; the hotbar changes it the same way, mixed environments on or off |
| The order of the vertical slide | the hotbar's; the tab bar's; All Clusters' | **All Clusters'**, unfiltered and with collapsed groups counted (`listedAbove`): the cluster listed above comes in from above, pushing the old one down; a cluster not listed counts as below every other | The owner named All Clusters' order |
| How the leaving cluster is drawn | a second tree built from a copy of the old cluster's state; a picture | **a picture**: `Canvas.Capture` reads the frame on screen when the scope changes, before the new cluster is drawn, cut to the navigator; it moves out beside the live tree and is dropped at the end | The tree is one widget drawn from the shown cluster's state (its rows, open groups, root row); a second one would mean a copy of all of it for 250 ms. The picture is taken only when the slide still runs after `Start` (Fyne's test driver ends an animation inside it), so tests take none |
| Reduce motion's reach | the navigator's slides only; every motion Cogpit has | **every motion**: the navigator's slides, the hotbar's and the strips' drags (their slide and glide, D-83, D-106), the reconnecting dot's blink (F13) | One switch named "Reduce motion" that leaves some of Cogpit moving would be a switch the user cannot trust |
| macOS's Reduce motion | ignored now that Cogpit has its own; the preference or macOS's | **either one stops all of it** (`shell.reduceMotion`) | The drags and the blink already followed macOS's setting (System Settings › Accessibility › Display); the slides follow it too, so the computer's accessibility setting never stops only part of Cogpit's motion. Cogpit's preference can only add stillness, never undo macOS's |
| The preference | default on or off; who may set it | **off by default** (the owner likes the slides); **agents and the CLI may set it either way** | It changes only how the window moves, like mixed environments |

Tests: `TestNavigatorSlideSettles`, `TestNavigatorSlideBetweenClusters` (the direction by the
order, the picture gone once settled), `TestNavigatorSlideReduceMotion`,
`TestReduceMotionIsThePreferenceOrTheSystems` (the four combinations, the drags and the blink ask
the same), `TestPreferencesReduceMotion`, `TestPreferencesCommands` (an agent's either way). The
first full run found a real bug: `container.NewClip` calls `ExtendBaseWidget` only in its own
`MinSize`, which the navigator's layout never asks, so Fyne's focus walk, which enters rendered
widgets only, did not find the tree or the clusters (↓ from the search field and Escape left the
keys in the field); `newNavSlide` calls it. PNGs: halfway into a cluster,
[dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_slide_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_slide_light.png); from kind-cogpit to prod,
the picture of the old tree leaving upwards,
[dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_swap_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/navigator_swap_light.png); Preferences › App with the
row, [dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/preferences_restore_session_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/preferences_restore_session_light.png).

**Not verified, and these are the gaps.** The owner looked at both slides in a development build
on the owner's Mac, which is the only check in a real window. Not measured: what the picture costs, a read
of the whole window's frame and a copy of the navigator's part, once at the start of a cluster
change (estimated at 20–40 ms on a Retina display). Not tried: a click during the 250 ms, which Fyne
may deliver to the part of the moving tree outside the navigator, since its hit test does not
follow the clip.

## D-108: Cogpit for Linux: a .deb and an APT repository on Pages

**The owner's request (2026-10-20 evening):** "ich will dass du für dieses Projekt auf diesem
Ubuntu Rechner die Linux Version dieses Tools baust und über github ci bereitstellst … Die
Installation soll über einen deb-Download über die Github releases durchgeführt werden und dann
über automatische updates up2date gehalten werden." Asked how updates arrive (an APT repository
whose releases install silently, the same with a confirmation, or an updater of Cogpit's own
without a repository), the owner answered: "Es geht hier um allgemeine User, nicht mich. Ich
entscheide nicht für andere User. Geht ein Apt Repo über gh-pages?" So the package sets up
Cogpit's signed APT repository on GitHub Pages, and whether apt installs its releases silently is
each user's own system setting (the Software Updater, unattended-upgrades), never the package's.
The owner's other answers the same evening: a new signing key in a GitHub environment `apt`
without a required reviewer, tags `v*` only; packages for amd64 and arm64. This brings Linux ahead
of the macOS beta and M11 ([D-7](#d-7-language-and-platforms)); Windows stayed with M11 until the
owner brought it forward on 2026-10-21 ([D-111](#d-111-cogpit-for-windows-an-nsis-setup-and-winsparkle)).

**Built 2026-10-20 night.** The package: `make dist-linux VERSION=x.y.z`
([`hack/linux/deb.sh`](../../hack/linux/deb.sh), the files in
[`packaging/linux`](../../packaging/linux)) builds `dist/linux/cogpit_<version>_<arch>.deb` with both
binaries built as the macOS app's are (the release's tags, [D-67](#d-67-the-demo-cluster-stays-out-of-releases),
[D-103](#d-103-fynes-thread-check-a-build-parameter-off-in-releases)), `/usr/bin/cogpit` and
`/usr/bin/cogpit-cli`, the launcher and its icons, an AppStream entry, the update helper
`/usr/libexec/cogpit/update` with its polkit action `io.guided-traffic.cogpit.update`, and
`/etc/apt/sources.list.d/cogpit.sources`. The repository:
[`hack/linux/apt.sh`](../../hack/linux/apt.sh) (`make apt-repo`, `make apt-verify`) at
`https://guided-traffic.github.io/cogpit/apt`, signed with the key `APT_SIGNING_KEY` of the
environment `apt` (Ed25519, fingerprint `BE09 5407 4B36 CBDE 8875  7E52 A9D2 608B 0DC7 6494`,
expires 2031-10-19; its public half in
[`packaging/linux/cogpit-archive-keyring.asc`](../../packaging/linux/cogpit-archive-keyring.asc)).
The release pipeline's jobs "Cogpit.deb (Linux amd64)", "(Linux arm64)", "Attach to the release
(Linux)", "APT repository (sign)" and "APT repository (deploy to Pages)"
([releasing › Linux](releasing.md#linux)); CI's job "Linux Package" builds and checks the package
on every push (`make test-linux-package`). The app's updater on Linux:
[`internal/update/apt_linux.go`](../../internal/update/apt_linux.go), the engine's
`UpdateRestarter`, `UpdateReporter` and `UpdateActor` ([`engine/updates.go`](../../internal/engine/updates.go)),
the button's Restart to Update ([`layoutbar.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/layoutbar.go)). Since the
release after v0.33.0 the MCP details offer the stdio registration of the package's
`/usr/bin/cogpit-cli`, as the macOS app offers its bundle's (`packagedCLIBeside` in
[`bundledcli.go`](../../cmd/cogpit/bundledcli.go)). The trust chain:
[updates › Linux](../security/updates.md#linux).

Every choice below is the lead's decision (2026-10-20), open to revision.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where the repository lives | GitHub Pages beside the appcast; a flat repository in every release (`…/releases/latest/download/`); a repository of its own | **Pages, under `/apt` beside `appcast.xml`** | The owner asked for Pages. A flat repository in the releases serves nothing between a release's creation and its Linux job's upload, several times a day, and a release whose Linux job failed would break every client's `apt update`; Pages changes only when a signed repository that checked is deployed |
| Pages serves one site | one deploy job for both; each deploy keeps the other's part | **each keeps the other's part**: the appcast's deploy fetches the served repository and checks it against the packages' key (`apt.sh mirror`), the repository's deploy copies the served appcast byte for byte; both deploys in the concurrency group `pages` | The appcast waits for the owner's approval (environment `sparkle`), Linux must not wait for it, nor the appcast for Linux |
| Pages' ten-minute cache | nothing; Acquire-By-Hash | **Acquire-By-Hash**, the previous generation's by-hash index files and packages kept | A client that reads an InRelease cached from before a deploy fetches the index that InRelease names, never a newer Packages under an older InRelease (a hash mismatch for ten minutes) |
| How many releases the repository holds | the newest; the two newest; all | **the two newest of each architecture** | An index cached from before the deploy still names the previous package; at about 50 MB a package the site stays near 200 MB of Pages' 1 GB |
| Where the signing job takes the packages from | the releases' assets; this run's artifacts and the served repository | **this run's artifacts and the served repository**, checked against the key before anything of it is kept | The previous package comes with the signed index that vouched for it; nothing is taken unchecked |
| A run of an older release that ends after a newer one's | deploy it; skip it | **skip it, with a warning** (`apt.sh newer`, exit 3) | Its repository would offer the older release to new installs |
| The sources file | written by a maintainer script; a conffile naming a keyring file; a conffile with the key inline | **a conffile, the key inline** (deb822 `Signed-By`) | dpkg keeps a deleted conffile deleted through upgrades, so a user who removes the repository keeps it removed; after `apt remove` the file still names a key it carries, where a keyring file in `/usr/share/keyrings` would be gone and `apt update` fail; `apt purge` removes it. No maintainer scripts at all. An inline key needs apt 2.4, older than every system the package runs on |
| The key | RSA 4096; Ed25519; an expiry | **Ed25519, for signing only, expiring 2031-10-19**, without a passphrase (CI imports it unattended) | apt's gpgv and sqv accept it on every system the package runs on; the expiry bounds a lost key, and a package update can carry a renewed key before it ends. The owner keeps a copy outside GitHub (a secret cannot be read back) |
| Where it signs | in the job that builds; in a job of its own | **a job of its own in the environment `apt`**, on GitHub's hosted runner; no Go and nothing of the packages runs beside the key | As Sparkle's signing ([D-4](#d-4-packaging-and-updates)) |
| The build runners | the organisation's self-hosted runners; GitHub's hosted ones | **GitHub's hosted `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`** | The self-hosted runners are x86-64 only; hosted runners are free for a public repository and a clean machine for every release |
| The oldest system | Ubuntu 22.04 (built there); Ubuntu 24.04 | **Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and later** (dpkg-shlibdeps: glibc 2.38) | GitHub retires its 22.04 runners; 24.04 is the current long-term release |
| The dependencies | dpkg-shlibdeps' alone; with the libraries GLFW loads itself | **with the X11 and Wayland libraries GLFW loads with dlopen, and libdecor with a plugin required** (first only recommended; required since the owner asked on 2026-10-20 night that the window always shows its minimize, maximize and close buttons) | dpkg-shlibdeps sees only libGL, libwayland-client and libc; a system without libX11 would install a Cogpit that opens no window; without libdecor a Wayland desktop that draws no title bars and runs no XWayland shows the window without buttons, also after an install without recommendations |
| The binaries | as `make build` makes them; position-independent | **position-independent** (`-buildmode=pie`) | As Debian builds its own Go programs; lintian asks for it |
| The Maintainer field | the owner's name and address; a project address | **the owner's** (`DEB_MAINTAINER`, overridable) | The project has no address of its own; the owner's is on every commit |
| The app's updater | none (apt and the Software Updater only); reading apt's state; fetching the repository itself | **apt's state** (`apt-cache policy cogpit`: no network, no root) at every start and every hour while the checks are on, and the Update button | D-4's one-click update; apt checks every file against the key, so Cogpit needs no verification of its own |
| How the button installs | `pkexec apt-get`; PackageKit; a helper with its own polkit action | **the package's helper through pkexec**, its polkit action `auth_admin_keep`: it refreshes the list of Cogpit's repository only and upgrades the package `cogpit` only, keeping a changed sources file | One password prompt that names Cogpit; the helper takes no argument a caller could choose; PackageKit is not on every system |
| After the install | restart at once; offer the restart | **offer it**: a toast, and the button reads Restart to Update | A restart the user did not click for would close the window mid-work |
| Help › Check for Updates… with nothing known | apt's lists only; the helper | **the helper** (the password prompt) | A fresh list needs root; the automatic checks need no password |
| Who runs `app.checkForUpdates` on Linux | any origin, as on macOS; the window only | **the window only** (`ErrUpdateCheckGUIOnly`); agents read `ui_state`'s `update` with its `restart` | On Linux the check acts: an agent's call would put a password prompt or a restart in front of the user unasked |
| The checksums | a file per platform; one | **one `SHA256SUMS`**, which the macOS and the Linux attach jobs merge in turn (`hack/ci/sha256sums.sh`, the concurrency group `release-files-<tag>`) | One file to check every download against, as before |
| `cogpit://` links | registered in the desktop file now; later | **later** ([G22](../parity/gaps.md)) | On Linux a link starts a second process, which would need a hand-over to the running Cogpit that does not exist yet |

**Verified (2026-10-20 night).** The package: lintian 2.117 (Ubuntu 24.04's, CI's) without a
finding but the documented overrides, lintian 2.129 (pedantic) with one warning more, of the hyphen
in the AppStream id (the app's id, kept; CI's first run found that the older lintian refuses an
override of that tag); installed in containers of Ubuntu 24.04 (its dependencies from the
archive), upgraded from 0.0.2 to 0.0.3 by the helper from a repository signed with a test key and
served over HTTP, with by-hash and a changed sources file kept; Cogpit's window open under Xvfb
(its WM_CLASS `Cogpit`); `apt remove` keeps the sources file and `apt update` stays quiet, `apt
purge` removes it. The repository's script: `hack/linux/apt-test.sh`, also in CI. The updater:
its tests, the restart script with a real process. **The pipeline, 2026-10-20 night:** v0.33.0 and
v0.34.0 built both packages on GitHub's runners, attached them with one merged `SHA256SUMS`, signed
the repository with the key and deployed it to Pages beside the appcast, which stayed as it was;
the repository holds both releases with both generations' by-hash files, and `apt.sh mirror` checks
it from Pages. **On the owner's workstation** (Ubuntu 26.04, GNOME on Wayland): the v0.33.0 .deb
downloaded from the release, checked against `SHA256SUMS` and installed with apt; `apt update`
read the repository from Pages with the key; Cogpit 0.33.0 started on the desktop showed GNOME's
title bar with minimize, maximize and close (an X11 window through XWayland, as Fyne 2.8 chooses
on GNOME) and, once v0.34.0 was in the repository, the Update button "Update to v0.34.0" from
apt's lists; the helper's two apt commands (run with sudo, since nobody could type polkit's
password at night) upgraded it to 0.34.0 from Pages, the running process then on its deleted file.
In a container, the button's click restarted Cogpit into the installed release (a new process).
**Not verified yet**, and these are the gaps: polkit's password dialog and the click on Restart to
Update in a desktop session; the arm64 package beyond GitHub's ARM runner; an update through
Ubuntu's Software Updater.

## D-109: The menus in the top bar on Windows and Linux

**The owner's decision (2026-10-21 morning), after the first look at Cogpit on Ubuntu:** "Unter
Ubuntu haben wir jetzt 3 Titelleisten? Eine Leiste hält nur die Systembuttons?" GNOME's title bar
with the window's buttons, Fyne's menu bar as a row of its own, and Cogpit's top bar. Asked whether
Cogpit's bar should become the title bar with the window's buttons in it (as on macOS and in Lens),
the menus move into Cogpit's bar under the native title bar, or all stay, the owner chose: "Wir
nutzen zwei Leisten, nativ." The system's title bar stays, with its buttons and everything the
window manager does with it (moving, snapping, a double click, its menu); the menus' titles move
into Cogpit's top bar, at its left before the logo. On macOS nothing changes: its menus are the
system's menu bar and Cogpit's bar is the title bar
([ui-parity › Layout](../parity/ui-parity.md#layout)).

**Built 2026-10-21** in [`menubar.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/menubar.go) (the titles, the open
menu's layer, `shell.setMainMenu`, `installMenuKeys`), [`bars.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/bars.go)
(the titles before the logo, a divider between) and [`fyneui.go`](../../internal/ui/fyneui/fyneui.go)
(the menus' keys once the window started).

Every choice below is the lead's decision (2026-10-21), open to revision.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
