| The menus' keys | the window's shortcuts on its canvas; Cogpit's own text fields forwarding unknown keys; the window's main menu kept for the keys | **the window's main menu, kept for the keys only**: set once, empty, while the window exists, so Fyne 2.8 builds no menu bar for it, then filled, and refilled in place after each rebuild of the menus | Fyne looks a shortcut up in the main menu before the focused widget is offered it; on the canvas a text field would swallow ⌃⇧P and ⌃P (Fyne's field drops every shortcut it does not know), and about 40 fields would have to change. The keys wait for the window's start, since before it Fyne would build its bar later from the filled menu. Fyne logs that an empty main menu has no child menu; that one line is kept out of Cogpit's log. Read in Fyne 2.8.2's source (`glCanvas.buildMenu`, `window.triggerMainMenuShortcut`): a Fyne update that changes either shows its bar again or loses the keys' precedence, which the tests below and a look after an update would show |
| The open menu | Fyne's pop-up menu; a layer of its own as Fyne's menu bar has | **a layer of its own**: Fyne's `widget.Menu` under its title below the bar, the titles' places in the layer, the rest a click on which closes it | Fyne's pop-up menu takes every event while open, so the pointer could not move to the next menu; with the titles' places in the layer, it does, as in a menu bar |
| Keys in an open menu | Fyne's pop-up menu's; with the neighbours | **↑ ↓ ↵ as Fyne's, Escape closes, ← and → go to the neighbouring menu (round) where no submenu takes them** | As a menu bar's |
| Alt | open the first menu, as Fyne's bar did; nothing | **nothing** | Fyne's handling belongs to its bar; the command palette (⌃⇧P) reaches every command from the keyboard |
| Quit | none; at the end of the first menu | **at the end of the first menu** (Cluster), after a separator, without a key | Fyne's bar added it there; GNOME's title bar closes the window too |
| The titles' look | Fyne's menu bar's (a full-height highlight); the bar's buttons' | **the bar's text, a pill behind a title the pointer is on (the theme's hover colour) and behind the open menu's (pressed)**, the titles before the logo, a divider between | They sit in Cogpit's bar beside its other buttons, which are pills |
| Windows | as before; the same as Linux | **the same as Linux** | The same situation: a native frame and Fyne's in-window menu bar; the Windows setup since D-111 |

**Verified (2026-10-21).** Tests (`menubar_test.go`): the titles in the menus' order before the
logo, the window's main menu with the same menus and Quit last in the first, refilled in place;
a title's click opens its menu under it below the bar, the pointer on another title switches, ← and
→ round, Escape, a click outside and a second click close; an item chosen with the keys runs and
closes; the keys wait for the window's start. Offscreen renders with the View menu open:
[dark](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/menubar_dark.png),
[light](../../internal/ui/fyneui/testdata/menubar_light.png). On the owner's workstation (Ubuntu
26.04, GNOME): two bars, GNOME's title bar with its three buttons and Cogpit's bar with the menus
before the logo, no line of Fyne's in the log. In a container with Xvfb and xdotool: a click on
View opens it; with the navigator's search focused and text typed in it, Ctrl+Shift+P opens the
command palette. Not tried: a click on a menu in a desktop session (XTest is refused there without
the owner's consent), Windows.

## D-110: Dark Cockpit, Cogpit's design language

**The owner's request (2026-10-20 evening), built that night, approved 2026-10-21.** The request: "Ich
möchte bitte, dass du auf einem separaten Branch ein neues UI Design ausarbeitest. Der Bezug zu Lens
ist hier nicht mehr wichtig. Wir wollen uns abheben, aber intuitiv bei der Sache bleiben. Unsere
aktuelle UI ist sehr steril, ich spüre kaum Leben in ihr." Its sources were his reference image (a
violet wave "the thinking", cyan tokens of decreasing granularity "the writing", brackets, a grid
floor) and the logo; Apple's elegance, "keinen Kindergarten", surprising but not shocking. Built in
the night on the branch `design-prototype` (PR #65): seven specialist assessments of the window
(visual design, UX, accessibility, SRE, macOS craft, trends, competitors), the palette and the shapes
by the lead, three build tracks (lists and chrome; the Overview and the integrations; drawer,
dialogs, forms, welcome and agent), a designer's critique of each from its renders, and a review
page with before and after, variant studies, an outlook and eight questions. The owner's verdict the
next morning: "Finde ich gut gelungen!", three changes (no cluster in the title bar,
[D-54](#d-54-the-layout-toggles-and-the-update-button); the MCP server opt-in,
[D-49](#d-49-the-external-mcp-servers-switch-honoured-by-cogpit-cli-mcp); the welcome page names a
kubeconfig file only for a name two rows share) and a toggle between light and dark (D-54), then
"Bereite den Merge vor".

What it is lives in [design-language.md](design-language.md): quiet when healthy and lit where it
matters, as an aircraft's dark cockpit; a navy stage whose surfaces step up in luminance; three
lights with one meaning each (the logo's glow blue for Cogpit and the user, cyan for the cluster's
data, violet for the agent only); tokens for what is counted, bracket labels for groups, a glow only
for what matters now, the horizon only where there is no data. It replaces D-22's Solarized palettes
in the window ([theme.go](../../internal/ui/fyneui/theme.go)); the terminal keeps Solarized's sixteen
colours ([ATTRIBUTION.md](../../ATTRIBUTION.md)).

| Question (the review page's) | Options | Built | Who decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dark Cockpit Cogpit's default look | default with Solarized selectable; default without Solarized; an extra palette | **the default, Solarized not offered as a palette**, as the branch was built and approved; the review page's ★ was "selectable", which the owner did not ask for | the owner, by approving the branch as built (open: Solarized can come back as a palette, the shapes take any) |
| Violet for the agent only | yes, Terminating rose; violet stays Terminating's too | yes: Terminating is rose, charts keep violet as the second series | built and approved |
| Status in lists | quiet, only deviations lit; every status a pill; coloured text | quiet: a spine and a pill for what deviates, Running plain with a dot | built and approved |
| The grid floor | only where there is no data; the Overview's head too; nowhere | only where there is no data (welcome, About) | built and approved |
| Where a cluster shows its integrations | the Overview's head and Cluster Settings; under every hotbar tile too; Settings only | the Overview's head and Cluster Settings | built and approved |
| A typeface of its own | Fyne's stays; one through the theme | Fyne's stays | built (unchanged) |
| The way to main | in parts with walks; the whole branch; discard | the whole branch, prepared for the merge on 2026-10-21 | the owner ("Bereite den Merge vor") |
| The first outlook topic | change set with receipt; two lanes; ambient triage; semantic zoom | none built | open, the owner's |
| A cluster's identity colour (a track had mapped "red" to a teal so no tile borrows a status hue) | the calm mapping; the user's own hue | the user's own hue: a red tile is often a user's own warning for production | the lead (2026-10-21 night), open to revision |

Tests: every palette test holds (`TestPaletteContrast`, `TestStatusColoursAreDistinct`,
`TestChartColoursAreDistinct`, `TestIdentityColorsContrast`); the shapes' render
`TestRenderGlowPrimitives`; the tracks' own (`TestBearingStates`, `TestOverviewHealthHeader`,
`TestAlertsPillSegments`, the instruments' in `instrument_test.go`); every `testdata` render and the
README's pictures drawn again before the merge. CI green on PR #65.

**Not verified, and these are the gaps.** Judged from Fyne's software renderer (offscreen renders),
not seen in the GL window on a Mac before the merge; no run of the perf harness (10,000 rows at
60 fps) with the new per-cell objects (reused by Fyne's table, nothing extra on a healthy row); Fyne's
own CustomDialog dialogs (Helm, kubeconfig, the integrations question) keep Fyne's frame; Flux and
Argo CD are not in the integrations' bearing (the engine reports no state for them as integrations).

## D-111: Cogpit for Windows: an NSIS setup and WinSparkle

**The owner's request (2026-10-21):** "Ich möchte, dass du auf einem Branch den Windows-Release für
dieses Tool vorbereitest. Schau dich erstmal um und besprich mit dir das Vorgehen." Asked four
questions, the owner chose the lead's recommendation each time: **an NSIS setup for the user**
(per user without an administrator, `/allusers`, `/S` and `/D=` as Lens's setup has them; options
weighed: an MSI built with WiX, per machine, whose v6 and v7 come under the Open Source Maintenance
Fee's EULA; the setup with a portable zip beside it, which would not update itself); **WinSparkle
with the same update key** (Sparkle's Windows port, MIT; a feed of its own on Pages signed with the
key Sparkle's feed is signed with, in the environment `sparkle`, so after the owner's approval of
each release; options weighed: WinSparkle with a key of its own in an environment of its own;
winget only, without a one-click update); **the first release unsigned** (Authenticode comes once
signing material exists; until then SmartScreen warns at the first start, and updates are checked
by the update key all the same; option weighed: no Windows files on a release until then); and
**the toolchain on the owner's Windows 11 workstation** (Go, MSYS2's MinGW-w64 gcc, NSIS and the
GitHub CLI through winget), to build there and look at the real window. And: "Arbeite nur auf einem
feature-branch, keine commits nach main": the branch `windows-release`, merged through a pull
request the owner approves, since the merge releases. This brings Windows ahead of the macOS beta
and M11 ([D-7](#d-7-language-and-platforms)), as D-108 brought Linux.

**Built 2026-10-21 on the branch `windows-release`.** The setup: `make dist-windows VERSION=x.y.z`
on Windows ([`hack/windows/setup.sh`](../../hack/windows/setup.sh),
[`packaging/windows/cogpit.nsi`](../../packaging/windows/cogpit.nsi)) builds
`dist/windows/Cogpit-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe` with both executables built as the macOS
app's are (the release's tags, [D-67](#d-67-the-demo-cluster-stays-out-of-releases),
[D-103](#d-103-fynes-thread-check-a-build-parameter-off-in-releases)), `cogpit.exe` a GUI program
(no console window), both with their icon, manifest and version information
([`hack/windows/resources.sh`](../../hack/windows/resources.sh),
[`packaging/windows/winres.json`](../../packaging/windows/winres.json), go-winres v0.3.3 pinned),
WinSparkle 0.9.4's `WinSparkle.dll` beside them (pinned by version and SHA-256,
[`hack/windows/winsparkle.sh`](../../hack/windows/winsparkle.sh)), the licence and the third-party
notices, a Start menu entry and the uninstall entry Settings › Apps lists. `make
test-windows-package` ([`hack/windows/setup-test.sh`](../../hack/windows/setup-test.sh)) installs
it silently for the user into a folder of its own, checks the files, both executables' version,
`cogpit-cli version`, the uninstall entry, the Start menu entry and that `cogpit.exe` is a GUI
program, installs it again over itself (as an update does) and uninstalls it. The app's updater:
[`internal/update/winsparkle_windows.go`](../../internal/update/winsparkle_windows.go) and the
feed's reading for the Update button, [`appcast.go`](../../internal/update/appcast.go); the window
closes when WinSparkle asks (`Updater.OnShutdownRequest`, fyneui's `Options.Quit`). The release
pipeline's jobs "Cogpit Setup (Windows x64)", "Attach to the release (Windows)", "Windows appcast
(draft)", "(sign)" and "(deploy to Pages)" ([releasing › Windows](releasing.md#windows)); CI's job
"Windows Package" builds and checks the setup on every push. Every text file is checked out with
LF on Windows too ([`.gitattributes`](../../.gitattributes)): Git for Windows' default CRLF had
failed the golden files, the tests that read `//go:build` lines and the scripts.

Every choice below is the lead's decision (2026-10-21), open to revision.

| Decision | Options weighed | Chosen | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| The setup's tool | NSIS; Inno Setup; WiX (MSI); MSIX | **NSIS 3** | zlib-licensed without conditions (Inno Setup asks commercial users for a licence, WiX v6 and later come under the OSMF EULA); Lens's Windows setup is an NSIS one, whose `/S`, `/allusers` and `/D=` the owner chose; MSYS2 ships it as a signed package beside the gcc CI needs anyway; MSIX would need a trusted signature before it installs at all |
| Where it installs | per user `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Cogpit`; Program Files | **per user by default**, Program Files with `/allusers`; an existing installation is updated where it is and as it was installed; `/D=` chooses | The owner's choice; no administrator for the install or any update, as VS Code's user setup |
| `/allusers` without an administrator | refuse; start again through UAC | **start again through UAC** (`runas`), with the same options and the folder; a declined prompt ends with `ERROR_CANCELLED` (1223); the uninstaller of such an installation the same | As Lens's setup elevates for `/allusers` |
| The machine's uninstall entry | the 32-bit setup's view (`WOW6432Node`); the 64-bit view | **the 64-bit view** (`SetRegView 64`) | The 64-bit app reads it there to know it was installed by the setup |
| Shortcuts | Start menu; Start menu and desktop | **the Start menu only** (`Cogpit.lnk`) | Windows 11 pins from the Start menu; a desktop icon nobody asked for is clutter, and the finish page offers to start Cogpit |
| `cogpit-cli.exe` on PATH | add the folder to the user's PATH; not | **not** | The MCP details give `cogpit-cli.exe`'s full path, as on macOS, where it is inside the bundle; a setup that edits PATH must undo it exactly on uninstall |
| A running Cogpit during an install or update | fail; replace on reboot; wait | **wait** for `cogpit.exe` to be free (silently up to a minute, else a Retry/Cancel prompt); a running `cogpit-cli.exe` (an agent's MCP bridge, for hours) is moved aside and removed by a later setup or uninstall | WinSparkle starts the setup and then asks Cogpit to quit; an agent's bridge must not block an update |
| Uninstalling | remove the user's files too; keep them | **keep** `%APPDATA%\Cogpit` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Cogpit`; remove WinSparkle's state in `HKCU\Software\guided-traffic\Cogpit\WinSparkle` | As `apt remove` keeps them on Linux; WinSparkle's state is the updater's, not the user's |
| Architectures | x64; x64 and arm64 | **x64** first | Fyne's OpenGL on Windows on ARM is untried, and Windows 11 on ARM runs x64 programs emulated; WinSparkle's arm64 DLL is fetched already for later |
| The oldest Windows | Windows 10; 10 1809 (build 17763); 10 22H2 as Lens | **Windows 10 1809**, checked by the setup and named in the feed's `sparkle:minimumSystemVersion` | ConPTY, the local terminal's console, came with 1809; Go 1.27 needs Windows 10 |
| Icon and version information | `fyne package`; go-winres; rsrc | **go-winres v0.3.3**, the resources made for each release build into `cmd/*/rsrc_windows_<arch>.syso` and removed after it (git ignores them); the icon group named `GLFW_ICON` | `fyne package` builds the binary itself, past the Makefile's tags and flags; GLFW loads the window's icon by the name `GLFW_ICON` (under another name the title bar showed Windows' generic icon, seen 2026-10-21); the icon drawn by `hack/icon -ico` at each size with a narrower margin than macOS's |
| The updater | WinSparkle; an updater of Cogpit's own; winget | **WinSparkle 0.9.4**, loaded at run time from the app's folder by its full path (no cgo, never the DLL search order); only for a release build that runs from the folder an uninstall entry names | The owner's choice; the same EdDSA signatures and tools as Sparkle; a copy outside the setup's folder would install a new copy elsewhere |
| The feed | one appcast with `sparkle:os` items; a feed of its own | **`appcast-windows.xml`** beside `appcast.xml` on Pages, its items `sparkle:os="windows-x64"` and `sparkle:installerArguments="/S /relaunch"`, the release notes a link to the release's page | The macOS item waits for Apple's notarization and the owner's approval, Windows must not wait for it; WinSparkle shows HTML, not Sparkle 2's Markdown |
| Where the Windows feed is signed | a job on Windows with WinSparkle's tool; the macOS feed's job | **a job of its own in the environment `sparkle`, on macOS, with Sparkle's own `sign_update`** (hack/macos/appcast.sh's `sign`, taking the setup and the feed's name) | The same key, the same reviewed tool and the same rules (a reviewer, tags `v*`); the owner approves two deployments of `sparkle` per release, the macOS feed's and this one |
| The Update button | WinSparkle's own scheduled checks (its window, unasked); Cogpit reads the feed | **Cogpit reads the signed feed** at every start and every hour while Check for updates automatically is on, verifies it with the key, and leaves out a release skipped in WinSparkle's window (its `SkipThisVersion`); WinSparkle's own checks off | WinSparkle shows its window as soon as a check of its own finds a release and tells its host nothing: Cogpit's button (F7) and its version need the feed. Go's HTTP client follows `HTTPS_PROXY`, not Windows' proxy settings: behind a proxy only Windows knows, the button stays away and Help › Check for Updates… (WinINet) still finds the release |
| The button's click | WinSparkle's window (Install update, the download, Install update again); install at once | **install at once**: the new command `app.installUpdate` (GUI only), on Windows WinSparkle's `check_update_with_ui_and_install`, whose window shows the check and the download and then runs the setup; Help › Check for Updates… keeps WinSparkle's window with the notes, Skip and Remind me later; on macOS and Linux `app.installUpdate` does what `app.checkForUpdates` does | **The owner's choice** (2026-10-21), after the end-to-end test: WinSparkle's second Install update, after a download of under a second, looked as if nothing happened ("ich hatte geklickt weil nichts passierte"); the click on "Update to v…" is the decision. GUI only: on Windows it installs and restarts Cogpit without asking again |
| After the install | WinSparkle relaunches; the setup relaunches | **the setup** (`/relaunch`), as the desktop's user (through Explorer when elevated) | WinSparkle starts the setup and asks the app to quit, then ends; only the setup knows when the files are in place |
| Pages | one deploy job for all; each keeps the others | **each of the three deploys keeps the other two parts as Pages serves them** (the feeds byte for byte, the APT repository checked against its key), in the concurrency group `pages` | As D-108's two |
| The setup's job on the release | in turn with the others; after Linux's | **after the Linux attach job, whatever it came to** (`needs` with `always()`), in the group `release-files-<tag>` | GitHub keeps one running and one waiting job in a group and cancels a second waiting one; Linux and Windows finish at about the same time |
| The runners | the organisation's self-hosted; GitHub's hosted `windows-latest` | **`windows-latest` with MSYS2's MINGW64 shell** (`msys2/setup-msys2`, MinGW-w64 gcc, make, unzip and NSIS from MSYS2's signed packages) | The self-hosted runners are Linux; GitHub's Windows image carries no NSIS |
| The local terminal | the terminal widget's own ConPTY (ActiveState's `termtest/conpty`); `golang.org/x/sys/windows` | **x/sys/windows** ([`localpty_windows.go`](../../internal/terminal/localpty_windows.go)): the shell starts suspended, joins a job object of its own (kill on close, breakaway allowed) and runs; closing the terminal ends every program started from it, GUI programs too, as closing a console window does | ActiveState's package ends the process when a pipe fails and starts the shell before it could be put in a job; x/sys has every call (it moved from an indirect to a direct dependency, nothing new) |
| The terminal's shell | cmd; Windows PowerShell; PowerShell 7 | **the preference's shell, else `pwsh.exe` on PATH, else Windows PowerShell, else `%ComSpec%`**; `$SHELL` ignored there (Git Bash sets a POSIX path) | Lens opens PowerShell; PowerShell 7 where the user installed it |
| kubectl first in the terminal | a symlink (needs a privilege); a hard link; a copy; its folder first on PATH | **its folder first on PATH** when the file is named `kubectl.exe` (Cogpit's downloads hold nothing else), else a hard link named `kubectl.exe` in the session's folder, else a copy; `KUBECONFIG` joined with `;`; Enforce kubectl does nothing on Windows yet | A symlink needs Developer Mode or an administrator; a hard link is refused for a file the user cannot write (System32) and breaks Scoop's shims; a copy costs 60 MB a terminal |
| A file another process holds open | fail (Windows refuses a rename or a removal then); retry | **retry for up to a second** (renames of Cogpit's files, the journals' writes, a draft's removal), as Go's own `cmd/go` does; the journals' owner file created sharing its deletion | Another Cogpit, an editor or a virus scanner holds a file for moments; the write was lost with a warning (found by the first test run on Windows) |
| The program a login's approval binds | the path the kubeconfig names; the file that runs | **the file that runs**: on Windows `os/exec` runs `plug` as `plug.exe` (PATHEXT), so the approval hashes that file | A decoy `plug` beside a `plug.exe` swapped at will would otherwise keep the approval ([trust boundaries](../security/trust-boundaries.md)) |
| The MCP registration commands | POSIX everywhere; PowerShell on Windows | **PowerShell on Windows** (single quotes, `*> $null`), POSIX elsewhere; the setup's `cogpit-cli.exe` beside a release's `cogpit.exe` offered for the stdio registration | Windows Terminal opens PowerShell; `>/dev/null` fails there |

**Verified (2026-10-21, the owner's Windows 11 Pro workstation, 26200).** `make dist-windows
VERSION=0.0.1` built the setup (43.7 MB) with NSIS 3.13 from winget and from MSYS2; `make
test-windows-package` installed it, installed it again over itself and uninstalled it, leaving no
entry and no shortcut. The release build's window: no console window, Windows' own title bar with
its three buttons and Cogpit's icon (after the `GLFW_ICON` fix), the menus in Cogpit's top bar
(D-109), per-monitor DPI; Explorer's Properties show Cogpit's version and publisher. The updater's
tests ([`winsparkle_windows_test.go`](../../internal/update/winsparkle_windows_test.go): every way
it is unavailable, the real WinSparkle.dll's functions, the button from the signed feed, a skipped
release) and the feed's on every system ([`appcast_test.go`](../../internal/update/appcast_test.go)).
**Every test of the repository ran on Windows for the first time** (2026-10-21): 91 failed at
first, most from CRLF checkouts, Unix paths and modes in fixtures, and some real faults (the
renames above, a log's resume under Windows' coarse clock, the plugin binding, Winsock's error
numbers, file URLs and paths in the window); after the fixes all 36 packages pass, in 222 seconds
on the owner's workstation. **End to end** (2026-10-21, a throwaway update key, the feed and the
setups served from `127.0.0.1`, the profile's folders replaced by test ones): the installed 0.0.1
read the signed feed at its start and showed "Update to v0.0.2"; WinSparkle's window showed the
release with its notes; after Install update it downloaded the setup (43.9 MB), checked its
signature, ran it as `/S /relaunch` and asked Cogpit to quit: 0.0.1 had quit 0.6 s after the
setup started, and 0.0.2 ran 4 s later, its window without the button; the uninstaller left
nothing. With the button installing at once (`app.installUpdate`, a click on "Update to v0.0.2"):
WinSparkle's window showed the download at 0.7 s, the setup ran at 1.3 s, 0.0.1 had quit at 1.8 s
and 0.0.2 ran at 4.6 s, without a question. **Not verified yet**, and these are the gaps: a release run of the pipeline (the first is
the one the merge makes); an install for all users through UAC; the setup on Windows 10 and on ARM;
a real terminal tab on ConPTY in the window (the session's tests pass); Authenticode
([H-139](../security/updates.md#h-139-the-windows-setup-is-not-signed-with-authenticode)). Seen
and left for later: Fyne's own dialogs (the file choosers, which on Windows are Fyne's) follow the
system's language ("Speichern") while Cogpit's text is English; the folder chooser offers no list
of drives.
